q: Which strategy involves making small optimizations, such as moving a database to a managed service, while keeping the application's core architecture?
explain: Replatform's 'tinker' step swaps in managed services for efficiency without redesigning the application. Rehost makes no changes; retire and retain leave the workload unmigrated.

q: An order system collapses during flash sales because web servers call the processing service directly. Which service decouples the two tiers and buffers the traffic bursts?
explain: SQS is a message queue: producers send, consumers pull at their own pace, so bursts get buffered instead of overwhelming workers. SNS pushes to many subscribers (fan-out). EventBridge is an event bus; Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows.

q: A microservices platform routes requests for /api/orders to one target group and /api/payments to another behind a single public endpoint. Which load balancer feature makes this path-based split possible?
explain: ALB listener rules inspect the HTTP path (and host header) to forward each request to the matching target group, the classic microservices front door. NLB works at Layer 4 without path awareness, GWLB inserts security appliances, and security groups filter rather than route content.

q: Engineers keep confusing SQS and SNS in a design review. Which one-line contrast should the lead architect put on the whiteboard?
options: Both are identical services with different names for billing
SQS stores files; SNS stores database tables
SQS is a pull-based queue where consumers poll for messages; SNS is a push-based pub/sub service that delivers to subscribers
SQS pushes messages instantly; SNS requires consumers to poll topics
explain: The defining difference is delivery style: SQS holds messages until workers pull them at their own pace, while SNS pushes published messages out to all subscribers immediately. Neither stores files or tables, and the polling/pushing roles are the reverse of the second option's claim.

q: Which TWO tasks are AWS responsibilities for an Amazon RDS deployment? (Select TWO.)
options: Setting the customer database user passwords
Classifying the customer data in the database
explain: For RDS, AWS patches the engine and maintains host hardware. Database user passwords and data classification are customer responsibilities in every model.

q: Which advantage lets a company serve a newly won overseas contract next week without constructing or leasing facilities in that country?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Go global in minutes means selecting Regions near new customers and deploying immediately on infrastructure AWS already operates worldwide. The contract is won and served in a week because no facility build-out is needed.

q: Which service is primarily a threat detection service rather than a vulnerability scanner?
explain: GuardDuty detects active threats and anomalous behavior from logs and intelligence feeds. Inspector is the vulnerability scanner; Macie classifies data; ACM issues certificates.

q: A compliance-driven firm needs its instances physically isolated on single-tenant hardware, but it does not need to see or control exactly which physical server each instance lands on, and it has no special per-socket licensing. Which tenancy option matches?
explain: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to one customer, providing isolation without the placement visibility and licensing control of Dedicated Hosts, which the firm explicitly does not need. Default tenancy shares hardware with other customers, and Spot describes pricing, not isolation guarantees.

q: An engineering manager asks what makes a subnet public in one sentence for a design document. Which sentence is exam-accurate?
options: A subnet is public when it is tagged with the word public
A subnet is public when it contains more than ten instances
A subnet is public when its instances use the largest instance types
A subnet is public when its route table sends internet-bound traffic to an internet gateway
explain: Public versus private is purely a routing designation: a route to an internet gateway makes a subnet public, regardless of instance count, size, or naming tags. Teams often mislabel by contents, but the exam keys strictly on the route table.

q: Which relational database service is MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible and supports up to 15 read replicas?
explain: Aurora is AWS's cloud-native relational engine, wire-compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, with storage that auto-scales and up to 15 low-latency read replicas. DynamoDB is NoSQL; Redshift is a data warehouse.

q: A food delivery firm runs its ordering database on EC2 instead of RDS. Who patches the database software in this self-managed setup?
explain: Self-managed databases on EC2 put database patching on the customer, unlike RDS where AWS patches the engine. The pricing or instance family does not change this split.

q: An operations team writes a nightly script that lists EC2 instances, stops development servers, and emails a report, all from a Linux shell with no browser involved. Which access tool is the script using?
explain: The CLI is the unified command-line tool for controlling AWS services from a terminal, which is exactly how shell scripts automate instance chores. The console is graphical and manual, QuickSight builds dashboards, and Artifact distributes compliance documents.

q: Which migration strategy transfers an entire hypervisor platform's workloads to its cloud counterpart with minimal disruption?
explain: Relocate is defined by hypervisor-level transfer, such as VMware estates moving to VMware Cloud on AWS. Retire and retain do not move workloads at all.

q: A database team wants its RDS instance reachable only from the application tier's servers and from no other source, enforced where the database's network interface lives. Which control is attached at that resource level?
options: A security group on the database permitting only the application tier's security group
A network ACL with a deny for the whole internet
explain: Security groups attach to the resource's ENI and can reference the application tier's security group as the only allowed source, a precise resource-level rule. NACLs act per subnet rather than per resource, DNS zones resolve names, and origin access identities protect S3 content behind CloudFront.

Cost Explorer's usage forecasts project likely spend from historical patterns (typically up to 3 months ahead, with a confidence interval). It informs budgeting but does not enforce limits or guarantee accuracy.
options: It enforces a maximum spending cap
It grants discounts for early commitment
It projects future costs from historical usage patterns
q: What does AWS Cost Explorer's forecasting feature do?

A checkout application must keep each shopper connected to the same target during a session because cart state lives in that server's memory. Which ALB capability preserves the shopper-to-target binding?
explain: ALB target groups support stickiness using cookies, pinning a user's requests to one target for the session's duration. Health checks remove bad targets, cross-zone settings spread load across AZs, and host-header rules choose target groups, none of which binds a user to a specific target.

q: A news publisher registers its domain through Amazon Route 53 and also hosts the DNS records there. Which pair of Route 53 capabilities is the publisher using?
options: Load balancing and target health management
DDoS mitigation and web application firewalling
Domain registration and authoritative DNS hosting with hosted zones
explain: Route 53 is both a registrar and a highly available DNS service whose hosted zones hold the records that answer queries worldwide. Caching content is CloudFront's role, firewalling and DDoS belong to WAF and Shield, and load balancing belongs to ELB, though Route 53 can steer traffic toward balancers.

q: A DBA lists the database engines available on Amazon RDS for a migration plan. Which set is accurate for RDS?
options: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, and SQL Server, plus Amazon Aurora
explain: RDS offers MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, and Microsoft SQL Server, with Aurora as the AWS-built MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible option. MongoDB maps to DocumentDB, Cassandra to Keyspaces, and Hadoop/Spark to EMR rather than RDS.

q: Which S3 feature automatically transitions objects to cheaper storage classes or deletes them on a schedule?
explain: Lifecycle policies automate transitions (e.g., Standard → Glacier after 90 days) and expirations. Versioning keeps old versions; replication copies across buckets/Regions; S3 Select retrieves subsets of object data.

q: An architect moves a bursty image-processing job to a serverless design so it can scale to thousands of parallel executions for a few minutes, then vanish. Which pillar most supports choosing that architecture for throughput?
explain: Using a massively parallel serverless approach to maximize processing throughput is a Performance Efficiency choice. Cost may also improve, but the stem's goal is processing capacity per unit time.

q: Under the shared responsibility model, which task is the CUSTOMER's responsibility when running an application on EC2?
options: Physical security of AWS data centers
explain: The customer handles security in the cloud: guest OS patching, data, IAM, firewall rules. AWS handles security of the cloud: facilities, hardware, hypervisor, and network infrastructure.

q: A developer builds a REST backend where each HTTP request runs a short piece of business logic, and the team wants zero servers to administer. Which pairing is the standard serverless pattern for this design?
options: AWS Direct Connect in front of Amazon RDS
Amazon API Gateway in front of AWS Lambda functions
Amazon Route 53 in front of Amazon S3
An Application Load Balancer in front of EC2 instances
explain: API Gateway receives and manages the HTTP requests while Lambda executes the logic per request, scaling automatically with no servers to run. The load balancer option still needs managed EC2 instances, and the other pairings do not execute request logic at all.

q: A team stores SSH private keys and OAuth tokens in a shared wiki page. Which change most improves secret handling?
options: Move the secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with IAM-controlled retrieval
Rename the wiki page to something obscure
Copy the secrets into more places for backup
Encrypt the wiki page with a shared password
explain: Secrets Manager provides encrypted storage, fine-grained IAM access, audit logging, and rotation for credentials and tokens, replacing informal secret sharing.

q: A company rebuilds its monolithic application as cloud-native microservices running on Lambda and DynamoDB to take full advantage of cloud capabilities. Which migration strategy is this?
explain: Refactor (re-architect) = rebuilding an application cloud-native, e.g., monolith to serverless microservices — the most effort but the most cloud benefit. Rehost moves as-is; Replatform makes only minor tweaks; Retain keeps the app on-premises for now.

q: Which statement about SCPs is FALSE and should be corrected in a team design doc?
options: SCPs never grant permissions by themselves
SCPs affect the management account in the same way as member accounts
SCPs act as guardrails on maximum permissions
SCPs can be attached to organizational units
explain: SCPs do not affect the management account, which is a common exam trap. They guardrail member accounts and OUs and only limit, never grant, permissions.

q: Who is accountable for firewall configuration when a customer places resources inside its own VPC subnets?
explain: VPC design, subnet layout, route tables, security groups, and network ACLs are customer architecture and configuration responsibilities.

q: Before launch, a team classifies its data by sensitivity and applies stronger protections to regulated records than to public marketing assets. Which pillar guides this classification work?
explain: Data classification and applying proportionate protection are Security pillar activities under data protection. The classification exists to decide how data must be safeguarded.

q: An organization with many accounts wants one administrator account to push consistent WAF rules to every account. Which service centralizes firewall administration?
explain: Firewall Manager centrally configures and audits WAF rules, Shield Advanced protections, and security groups across accounts in an AWS organization.

q: Which TWO are valid reasons a team chooses EC2 over Lambda for a workload? (Select TWO.)
options: The workload consists of tiny tasks lasting a few seconds each
The workload runs continuously for several hours without stopping
The workload needs a custom operating system kernel configuration
The workload must respond to S3 upload events in milliseconds
explain: EC2 fits long-running work beyond Lambda's 15-minute ceiling and gives full control of the guest operating system and kernel settings. Short event-driven tasks triggered by S3 events are precisely the pattern Lambda was built to handle serverlessly.

q: Which TWO facts about AWS edge locations belong in an architecture design document? (Select TWO.)
options: There are more edge locations than there are Regions
Every edge location contains the full set of AWS services including RDS and Redshift
Edge locations serve content for CloudFront and help answer Route 53 queries close to users
An edge location is another name for an Availability Zone
explain: Edge locations form a wide, lightweight footprint that outnumbers Regions, hosting CloudFront caches and Route 53 resolvers near users. They do not run the full service catalog, and they are distinct from AZs, which are the data-center building blocks of Regions.

q: An architect quotes the durability figure AWS designs S3 objects for across storage classes. Which figure is correct?
options: 100 percent durability with no possibility of loss
explain: S3 is designed for 99.999999999 percent durability, meaning an object loss is expected roughly once in ten thousand years per ten thousand objects, achieved by storing data redundantly across multiple devices and AZs. The 99.99 percent figure describes S3 Standard availability, a different metric.

q: An application running on an EC2 instance needs to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the best practice?
options: Embed IAM access keys in the application code
Use the root user's access keys
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
explain: An IAM role gives the instance temporary, automatically rotated credentials — no long-lived keys to leak or rotate. Embedded keys end up in code repos; public buckets expose data to the internet.

q: After moving its order database into managed RDS housing, a retailer gets a notice about a pending engine maintenance window. Which party actually applies that engine update?
options: AWS as the managed service operator
explain: RDS is a managed service, so AWS patches the host and database engine software. The retailer still controls access, security groups, parameters, and its own data.

q: A company with multiple AWS accounts wants a single bill and volume discounts pooled across all accounts. Which feature provides this?
explain: Consolidated billing (via Organizations) merges accounts under one payer: one bill, and usage aggregates for volume-discount tiers. Tags categorize spend; Budgets alert; Marketplace sells third-party software.

Under Consolidated Billing, unused Reserved Instance hours in one account can apply to matching usage in other accounts in the organization (when sharing is enabled), maximizing the benefit of the commitment.
options: Each account's Reserved Instances are locked to it forever
Consolidated Billing converts RIs to Spot Instances
Unused Reserved Instance hours can benefit other accounts in the organization
Unused hours roll over as credits to the next month
q: How does Consolidated Billing affect Reserved Instance discounts across member accounts?
A game company used to spend $200,000 before knowing whether a title would succeed. On AWS it spends a few hundred dollars to test demand first. Which economic shift made this possible?
options: Moving from large upfront commitment to small incremental consumption spending
Eliminating the need for any spending
explain: Cloud economics lets the company validate demand with small, incremental spend instead of a huge pre-commitment. Spending still occurs and success is not guaranteed; the risk profile of the spend changed.

q: Which TWO activities belong to the Reliability pillar of the Well-Architected Framework? (Select TWO.)
options: Testing recovery procedures so failures can be restored within objectives
Automatically recovering workloads from infrastructure failure
Negotiating volume discounts with software vendors
Deleting data that retention rules no longer require
explain: Testing recovery and automatic recovery from failure are Reliability design areas. Deleting expired data serves sustainability and governance, and vendor negotiation is procurement, not workload reliability.

q: An online store processing card payments on AWS must comply with which program?
explain: Payment card processing falls under PCI DSS, the card industry standard for protecting cardholder data. GDPR covers EU personal data and FedRAMP covers US government systems.

q: Which service provides resizable virtual servers in the AWS Cloud?
explain: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) = virtual servers you fully control: instance type, OS, storage, networking. Lambda runs code without servers; S3 stores objects; RDS is a managed database.

The AWS Billing Dashboard (Billing and Cost Management console home) gives a high-level view: month-to-date spend, forecasted spend, and a breakdown of top services, with links into Cost Explorer and other cost tools.
q: On the first screen of the Billing and Cost Management console, which element provides a high-level overview of month-to-date spend and forecasts?
A company makes its application available to customers on three continents in a single afternoon by deploying to additional AWS Regions. Which advantage of cloud computing does this demonstrate?
options: Stop spending money on running data centers
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Go global in minutes = deploying worldwide in a few clicks instead of building data centers per market. Economies of scale is about lower prices from AWS's size; speed and agility is about experimenting fast; the data-center point is about undifferentiated heavy lifting.

q: A web platform needs HTTPS termination, request inspection by AWS WAF, and routing that understands cookies and headers, all at its public entry point. Which ELB choice provides this Layer 7 feature set?
options: Gateway Load Balancer, which terminates website TLS by default
Classic Load Balancer, which is the only WAF-compatible option
Network Load Balancer, which inspects HTTP headers natively
Application Load Balancer, which integrates with AWS WAF and routes on HTTP content
explain: The ALB terminates TLS, integrates with WAF for request filtering, and routes using headers, paths, and cookies because it operates at Layer 7. NLB works below HTTP semantics, GWLB steers traffic to appliances, and the Classic balancer long ago lost its position as the feature-richest web tier option.

q: A manufacturer retires its on-site server room, ending contracts for diesel generators, precision cooling, and overnight facility guards, while its engineers refocus on production software. Which advantage is this?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explain: Ending the undifferentiated work and cost of operating physical facilities is stop spending money running and maintaining data centers. AWS operates the facilities; the manufacturer redirects effort to its own products.

q: A law firm must prove that archived case files cannot be altered or deleted for five years by anyone, including the account root user. Which S3 Object Lock retention mode enforces this strongest guarantee?
options: Retention through a bucket policy only
explain: In compliance mode, a protected object cannot be overwritten or deleted by any user, including the root user, until the retention period expires. Governance mode allows privileged users to change retention, and a bucket policy alone does not provide WORM enforcement.

q: A defense contractor is barred by contract from using any public cloud and builds an automated, self-service internal platform in its own facility. Which deployment model is it using?
explain: Contractual prohibition on public cloud plus an internally run virtualized platform equals an on-premises private cloud. Nothing runs on AWS in this scenario.

q: A gaming studio uses Amazon RDS. Which configuration remains the studio responsibility?
options: Setting database parameters and controlling who can connect
Patching the RDS host operating system
explain: With RDS, AWS handles host patching, hardware, and engine patching. The customer still sets parameters, manages credentials and access, and configures security groups.

q: If an entire Availability Zone becomes unavailable, what happens to a properly designed multi-AZ application?
options: All data in the Region is lost
It continues operating from the remaining Availability Zones in the Region
It must wait for the zone to be repaired before serving anyone
It automatically moves to an edge location permanently
explain: Multi-AZ design exists precisely so one AZ's loss is survivable using the others. Data is replicated across AZs in such designs, so a single zone failure is not data loss.

q: An application is designed so that when a component fails, traffic automatically shifts to healthy components with no manual intervention. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar does this demonstrate?
explain: Reliability = the ability of a workload to perform its function correctly and consistently — including automatically recovering from failure. Security protects data and systems; Operational Excellence is about running and improving operations; Cost Optimization is about avoiding unnecessary spend.

q: An app team wants social sign-in with Google and Facebook for its users alongside email registration. Which service supports these identity providers for app users?
options: Amazon Cognito user pools with federated providers
explain: Cognito user pools can federate with social and enterprise identity providers while also supporting native sign-up, giving the app one user directory.

q: Which outcome is the main promise of the 'stop guessing capacity' economic idea?
options: Forecasting teams are reassigned to sales
Spending aligns with real demand instead of with a forecast made months earlier
explain: When capacity follows observed demand, money is spent on resources actually needed rather than on a possibly wrong prediction. Demand stays unpredictable; the spending simply tracks it.

Business Support includes 24/7 phone and chat access with a response time of less than 1 hour for a production system down. The sub-15-minute response for business-critical outages is an Enterprise plan feature.
q: A company on the AWS Business Support plan has a production system completely down at 2 a.m. What is the guaranteed response time for the initial response from AWS Support?
Developers push application code to a service that provisions servers, patching, and scaling for them, so they never administer an operating system. Which model is this?
explain: PaaS, exemplified by Elastic Beanstalk, manages the underlying platform so developers focus on code. With IaaS they would still patch and administer the operating system themselves.

q: External partners refuse to change their tooling: their systems upload delivery files nightly over SFTP, and the files must land directly in an S3 bucket. Which AWS service accepts SFTP, FTP, and FTPS transfers straight into S3?
explain: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, and FTP endpoints whose files land directly in S3 (or EFS), so partners keep their existing clients. DataSync is for controlled sync between storage systems, API Gateway fronts APIs, and CloudFront delivers content outbound.

q: Which deployment model keeps all infrastructure in the company's own facilities with no cloud usage?
explain: On-premises (private cloud) = everything in your own data center. Public cloud = shared AWS infrastructure; hybrid = both connected together.

q: What information does IAM last-accessed data provide?
options: When a user or role last used a service or action, to trim unused permissions
The password age of the root user
The cost of each service last month
The IP address of every S3 object
explain: Last-accessed information shows service and action usage history, helping administrators safely remove permissions that identities no longer use.

q: A payment app must prove to auditors which identities used its encryption keys and when. Which KMS property supports this?
options: Keys are stored in S3 buckets
Every KMS API call is logged in CloudTrail
explain: KMS integrates with CloudTrail so every key use, including decrypt calls, is recorded with the caller identity and time, supporting audit requirements.

q: A company's application must stay available even if an entire AWS Region suffers an extended outage. What should the architect do?
options: Add more EC2 instances in a single Availability Zone
Deploy the application to a second Region
Deploy across multiple Availability Zones in the same Region
Serve traffic through edge locations only
explain: Only a second Region survives a regional outage — AZs protect against a data-center failure, not a Region-wide one. Edge locations cache content; they don't run your application. Multi-AZ is high availability, not disaster recovery against regional events. Domain 2 — Security and Compliance

q: A trading application needs a load balancer handling millions of TCP requests per second with ultra-low latency and a static IP address. Which load balancer type is the best fit?
explain: NLB operates at Layer 4 with ultra-low latency, millions of requests per second, and static/Elastic IP support. ALB is Layer 7 for HTTP/HTTPS routing. GWLB deploys third-party virtual appliances like firewalls.

q: A startup runs containers on Amazon ECS and is tired of patching and scaling the EC2 instances underneath them. Which launch option removes server management while keeping ECS?
options: Moving tasks into an Auto Scaling group of larger instances
Placing tasks in a placement group
Converting tasks to Lambda functions with a 15-minute limit
explain: Fargate is the serverless compute engine for ECS and EKS: you define task CPU and memory and AWS runs the containers with no EC2 instances to manage. Larger Auto Scaling instances still need management, and Lambda imposes function limits containers may not fit.

Cost Explorer's Reserved Instance and Savings Plans recommendations analyze your actual usage patterns and estimate the savings from commitments, including for consolidated organizations. The Pricing Calculator only models hypothetical estimates.
q: Which tool recommends specific Reserved Instance and Savings Plans purchases based on your actual usage patterns?

explain: Convertible Reserved Instances let you change instance family, size, OS, and tenancy during the term in exchange for a smaller discount than Standard RIs (which only allow attributes such as size within the same family and AZ changes).
q: A company expects its instance family requirements to change during the term and needs the flexibility to exchange its reservation for a different instance family. Which option provides that?
As a company moves from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS, what generally happens to its operational responsibilities?
options: They shift entirely to the customer's security team
They stay identical across all three models
They decrease, because the provider manages more layers of the stack
They increase, because each model adds customer duties
explain: Each step from IaaS to PaaS to SaaS transfers more layers - OS, runtime, then the application itself - to the provider. That progressive handover is the core comparison the exam expects.

q: A company wants to be notified about unusual spikes in AWS spending without manually setting budget thresholds. Which service uses machine learning to detect these anomalies?
explain: Cost Anomaly Detection uses ML to spot unusual spend patterns and alert you — no thresholds to configure. Budgets alerts on thresholds you set yourself; Cost Explorer visualizes past spend; the Pricing Calculator estimates future costs before you build. AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02).

q: A secrets audit finds database passwords stored in plain text inside application config files. Which service should store and rotate those passwords instead?
explain: Secrets Manager centrally stores credentials and API keys and can rotate supported database credentials automatically, removing plain-text secrets from code and configs.

q: Data is accessed infrequently but must be retrievable within milliseconds when needed. Which S3 storage class fits?
options: S3 One Zone-IA for critical data
explain: S3 Standard-IA (Infrequent Access) = millisecond retrieval with lower storage cost, ideal for rarely-but-quickly-needed data like backups. Glacier classes take minutes to hours; One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ, so it suits recreatable data, not critical data.

q: Which TWO are valid reasons to choose AWS Secrets Manager over storing a secret in a plain configuration file? (Select TWO.)
options: Central audit trail of secret retrieval
explain: Secrets Manager adds scheduled rotation and CloudTrail-audited retrieval with IAM control. Certificate issuance is ACM and DDoS cost protection is Shield Advanced.

q: Executives want interactive dashboards and charts over sales data that refresh daily, built by business users without writing code or managing reporting servers. Which AWS service delivers this business-intelligence experience?
explain: QuickSight is the BI service for building and sharing dashboards and visualizations with a per-user pricing model and no servers to run. EMR and Glue process data upstream, and Kinesis ingests streams; none of them is the presentation layer executives asked for.

q: Which sign-in identity should be used for everyday administration of an AWS account?
options: An IAM user or role with administrative permissions and MFA
A shared team account without MFA
explain: Daily administration should use an IAM identity with MFA and only the permissions needed. Root is reserved for the few tasks that specifically require it.

q: Why might a company choose a hybrid deployment instead of moving everything to AWS at once?
options: Hybrid removes the need for any network connectivity
Hybrid guarantees lower cost than every other model
Some workloads must stay on-premises for compliance, latency, or existing investment while others gain cloud benefits
AWS requires a phased approach for all customers
explain: Hybrid fits when part of the estate is bound to premises by regulation, latency, or sunk investment. It actually depends on connectivity between the environments, the opposite of the first distractor.

q: An auditor asks which IAM users have not rotated access keys in over a year. Where is this information found?
explain: The credential report shows access key creation and rotation timestamps for every user, making stale keys easy to spot during security reviews.

q: Who maintains the firmware on the physical hosts that underpin Amazon EC2?
explain: Firmware and physical host maintenance sit below the virtualization layer and are entirely AWS responsibilities under security of the cloud.

q: A firm wants human workforce sign-in managed centrally with its existing identity provider across many AWS accounts. Which capability supports this federation model?
options: IAM Identity Center with external identity provider federation
IAM users with passwords in each account
Sharing one IAM user across the firm
explain: IAM Identity Center federates with external identity providers and maps workforce users to permission sets across accounts, avoiding duplicated per-account users.

q: A review asks whether a workload's design can keep meeting its service objectives as usage grows tenfold, by adding resources rather than redesigning. Which pillar's scalability questions are being asked?
explain: Planning for growth and change so the workload continues to function is Reliability territory in the Well-Architected Framework, which covers scaling to meet demand without failure. Performance asks how efficiently resources are used, a different question.

q: An application in one AWS account must read a bucket owned by a second account. What IAM construct enables this cleanly?
options: The root credentials of the second account
A cross-account role in the bucket-owning account that the first account can assume
A public bucket policy with no restrictions
explain: Cross-account roles let principals in one account assume a role in another with scoped permissions and temporary credentials, the standard pattern for account-to-account access.

q: A company is assembling a data lake on S3 and needs to set up fine-grained access controls for data scientists plus a catalog of lake tables from one governance service. Which service simplifies building and securing data lakes this way?
explain: Lake Formation layers data-lake setup, cataloging, and fine-grained permissions (down to column level) over S3-based lakes. CloudFront distributes content, WAF filters web requests, and Route 53 resolves names; none governs lake data access.

q: Which TWO S3 features help a company recover data or prevent its loss after mistakes or deletions? (Select TWO.)
explain: Versioning lets you restore earlier versions after overwrites or deletes, and Object Lock can stop objects from being deleted for a retention period. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads and website hosting serves content; neither protects data from loss.

q: A help desk resets IAM user passwords. Which setting forces the user to choose a new password at next sign-in?
options: Requiring password reset on next sign-in when setting the password
explain: When an admin sets a user password, IAM can require the user to create a new one at next sign-in, so the admin-set value is only temporary.

q: An insurer stores policy files in S3. Who is accountable if a bucket is left public because of a permissive policy the insurer wrote?
explain: A permissive bucket policy is a customer configuration error. AWS provides tools like Block Public Access and Access Analyzer, but the account owner owns the policy.

q: Every time a new order lands in a DynamoDB table, a small process must email a receipt and update a search index, reacting to inserts and edits as they happen. Which DynamoDB feature emits the change events that trigger this processing?
options: S3 event notifications on the table
explain: DynamoDB Streams captures a time-ordered log of item-level changes that consumers such as Lambda can react to for receipts, indexing, and replication. TTL only expires items, S3 events concern buckets, and RDS subscriptions report database instance events, not table changes.

q: For a self-managed database on EC2, who patches both the guest OS and the database software?
options: AWS for the OS and customer for the database
explain: Self-managed on EC2 means the customer owns the full stack above the hypervisor, including guest OS patching and database software patching, unlike RDS.

q: Which service investigates a GuardDuty finding by showing which resources a compromised role interacted with over the past weeks?
explain: Detective pre-collects and graphs log data so analysts can pivot from a GuardDuty finding to the full activity history of a role, instance, or IP address.

q: A data science team wants one managed platform covering the whole machine-learning lifecycle: preparing data, training models, tuning them, and deploying endpoints for predictions. Which service is AWS's end-to-end ML platform?
explain: SageMaker is the full ML workbench for building, training, tuning, and deploying custom models at scale. Rekognition, Comprehend, and Polly are pre-built AI services for vision, language understanding, and speech respectively, not platforms for training your own models.

q: A media pipeline tolerates occasional duplicate messages and slight reordering but needs virtually unlimited throughput at the lowest cost per request. Which SQS queue type matches this relaxed profile?
options: A single EC2 instance holding an in-memory list
SNS FIFO topics for all traffic
explain: Standard queues maximize throughput with at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering, the right trade when consumers are idempotent. FIFO guarantees cost more and cap throughput in exchange for ordering the workload does not need, and a hand-rolled in-memory list is neither durable nor scalable.

q: A company runs a scaled-down but fully functional copy of its production environment in another Region, ready to take over traffic within minutes of an outage. Which disaster recovery strategy is this?
explain: Warm standby = a scaled-down live copy that can scale to full production quickly — faster recovery than pilot light, cheaper than multi-site. Backup and restore has no running copy (slowest); a pilot light keeps only the minimal core, not a functional copy.

q: Which strategy keeps an application in its existing environment for now, possibly migrating it in a later phase?
explain: Retain is the deliberate decision to leave a workload where it runs, at least temporarily. Retire eliminates it; the other two move it with different degrees of change.

q: A company must run workloads on dedicated physical servers to satisfy software licensing terms. Which EC2 option?
explain: Dedicated Hosts = physical servers dedicated to your use, giving visibility into sockets and cores for BYOL licensing. Dedicated Instances run on dedicated hardware without host visibility.

q: Database instances sit in subnets whose route tables have no route to an internet gateway at all. What kind of subnets are these, and what is the immediate consequence for the databases?
options: Private subnets; the databases cannot be reached directly from the internet
Peered subnets; the databases join another VPC automatically
Edge subnets; the databases are cached at edge locations
Public subnets; the databases get public IP addresses automatically
explain: Subnets without an internet gateway route are private, which shields their instances from inbound internet connections while still allowing internal VPC communication. They receive no automatic public addresses, are not cached anywhere, and have nothing inherently to do with VPC peering.

q: A firm in Toronto opens a second office in Vancouver and wants users there to reach its app quickly, but the app must remain in Canada. What should it evaluate first?
options: Moving the application to the cheapest Region worldwide
Ignoring latency because all Regions perform identically
Whether a Canadian Region or closer Canadian deployment option keeps data in-country with lower latency
explain: The evaluation must balance the residency constraint (stay in Canada) against latency improvement, the standard Region-selection trade-off. Cheapest-worldwide could breach the residency requirement.

q: A company needs point-in-time, incremental backups of its EBS volumes, stored durably and restorable to a new volume. Which feature provides this?
explain: EBS snapshots are incremental, point-in-time backups of volumes stored durably in S3 — restore one to create a new volume. AMIs are full machine templates; instance store is ephemeral scratch space; encryption protects data but isn't a backup.

AWS Prescriptive Guidance publishes strategies, guides, and patterns written by AWS experts and partners for specific outcomes such as migrations. Artifact hosts compliance reports; the CUR is billing data.
q: Which of these is an official AWS guidance publication series providing step-by-step, best-practice implementation guidance created by AWS experts?
An online game must store player session data with single-digit millisecond latency and unpredictable traffic spikes, without managing any servers. Which database fits best?
explain: DynamoDB is serverless NoSQL key-value with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale — built for sessions, carts, and leaderboards. RDS requires provisioning and suits relational workloads; Redshift is an OLAP data warehouse; Neptune is a graph database.

q: An engineering group likes Elastic Beanstalk for quick deployments but now needs to version-control every network and database setting as reviewable code that can recreate the whole environment. Which service should the group adopt for the infrastructure itself?
options: AWS Elastic Beanstalk saved configurations only
Amazon EC2 user data scripts only
explain: CloudFormation models the full stack in JSON or YAML templates that can be versioned, reviewed, and redeployed identically, which is infrastructure as code. Beanstalk saved configurations and user data help individual environments but do not declaratively model the entire infrastructure the same way.

q: Hundreds of smart meters publish status events every minute; downstream, a billing system, a maintenance system, and an analytics pipeline each need their own copy of every event to process independently. Which design fans each event out to all three consumers reliably?
options: Publish events to an SNS topic with an SQS queue subscribed for each consuming system
Send events through one Lambda function that calls the systems in sequence
Store events as objects in S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Write events to a single SQS queue that all three systems poll competitively
explain: The SNS-to-SQS fan-out pattern gives each consumer its own queue fed by the same topic, so systems process independently at their own pace with durable buffering. One shared queue would deliver each message to only one poller, archives cannot feed live pipelines, and sequential calls couple the systems' availability together.

q: A landscaping supplier's finance chief likes that a failed online-ordering experiment cost only a few dollars of metered usage instead of a purchased server sitting idle in a closet. Which advantage made the failed experiment cheap?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explain: Because cost followed usage, shutting the experiment down stopped the expense, which is the variable-expense advantage. Capacity guessing, facility upkeep, and release speed are not what kept the experiment inexpensive.

q: Which storage service is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability of objects?
explain: S3 redundantly stores objects across multiple devices and AZs, delivering 11 nines of durability. EBS volumes live in one AZ; instance store is ephemeral; EFS is file storage.

q: A team already runs Kubernetes on-premises and wants AWS to manage the Kubernetes control plane while the team keeps its existing manifests and tooling. Which service fits?
explain: EKS = managed Kubernetes: AWS runs the control plane, you keep standard Kubernetes manifests and tools. ECS is AWS's own orchestrator (not Kubernetes); Fargate is serverless compute for containers; Beanstalk is a PaaS for uploading code.

q: A podcast network stores episode audio; brand-new episodes are streamed constantly, older seasons are opened rarely, and nobody can predict which old episode a viral post might revive. Which S3 storage class automatically adapts placement to each object's changing access pattern?
explain: Intelligent-Tiering monitors each object's access and moves it between frequent and infrequent tiers automatically, removing the need to predict patterns. The IA classes assume infrequent access from the start, and Glacier Flexible requires restore steps before reading.

q: Which service collects metrics and can trigger an alarm — for example, alerting when EC2 CPU exceeds 80%?
explain: CloudWatch is the monitoring service: metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards. CloudTrail answers 'who did what'; CloudWatch answers 'how is it performing'.

q: Developers need temporary access to a production S3 bucket. What is the AWS-recommended approach?
options: Email the bucket credentials to the team
Share the root account access keys
Create an IAM user per developer with permanent access keys
Create an IAM role that the developers assume
explain: IAM roles grant temporary credentials (via STS) — nothing long-lived to leak. Never share root keys or distribute permanent credentials; roles are the exam's answer for every "temporary access" scenario.

q: A health insurer stores claims on AWS and a partner asks which services it may use for regulated data. What concept should guide service selection?
options: HIPAA-eligible services covered under the BAA
Any service, because the BAA covers everything automatically
explain: Only services designated HIPAA-eligible and covered by the BAA may process protected health information, and they must still be configured compliantly.

Infrastructure Event Management (IEM) provides structured planning, preparation, and real-time support around discrete events such as migrations, launches, and peak shopping periods. It is included with Enterprise and available for a fee on Business.
q: A team wants AWS Support engineers to proactively monitor their environment during a planned migration weekend. Which offering is designed for event-based support like this?
A startup chooses Elastic Beanstalk specifically because it wants to upload code and have capacity provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring handled automatically. Which model attracted it?
explain: Beanstalk is PaaS: the platform assembles and manages the environment around the customer's code. The startup is not consuming a finished third-party application, so SaaS does not fit.

q: A weather startup's DynamoDB usage is smooth and predictable month after month, so the team wants to set table throughput in advance and let AWS adjust it within defined limits as traffic wobbles slightly. Which capacity mode fits a known, steady workload?
explain: Provisioned mode suits predictable workloads: you declare read and write capacity units (with optional Auto Scaling) and pay for that reservation. On-demand mode exists for unpredictable traffic billed per request, and Spot and dedicated modes are not DynamoDB options at all.

q: A Danish design tool gains its first users in Japan after the team enables a Tokyo Region deployment without hiring local infrastructure staff or shipping equipment. Which advantage applies?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Entering a faraway market with no local build-out is go global in minutes. No pricing, billing-model, or facility-closure detail drives the answer; the new geography does.

q: Under IaaS, which task remains the customer's responsibility?
options: Replacing failed disks in the data center
Patching the guest operating system on virtual servers
explain: IaaS customers control and maintain the guest OS and above, while the provider owns physical hosts, disks, and the hypervisor. This split is the defining responsibility line for IaaS.

q: A product team debates Local Zones and Wavelength for a mobile game companion app. The players are spread across a metro area on ordinary broadband and Wi-Fi, not on a specific carrier's 5G network. Which option matches the audience's actual connectivity?
options: AWS Outposts, which requires a rack in every player's home
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration, which hosts game compute at edges
AWS Wavelength, which only serves devices attached to partner 5G networks
AWS Local Zones, which extend AWS services into large metropolitan areas for nearby end users
explain: Local Zones place AWS compute in big population centers to trim latency for broadband users generally. Wavelength zones exist specifically inside telecommunications carriers' 5G infrastructure, Outposts belongs in facilities you operate, and Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads rather than hosting compute.

q: A cost review finds a compute workload running on older Intel-based instances; an engineer proposes moving it to AWS Graviton processor-based instances. What is the usual motivation the exam associates with Graviton?
options: Better price-performance for many general workloads compared with equivalent x86 instances
Graviton is required to run any container on ECS
Graviton instances are the only ones supporting EBS volumes
Graviton provides the GPU acceleration needed for ML training
explain: Graviton (Arm-based) instances are promoted for superior price-performance across web, container, and many general workloads versus comparable x86 options. Containers, EBS support, and acceleration are available broadly; GPUs belong to accelerated computing families, not Graviton.

q: A company wants one place that shows, for every supported resource type, whether configurations comply with its internal standards, with a history it can hand to auditors each quarter. Which pairing delivers both the evaluations and the history?
options: AWS Config rules and the AWS Config configuration timeline
CloudTrail log files in an S3 bucket alone
explain: Config continuously records configurations (the timeline auditors review) and evaluates them with rules that flag violations as they occur, covering both halves of the request. Dashboards show performance, raw CloudTrail files are hard to audit without tooling, and Trusted Advisor's checks are advisory best practices rather than your own standards.

q: Which event can directly trigger an AWS Lambda function without any custom polling code?
options: An object being created in an Amazon S3 bucket
An EC2 instance reaching 90 percent CPU for an hour
A user opening the AWS Management Console
explain: S3 object-created events are a native Lambda trigger, alongside API Gateway calls, DynamoDB Streams, and EventBridge schedules. Console sign-ins, CPU levels, and invoices do not invoke functions directly; CPU alarms act through CloudWatch instead.

q: Which statement about SOC reports in Artifact is correct?
options: They describe the customer application security
They replace the need for customer audits entirely
They certify that a customer workload is compliant
They report on AWS controls and are used as evidence that the underlying platform is compliant
explain: Artifact reports attest to AWS-managed controls. They support, but do not replace, the customer responsibility to build and audit a compliant workload on top.

q: An IAM user needs temporary elevated access for an incident and then must return to normal rights. What pattern fits best?
options: Create a second permanent admin user
Share the root login during the incident
Have the user assume an elevated role for the incident session only
explain: Assuming an elevated role gives time-bound credentials that expire with the session, matching incident needs without leaving permanent excess privilege behind.

q: A bank needs a database whose transaction history is immutable and cryptographically verifiable, so auditors can prove no record was ever altered after the fact. Which database provides a transparent, append-only ledger with that proof built in?
explain: QLDB is a ledger database with a journal that is append-only and cryptographically chained, letting anyone verify that history has not been tampered with. DynamoDB, Aurora, and ElastiCache all permit normal updates and deletes, so they cannot offer built-in ledger proof.

q: A company peers VPC A with VPC B, and VPC B with VPC C, then is surprised that A cannot reach C through B. Which peering property explains this behavior?
options: VPC peering blocks all database ports by default
VPC peering is non-transitive, so each pair needs its own connection
VPC peering only works within a single Availability Zone
VPC peering routes expire after 24 hours
explain: Peering connections never forward traffic onward: A-to-B and B-to-C peering does not grant A-to-C reachability, which is why large estates adopt Transit Gateway's transitive hub. Peering has no 24-hour expiry, spans AZs freely, and does not filter ports by itself.

q: A web application is being probed with SQL injection attacks. Which service blocks them at the application layer?
explain: WAF is a Layer 7 web application firewall with managed rules for SQL injection and XSS. Shield defends against DDoS; GuardDuty detects threats but doesn't block inline; NACLs are stateless subnet filters.

q: Which TWO are genuine cloud economics benefits a company can realize on AWS? (Select TWO.)
options: Paying the same amount even if usage triples
Releasing unused resources to stop their charges
Receiving a guaranteed profit each quarter
Paying only for resources actually consumed
explain: Consumption billing and the ability to release idle resources are real economic benefits. Profits are never guaranteed, and usage-based bills do rise when consumption rises.

q: A retailer is modernizing and replaces its aging Classic Load Balancer. For standard web traffic with content-based routing, which current load balancer family do architects reach for instead?
options: Application Load Balancer and Network Load Balancer
explain: Modern designs split web load balancing between the ALB for Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS features and the NLB for Layer 4 performance, superseding the Classic Load Balancer's generation. Gateway Load Balancers insert appliances, and NAT or DNS weighting do not replace load balancer functions like target health checks.

q: Who chooses the Availability Zones and VPC layout for a customer application, as part of security in the cloud?
explain: Architecture choices such as VPC layout, subnets, and AZ placement are customer design responsibilities, even though AWS operates the facilities behind them.

q: Before analysts can query new supplier files in S3 with Athena, a crawler scans the files, infers their schemas, and registers tables so the files become queryable. Which Glue component performs this automatic schema discovery?
explain: Glue crawlers scan data stores, classify formats, infer schemas, and write table definitions into the Glue Data Catalog that Athena and other services then use. The other options are query, visualization, or streaming constructs that do not perform schema discovery.

q: An Auto Scaling group is configured to maintain 4 EC2 instances. One instance fails its health check. What does Auto Scaling do?
options: Continues running with 3 instances until someone intervenes
Terminates the unhealthy instance and launches a replacement to keep 4 running
Moves the failed instance to another Availability Zone
explain: Auto Scaling continuously health-checks instances and replaces unhealthy ones automatically to maintain the desired count. It never waits for manual intervention, and it replaces (terminates + launches) rather than moving instances between AZs.

q: A healthcare startup will handle protected health information on AWS. What must it sign with AWS before doing so?
explain: HIPAA requires a Business Associate Addendum with AWS, and the workload must use HIPAA-eligible services configured compliantly by the customer.

q: An administrator grants a billing clerk access to view invoices but nothing else. Which principle is being applied?
explain: Least privilege grants only the permissions required for the job, here billing visibility alone, reducing blast radius if the credentials are misused or compromised.

q: Which TWO services can run application code or containers without the customer managing any servers? (Select TWO.)
options: Amazon RDS read replicas used as compute
explain: Lambda runs functions and Fargate runs containers, both with AWS managing the underlying servers entirely. EC2 is the classic customer-managed server option, and RDS replicas are database copies, not general serverless compute.

q: An e-commerce site automatically adds web servers during a flash sale and removes them afterward. Which concept does this describe?
explain: Elasticity = resources automatically expand and contract with demand. Scalability is the ability to handle growth; agility is speed of innovation; fault tolerance is surviving component failure.

q: What is the difference between AWS Artifact and AWS Audit Manager?
options: Artifact scans containers, Audit Manager blocks DDoS
They are the same service with two names
Artifact is only for billing documents
Artifact provides AWS compliance reports, Audit Manager collects evidence about the customer usage
explain: Artifact is where AWS publishes its own reports and agreements. Audit Manager examines the customer account activity and assembles evidence for the customer audits.

q: Which pillar asks teams to understand and reduce the environmental impact of their cloud workloads over time?
explain: The Sustainability pillar addresses the environmental dimension of workloads, including resource efficiency viewed through emissions and energy. Cost Optimization views the same actions through money instead.

q: A compliance review notes that a firm's Direct Connect link is private but asks whether the traffic on it is encrypted by default. Which accurate statement should the review record?
options: Direct Connect is a private connection but does not encrypt traffic by itself; encryption can be added, for example with a VPN over the Direct Connect link
Direct Connect traffic crosses the public internet unencrypted by design
Direct Connect automatically encrypts everything with no configuration possible or needed
Direct Connect cannot carry encrypted traffic under any configuration
explain: Direct Connect avoids the public internet, which provides privacy of path but not cryptographic encryption; teams needing encryption layer IPsec VPN over the connection or use application-level encryption. It neither encrypts automatically nor forbids encryption, and its traffic does not traverse the public internet.

q: A fintech startup in South America must keep all customer records inside its home country by law, and its users are concentrated in one metropolitan area. Which Region-selection reasoning should lead the design?
options: Deploy in every Region at once so the law averages out
Choose the Region with the most edge locations for record storage
Choose the cheapest Region worldwide regardless of the law
Choose the Region in that country to satisfy data residency law, accepting that compliance outranks small latency gains elsewhere
explain: Data residency and compliance requirements are a primary Region-selection factor: regulated records stay in an in-country (or legally approved) Region even if another Region is cheaper. Cost, edge counts, and global spraying of regulated data do not override a legal residency mandate.

q: A CIO asks for the difference between the Personal Health Dashboard and the AWS Health Dashboard's organization view during an outage review. Which explanation is accurate?
options: The personal view shows events affecting your own account's resources; the organization view aggregates health events across all accounts in the organization
The personal view covers every AWS customer worldwide; the organization view covers only competitors
The organization view replaces CloudWatch alarms for application metrics
Both views show only global service status with no account-specific information
explain: AWS Health provides a public service-status picture plus account-specific views: the personal (your account) view shows events impacting your resources, while the organization view rolls those events up across member accounts. Neither view is a metrics system like CloudWatch, and neither concerns other customers' resources.
Developer Support starts at $29 per month (or 3% of monthly AWS charges, whichever is greater). Business starts at $100, Enterprise On-Ramp at $5,500, and Enterprise at $15,000 per month.
q: What is the minimum monthly price of the AWS Developer Support plan?
A Windows-based workload needs Kerberos authentication and Group Policy from a managed domain. Which AWS service should the team choose?
options: AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD
explain: Directory Service for Microsoft AD delivers managed Active Directory with Kerberos and Group Policy support for Windows and directory-aware workloads.

q: A startup stores user uploads in S3 and wants objects older than 30 days in a rarely used reports bucket to move to cheaper storage automatically, then be deleted after two years. Which two Lifecycle actions does this policy combine?
explain: Lifecycle rules pair transitions, which move objects to cheaper classes as they age, with expirations, which delete objects or versions at end of life. The other action pairs belong to replication, access control, and reporting features, not Lifecycle management.

q: A flash-sale platform cannot predict DynamoDB request volume at all; some hours see a hundred requests, others see two million. Which capacity mode removes capacity planning from this launch entirely?
options: Reserved capacity purchased for three years
Provisioned capacity fixed for the year
explain: On-demand mode bills per request and absorbs unpredictable spikes with no throughput planning, which is precisely the flash-sale profile. Fixed or ticket-based provisioning risks throttling during the sale, and DynamoDB sells no three-year capacity reservations.

q: A team wants an alert whenever an S3 bucket becomes public, based on configuration evaluation rather than API calls alone. Which service evaluates the bucket posture?
explain: Config rules continuously or on-change evaluate resource configurations, such as bucket public access settings, and report compliant or noncompliant status.

q: A security manager asks who made a specific IAM policy change at 2 AM. Which log source answers with the caller identity and time?
explain: CloudTrail records management events with who, what, when, and from where for API activity such as IAM policy changes, forming the core audit trail.

q: Which statement correctly distinguishes CAF from the Well-Architected Framework?
options: The two frameworks contain identical categories with different names
CAF guides the organizational adoption of cloud, while Well-Architected guides the design of individual workloads
CAF designs individual workloads, while Well-Architected plans company-wide adoption
CAF applies only after all workloads are migrated
explain: CAF's six perspectives organize the people, governance, and platform changes of adoption, while Well-Architected's six pillars evaluate workload design. Keeping that scope difference straight is a favorite exam distinction.

Short-term trials begin when you activate a service and run from a few days to a few months depending on the service. They are the third Free Tier category alongside Always Free and 12 Months Free offers.
q: A developer activates an AWS service that offers a 30-day free usage period for new users of that service. Which Free Tier type is this?

explain: Basic and Developer plans include seven core Trusted Advisor checks (such as S3 bucket permissions, MFA on the root account, and service limits). The complete check library requires Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, or Enterprise Support.
options: The full set of Trusted Advisor checks
No Trusted Advisor checks at any plan below Business
Seven core checks covering security, service limits, and basic configuration
q: Which AWS Trusted Advisor checks are available to customers on the Basic and Developer Support plans?
Instead of freezing a perfect architecture on day one, a team expects its design to change as it learns, using services that allow components to be swapped over time. Which principle is this?
options: Document the architecture and lock it
explain: Evolutionary architecture assumes requirements and services will change, so designs stay adaptable. Locking the design at launch contradicts both cloud practice and business learning.

q: A data team must synchronize 200 TB from a network file system on-premises into Amazon S3 on a recurring schedule, with built-in validation that files arrived intact. Which service is purpose-built for scheduled, large-scale data movement between storage systems?
explain: DataSync automates moving and synchronizing data between on-premises storage and AWS services, handling scheduling, verification, and bandwidth control at scale. DMS migrates databases, EventBridge routes events, and Systems Manager manages operations; none is a bulk file-sync engine.

q: Which TWO statements about Availability Zones are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: Availability Zones in a Region are connected by low-latency links
Each Availability Zone spans several continents
An Availability Zone contains multiple Regions
Each Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers
explain: An AZ is one or more discrete data centers within a Region, and AZs are interconnected with low-latency links for replication. AZs never contain Regions or span continents.

q: Which of these tasks can ONLY be performed by the AWS account root user?
explain: Closing an account is root-only — IAM users, even administrators, cannot do it. The other tasks are routine IAM-permitted actions, which is exactly why daily work should never use root. Domain 3: Cloud Technology and Services (Q55–88)

q: An inline policy is best described as a policy that does what?
options: Is embedded directly on a single user, group, or role
Applies to every account in an organization
explain: Inline policies are embedded in exactly one identity and are deleted with it, suited to strict one-to-one permission needs rather than reusable shared permissions.
The Concierge team is an Enterprise Support benefit staffed by billing and account experts. It handles non-technical account and billing questions, separate from the technical support engineers.
q: Which team, available only with Enterprise Support, helps customers with billing and account questions such as payment issues and account management?

explain: Developer Support targets less than 24 business hours for general guidance and less than 12 business hours for an impaired system. Sub-hour targets require Business or higher, which operate around the clock.
options: Within the same calendar week, no target
q: A customer opens a case about a general 'how-to' question on the Developer plan. What response time applies?

A regional furniture retailer cancels a planned $90,000 server purchase and instead pays a monthly bill that rises and falls with the compute and storage it actually consumes. Which cloud advantage is the retailer using?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explain: Replacing a large upfront capital purchase with consumption-based monthly billing is trading fixed expense for variable expense. Economies of scale concerns provider pricing power, and going global concerns geographic reach.

The Free Tier has three types: Always Free (ongoing limits, e.g., Lambda requests), 12 Months Free (e.g., S3, EC2, CloudFront allowances for the first year), and short-term Trials tied to activating a service.
q: Which AWS Free Tier category includes offers such as Amazon S3 free storage for the first 12 months after sign-up?
Multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones need shared file storage accessed via NFS. Which service?
explain: EFS (Elastic File System) = managed NFS file storage that scales automatically and is accessible from many instances across AZs. EBS attaches to one instance in one AZ; instance store is ephemeral.

q: Which EC2 storage option loses its data when the instance is stopped or terminated?
explain: Instance store volumes are physically attached ephemeral disks — fast, but data vanishes on stop/terminate. EBS persists independently of the instance; EFS and S3 are network storage that outlive any instance.

q: A customer runs a database on Amazon EC2. Who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?
options: Shared equally between AWS and the customer
explain: On EC2 (IaaS), the customer controls the OS — so patching it is the customer's job. AWS handles the underlying hypervisor and physical hosts. With managed services like RDS, AWS takes on more of the stack.

q: A global retailer wants a single domain name to keep working even if an entire Region's storefront fails, with DNS automatically steering shoppers to the surviving Region's storefront. Which combination delivers DNS-level regional failover?
options: Route 53 failover routing with health checks on each Region's endpoint
A larger EC2 instance in the primary Region
CloudFront caching with a very long TTL
Two S3 buckets with versioning enabled
explain: Failover routing plus health checks moves DNS answers to the healthy Region when the primary fails checks, giving shoppers a working destination automatically. Versioned buckets store data but do not steer shoppers, a bigger instance remains a single point of failure, and long-lived caches can keep serving a dead origin's stale content.

q: Which CAF perspective helps an organization maximize business value while managing and minimizing business risk during adoption?
explain: Governance is framed in CAF as maximizing value while managing risk across the adoption portfolio. Business perspective sets outcomes; Governance oversees that they are achieved within risk tolerance.
Enterprise On-Ramp targets less than 30 minutes for business-critical systems down and less than 1 hour for urgent issues. The less-than-15-minute target belongs to full Enterprise Support.
q: An Enterprise On-Ramp customer suffers a business-critical system outage. What initial response time does the plan target?
A video startup renders on EC2 Spot Instances. Spot capacity runs on AWS hardware. Who secures the rendering application itself?
explain: The application layer is always customer responsibility on EC2, regardless of pricing model. AWS secures the hardware and hypervisor that Spot Instances run on.

q: What is the role of an AWS edge location?
options: Hosting the only copy of a customer's database
Replacing Regions for running large applications
Caching content and serving services such as CloudFront and Route 53 close to end users for lower latency
Providing office space for AWS support teams
explain: Edge locations are endpoints for services like CloudFront content caching and Route 53, positioned near users to cut latency. They outnumber Regions and do not replace them for general application hosting.

q: Which advantage is shown when developers can obtain a test environment in minutes instead of waiting six weeks for purchased hardware to arrive and be racked?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Minutes-long provisioning that lets teams move and experiment faster is increased speed and agility. Facility savings and global reach are side effects at most; the stem is about elapsed time to start work.

Amazon S3 charges for the amount of data stored, the number and type of requests (GET, PUT, etc.), and data transfer out — plus features like replication. CPU utilization is an EC2-style metric, not an S3 pricing factor.
options: The data transferred out of S3
The number of CPU cores in your account
The storage class of the objects
The number of requests made against the bucket
q: Which of the following is NOT a factor in Amazon S3 pricing?
A developer needs to assume a production role only when connecting from the corporate network. How can this condition be enforced?
options: By adding a Condition element to the policy or trust policy
By using a larger instance type
explain: Policy Condition elements restrict when a policy applies, for example by source IP, MFA presence, or time, and can be used in role trust and permission policies.

q: What data sources does GuardDuty analyze to generate findings?
options: CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs
explain: GuardDuty consumes CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS query logs, correlating them with threat intelligence to detect malicious or anomalous activity.

q: A compliance pipeline needs clickstream records delivered automatically into S3 and Redshift in near-real time, buffered and batched, with no consumer code to write or servers to run. Which Kinesis family member is the managed delivery service for this?
options: AWS Lambda with a 15-minute batch window
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with custom consumers
explain: Firehose is the fully managed delivery stream: it captures, buffers, optionally transforms, and loads data into destinations like S3 and Redshift without you building consumers. Data Streams would require writing and running consumer applications, which the scenario explicitly rules out.

q: An architect assumes any single component can fail at any moment and ensures the application keeps working when one does. Which cloud design principle is this?
options: Design for a single data center
Centralize all functions in one service
explain: Designing for failure means expecting component faults and building recovery and redundancy in from the start. The opposite assumptions are what cause brittle architectures.

q: Which service is the best fit to centrally view AWS Foundational Security Best Practices control results across accounts?
explain: Security Hub evaluates the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard across accounts and Regions and reports each control status in its dashboard.

q: An accounting firm scans paper invoices and needs not just the raw characters but the structured fields (vendor, totals, line-item tables) extracted into its systems automatically. Which service goes beyond plain OCR to understand document structure?
explain: Textract extracts text plus structure from documents: forms' key-value pairs, tables, and handwriting, which is exactly what invoice processing requires. Rekognition labels images, Comprehend analyzes already-digital text, and Transcribe works on audio, so none parses scanned document layouts.

q: A team needs to know whether a container image pushed to ECR contains a library with a known CVE before deployment. Which service reports it?
explain: Inspector scans ECR container images for package vulnerabilities with known CVEs and reports severity, so teams can remediate before workloads run.

q: A mining operation at a remote site with unreliable connectivity collects 40 TB of survey data on rugged devices and ships the devices to AWS to ingest the data. Which Snow family member is the small, portable option suited to harsh field conditions?
explain: Snowcone is the smallest Snow device, portable and rugged for edge and field collection where connectivity is poor, with data shipped back for import to S3. Snowmobile is an exabyte-scale truck, EFS is an in-cloud file system, and DataSync needs usable network bandwidth.

q: A company migrates its on-premises database to Amazon RDS with only minor changes to the application, keeping the same database engine family. Which migration strategy is this?
explain: Replatform ("lift, tinker, and shift") = moving with small optimizations, like shifting a database to RDS. Rehost is lift-and-shift with no changes; Repurchase means switching to a different (usually SaaS) product; Retire means decommissioning the application.

q: Remote employees at a design studio connect one by one from home networks to the company VPC to reach internal tools. Which VPN variant is built for individual user devices rather than whole office networks?
explain: Client VPN gives individual devices a secure tunnel into AWS or on-premises networks, administered per user and device. Site-to-Site VPN links entire networks through customer gateways, Direct Connect is a dedicated circuit, and Connect attachments extend hub routing for SD-WAN appliances.

q: A consultancy estimates a migration business case. It counts avoided data-center lease renewal, reduced hardware refresh spending, and lower operations headcount as savings. What kind of analysis is it performing?
explain: Weighing all ownership costs, including facilities and staffing, against cloud costs is a total cost of ownership comparison. The listed items are cost categories, not security or reliability activities.

q: What does "fault tolerance" mean?
options: Data is backed up every day
The system continues operating even when a component fails
The system stays available during planned maintenance windows
explain: Fault tolerance = no single point of failure brings the system down; it keeps running through the failure. High availability is the broader goal of minimal downtime; fault tolerance is one way to achieve it.

q: A developer wants to deploy a web app by simply uploading code, letting AWS handle capacity, load balancing, and patching. Which service?
explain: Elastic Beanstalk is PaaS: you supply the code, it provisions and manages the EC2, load balancer, and auto-scaling underneath. Lambda is for event-driven functions, not full web apps; CloudFormation is infrastructure-as-code templates.

q: Adding more identical web servers behind a load balancer to serve a growing user base is an example of which scaling approach?
explain: Adding more instances is horizontal scaling, or scaling out. Vertical scaling makes a single instance bigger; bursting describes temporary capacity use, not the direction of growth.

q: A finance director classifies a one-time purchase of on-premises servers, expected to last five years, for budgeting purposes. How is that purchase best classified?
explain: Buying long-lived hardware upfront is capital expenditure: a large fixed investment depreciated over years. Cloud usage charges, by contrast, are operating expenditure tied to consumption.

q: Which TWO are perspectives of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework? (Select TWO.)
explain: CAF's six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations. Marketing, Sales, and Procurement are not CAF perspectives. Domain 2: Security and Compliance (Q25–54)

q: A developer platform runs on EC2 and the team wants custom antivirus on each instance. Who installs and updates that antivirus?
options: AWS by default on all EC2
The antivirus cannot be used on EC2
explain: Customer-chosen endpoint software on EC2 instances is installed and maintained by the customer. GuardDuty detects threats but does not install antivirus agents.

q: A trainee asks for the plain definition of an Availability Zone to put in onboarding notes. Which statement should the notes carry?
options: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within an AWS Region
An Availability Zone is a country where AWS sells services
An Availability Zone is a CloudFront cache point at an airport
An Availability Zone is a single server rack inside a Region
