explain: Each AZ consists of one or more discrete data centers engineered with redundant power, networking, and connectivity, and Regions contain multiple AZs for fault isolation. Racks are far smaller than an AZ, countries describe geography rather than AZs, and cache points are edge locations.

q: A development team needs servers for short-term testing with unpredictable stop times. Which EC2 pricing model fits best?
explain: On-Demand = pay by the second with no commitment — perfect for short, unpredictable work. Reserved needs a 1–3 year commitment; Spot can be interrupted; Dedicated Hosts are for physical-server compliance needs.

q: EC2 instances in a private subnet need outbound internet access for software updates but must NOT be reachable from the internet. Which component?
explain: A NAT gateway lets private-subnet instances initiate outbound connections while blocking unsolicited inbound traffic. An internet gateway would make the subnet public; peering connects VPCs; a virtual private gateway terminates VPNs.

q: Which service aggregates security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie into a single prioritized dashboard?
explain: Security Hub centralizes findings across security services and accounts into one view with standardized severity. Detective is for investigating an incident's root cause once found.

q: Which TWO statements contrast DMS and SCT correctly? (Select TWO.)
options: DMS moves and replicates the actual data between databases
DMS converts stored procedures between SQL dialects
SCT converts schema and code from one database engine to another
SCT continuously replicates changed rows during cutover
explain: The pair divides migration labor: SCT handles schema and code conversion between engines, while DMS handles data movement and ongoing replication until cutover. Swapping those roles, as the two incorrect options do, is the classic confusion to avoid.

q: Which strategy is the most expensive and time-consuming but delivers the greatest cloud-native benefit?
explain: Refactoring re-architects the application around cloud-native services, costing the most effort while unlocking the most capability. Rehost and replatform are faster but shallower.

q: What is an AWS Region?
options: A content caching point at an internet exchange
A geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones that are isolated from each other
A single data center building inside a city
One rack of servers within a data hall
explain: A Region is a named geographic area made up of several AZs, each AZ being one or more discrete data centers. A single building describes part of an AZ, not a Region.

q: A non-critical internal tool can tolerate several hours of downtime after a disaster. The company wants the cheapest possible recovery option. Which disaster recovery strategy fits best?
explain: Backup and restore = periodically backing up data and rebuilding after a disaster — the cheapest strategy, with the longest recovery time. Pilot light, warm standby, and multi-site all keep infrastructure running in the second Region, which costs more.

q: A multi-account company wants Firewall Manager to apply a WAF policy, but one account already has conflicting rules. What does Firewall Manager do conceptually?
options: It converts WAF rules into IAM policies
It disables WAF for the whole organization
It identifies noncompliance and can remediate the account firewall configuration
explain: Firewall Manager continuously evaluates member accounts against its policies and reports or remediates noncompliant firewall configurations to keep coverage uniform.

q: A company needs to launch 50 identically configured web servers — same OS, patches, and application code. What should it create first?
options: An EBS snapshot of user data
explain: An AMI is a template containing the OS, software, and configuration — launch any number of identical instances from it. EBS snapshots back up volumes; the instance type sets size, not configuration; placement groups control physical placement for latency.
Only the full Enterprise Support plan includes a dedicated TAM who works exclusively with that customer. Enterprise On-Ramp provides access to a pool of TAMs shared across customers instead.
q: Which AWS Support plan provides a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) assigned to a single customer account?
A developer is denied access even though their group policy allows the action, and an SCP in the organization denies that service. Why is the request denied?
options: Group policies expire after a year
The console blocks new services by default
IAM groups cannot allow service actions
SCPs set a maximum permission ceiling that identity policies cannot exceed
explain: SCPs act as guardrails capping what member accounts can do. When an SCP denies a service, no identity policy inside the account can allow it.

q: A compliance officer asks a different question than the operations team: not how the servers are performing, but exactly who stopped the production database last Friday and from which IP address. Which service's records answer the officer?
explain: CloudTrail is the audit log of API activity: it records who made each call, when, and from where, across console, CLI, and SDK actions. CloudWatch measures performance, Systems Manager executes operations, and QuickSight visualizes business data; only CloudTrail answers who-did-what questions.

q: During an audit, a bank must prove who accessed its S3 data. Enabling and reviewing access logging is whose responsibility?
options: AWS automatically proves it without setup
explain: Customers must enable and review logging for their resources and retain evidence for audits. AWS provides CloudTrail and S3 logging features for the customer to use.

q: A CIO wants one console and one set of policies to schedule and audit backups for EBS volumes, RDS databases, DynamoDB tables, and EFS file systems across accounts. Which service centralizes backup management this way?
explain: AWS Backup centrally defines backup plans, schedules, retention, and cross-account policies spanning many AWS services, including EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, and EFS. Lifecycle policies only manage S3 objects, manual snapshots cover one resource type, and CloudTrail records API calls rather than managing backups.

q: An on-call engineer watches a dashboard of CPU, network, and disk graphs for the production fleet and has alarms that page the team when error rates spike. Which service supplies these metrics, dashboards, and alarms?
explain: CloudWatch collects metrics, logs, and events, renders dashboards, and fires alarms on thresholds, which is the operational monitoring picture described. CloudTrail records API history for auditing, Config tracks resource configuration changes, and X-Ray traces application requests rather than hosting fleet metrics.

q: If a customer managed KMS key is disabled, what happens to data encrypted under it?
options: It is automatically decrypted for convenience
It cannot be decrypted until the key is re-enabled
explain: Disabling a KMS key immediately blocks encrypt and decrypt operations with it, which is a fast way to cut off access to data protected by that key.

q: Which TWO scenarios are examples of the Retire strategy? (Select TWO.)
options: Decommissioning a duplicate internal wiki that nobody maintains or reads
Shutting down a legacy payroll program replaced years ago that still runs idle
Moving a file server to EC2 unchanged
explain: Retire applies to workloads switched off because they are unused or superseded, like the orphaned wiki and the idle legacy program. The other options are rehost and refactor migrations.

q: A game studio needs single-digit millisecond latency for players in one metro area — closer than the nearest AWS Region can deliver. Which extends AWS compute and storage to the metro edge?
explain: Local Zones place AWS compute and storage in major metro areas for low-latency local users. Edge locations cache CloudFront content (no general compute); Outposts lives in the customer's own data center; Wavelength embeds compute in 5G carrier networks.

q: Which design principle is satisfied by automatically adding compute during a traffic spike and removing it when traffic falls?
explain: Elasticity is the principle of capacity following demand automatically in both directions. Decoupling concerns component independence, and evolutionary design concerns change over time.

q: A development team stores catalog data as JSON documents and its application already speaks the MongoDB API; the team wants a managed, scalable document database without rewriting drivers. Which service is MongoDB-compatible by design?
explain: DocumentDB is AWS's MongoDB-compatible document database, letting existing MongoDB drivers and tools work against a managed, scalable service. Keyspaces targets Cassandra workloads, Neptune is graph, and Timestream is a time-series database.

q: Which TWO facts about Amazon ElastiCache should a new platform engineer learn first? (Select TWO.)
options: It is primarily an in-memory caching layer that sits in front of a database
It provides petabyte-scale SQL analytics over historical data
It offers Redis and Memcached as its two engines
It is the recommended system of record for financial ledgers
explain: ElastiCache provides managed Redis and Memcached in-memory caches that accelerate reads in front of a primary database. Financial ledgers belong in durable transactional stores or QLDB, and petabyte SQL analytics is Redshift's warehouse role, not a cache's job.

q: A container team uses Amazon ECS with the EC2 launch type today and wants to keep the same task definitions but stop managing hosts. Which change achieves this with the least redesign?
options: Rewrite every task as a Lambda function
Move the containers to Amazon Lightsail
Switch the services to the Fargate launch type
Register the tasks with AWS Batch
explain: ECS task definitions work on both launch types, so switching to Fargate keeps the application design while AWS takes over host provisioning and patching. Rewriting as functions or moving platforms would be far larger changes than the goal requires.

q: A company processes sensitive data under a policy that traffic to AWS services must never leave the private AWS network. How can its workloads reach S3 while honoring this policy?
options: A public subnet with Elastic IPs
explain: A gateway VPC endpoint adds a private route to S3 (and DynamoDB) that stays on the AWS network. An internet gateway exposes the subnet publicly; a NAT gateway still sends traffic out to the internet; public subnets with Elastic IPs are internet-facing by design.

q: Which service is a fully managed data warehouse for OLAP analytics over petabytes of structured data?
explain: Redshift = columnar data warehouse for complex analytical queries (OLAP). DynamoDB is operational NoSQL; RDS is transactional (OLTP); ElastiCache is in-memory caching.

q: A CloudWatch alarm on a web tier's CPU stays in the ALARM state for ten minutes during a product launch spike. Which automated responses can CloudWatch alarms trigger directly?
options: Conversion of the instances into Lambda functions
Notifications through SNS and actions such as Auto Scaling or EC2 actions
Automatic rewriting of the application source code
Deletion of the associated S3 buckets
explain: Alarms commonly notify via SNS and drive scaling or EC2 actions, closing the loop from observation to response. CloudWatch never edits application code, deletes storage on its own policies, or transmutes instances into functions.

q: An accounting firm buys a SaaS email product built on AWS. Which task remains the firm responsibility?
options: Managing which employees have accounts and access
explain: Even with SaaS-leaning services the customer manages its users, access, and data. The provider handles servers, patching, facilities, and the underlying platform.

q: A social platform's hardest questions are all about relationships: friends of friends, shared interests, and influence paths across a web of connected people. Which database is built to store and traverse exactly these connections?
explain: Neptune is a graph database optimized for storing relationships and running traversal queries such as friends-of-friends and recommendation paths. Redshift analyzes tabular data, DocumentDB stores JSON documents, and QLDB keeps a verifiable transaction ledger; none models connected data as a graph.

q: Which service provides DNS, domain registration, and global traffic routing with health checks?
explain: Route 53 = AWS's DNS service (plus domain registration and routing policies like latency-based and failover routing). CloudFront is the CDN; Global Accelerator improves global app performance via the AWS backbone.

q: A hospital group evaluates keeping a rarely used research cluster on-premises. The cluster still incurs power, cooling, and maintenance costs while idle. What does cloud economics suggest?
options: Idle owned capacity still costs money, so on-demand resources used only during studies would cut the waste
Rarely used systems should always stay on-premises
Maintenance contracts end automatically when systems idle
Idle hardware costs nothing after purchase
explain: Owned idle systems keep consuming budget through facilities and upkeep. Paying only during active studies removes the standing cost of an idle cluster.

q: Which statement about AWS Regions is TRUE?
options: Resources in one Region are automatically replicated to all other Regions
Each Region consists of multiple isolated Availability Zones
Each Region contains exactly one Availability Zone
A Region is a single data center building
explain: A Region is a geographic area made up of two or more AZs — each AZ being one or more discrete data centers. Replication across Regions never happens automatically; edge locations (not Regions) handle caching.

q: A company wants its SaaS CRM to trigger a Lambda function whenever a new lead is created, and also run a cleanup task every night at midnight. Which service routes these events and schedules?
explain: EventBridge is the serverless event bus: it ingests events from SaaS apps and AWS services and routes them to targets like Lambda, plus scheduled rules (cron). SQS/SNS are messaging primitives; Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows rather than routing SaaS events.

q: Security Hub shows a failing check because an account does not meet a security standard control. What is Security Hub primarily evaluating here?
options: Security posture against standards such as CIS benchmarks
explain: Security Hub runs standards checks, for example CIS AWS Foundations, and reports control pass or fail status as part of posture management.

q: A developer asks how to see what an S3 bucket policy looked like before a change last week. Which service timeline shows the prior configuration?
explain: Config records configuration items over time, so its timeline shows a resource prior settings and the changes between recorded versions.

q: Which TWO Route 53 routing policies exist for steering users based on geography or failure? (Select TWO.)
options: Geolocation routing, which answers based on the user's location
Latency routing, which always answers with the most expensive Region
Failover routing, which switches to a standby when health checks fail
Simple routing, which health-checks every record before answering
explain: Geolocation and failover are genuine Route 53 policies for location-based answers and active-passive disaster designs respectively. Latency-based routing picks the fastest Region, not the priciest, and simple routing performs no health checking at all.

q: A startup wants to avoid large upfront server purchases and pay only for what it uses. Which cloud benefit describes this?
options: Trade capital expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Cloud shifts spending from CapEx (buying hardware up front) to OpEx (pay-as-you-go variable expense). The other options are real benefits, but only A matches avoiding upfront purchases.

q: Which statement about encryption responsibility is correct?
options: Customers never need to think about encryption
Customers decide encryption requirements for their data
Encryption removes the need for IAM
AWS chooses all customer encryption keys
explain: Customers decide if, where, and how their data is encrypted and which keys to use. IAM is still required because encryption does not replace access control.

q: Which TWO load balancer facts are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: The Application Load Balancer is the best choice for raw UDP game traffic
The Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 and can preserve static IP addresses
The Gateway Load Balancer is used to terminate end-user TLS sessions for websites
The Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and understands HTTP and HTTPS
explain: ALB is the Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS balancer with content routing, and NLB is the Layer 4 balancer known for extreme performance and static IPs. UDP traffic belongs on NLB, not ALB, and GWLB exists for virtual appliances, not website TLS termination.

q: During a design review, an architect asks: 'What happens to users when, not if, this dependency becomes unavailable?' and requires an answer for every dependency. Which principle is being enforced?
explain: Framing failure as inevitable and designing the user experience around it is the design-for-failure principle. The review question is its classic expression.
Paid Support plans charge the greater of the plan's monthly minimum or a percentage of the account's monthly AWS usage, so support cost scales as usage grows. There is no per-case or per-seat charge.
options: A flat fee per support case opened
A percentage of the customer's revenue
The greater of the monthly minimum or a percentage of monthly AWS charges
q: How is the price of AWS paid Support plans (Developer and above) generally calculated beyond the minimum fee?
Route 53 health checks watch a company's primary site every 30 seconds. When the primary starts failing its checks, what does Route 53 do in a failover configuration?
options: It stops returning the primary's DNS record and answers with the secondary site's record
It increases the primary server's instance size
It emails the site's source code to the secondary Region
It automatically repairs the primary web server
explain: Health checks feed DNS decisions: once the primary is marked unhealthy, failover routing returns the secondary record so new visitors land on the standby site. Route 53 never repairs servers, resizes instances, or moves application code; it only changes DNS answers.

q: A company is assessed against ISO 27001 for its own ISMS while running on AWS. What role do AWS ISO certificates play?
options: They automatically certify the company ISMS
They exempt the company from access reviews
They provide evidence about the provider layer so the company can focus its ISMS scope on its own controls
explain: Provider certificates are inherited evidence for the platform layer. The company still certifies its own information security management system and controls.

q: A CISO's adoption team ensures that as accounts multiply, the organization keeps a single clear view of who can access what and can prove it to auditors. Which CAF perspective is this?
explain: Identity visibility, auditability, and access control during adoption are Security perspective capabilities in CAF. Governance consumes that evidence for oversight, but the control work itself is Security perspective.

q: If a physical server hosting many customers fails, who replaces the hardware?
explain: Hardware ownership and replacement are core security of the cloud duties for AWS. Customers never handle physical servers inside AWS data centers.

q: A retailer loads its entire product catalog into memory on EC2 to answer queries in microseconds, and the dataset keeps growing. Which EC2 instance family best matches a workload dominated by large in-memory datasets?
explain: Memory optimized instances provide large amounts of RAM per vCPU for in-memory databases, real-time caches, and big-data analytics held in memory. Compute optimized favors CPU, accelerated computing adds GPUs, and general purpose offers only a balanced mix.

q: By default, how long does CloudTrail event history in the console let you search recent management events without a trail?
explain: CloudTrail provides 90 days of searchable event history for management events by default. Longer retention requires creating a trail delivering logs to S3.

q: A mobile backend stores each player's profile as flexible JSON-like items looked up by a single player ID, billions of times a day, with no joins between tables. Which database design is this workload textbook-shaped for?
explain: Single-key lookups of self-contained items at massive scale with no joins is the core DynamoDB use case, delivering predictable single-digit millisecond latency. Warehouse scans, graph traversal, and relational joins answer different shapes of questions than this access pattern asks.

q: A CIO wants the fastest possible data-center exit and accepts that optimization will happen after workloads land in AWS. Which strategy should dominate the plan?
explain: Rehosting is the fastest path out because nothing is redesigned during the move; optimization is deferred until after landing. Refactoring first would delay the exit by months.

q: A company wants a managed Microsoft Active Directory in AWS to join EC2 instances to a domain and reuse AD credentials. Which service provides it?
explain: Directory Service offers managed Microsoft AD options for domain joining and directory-aware workloads, and can also connect to an on-premises directory.

q: A security team wants MFA required before a sensitive role can be assumed. Where can that requirement be set?
options: In a security group inbound rule
In the role trust policy using an MFA condition
explain: A Condition on the trust policy, such as aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent, can require MFA at assume time, adding assurance for privileged role sessions.

q: Security Hub standards rely on which service to evaluate many of the underlying configuration checks?
explain: Many Security Hub standard controls are implemented as AWS Config rules, and Security Hub consumes their evaluation results to score the standard.

q: A company's strategy document says one workload will be 'lifted, tinkered with, and shifted' by moving its cache to ElastiCache during migration while the app logic stays put. Which strategy is documented?
explain: The phrase lift-tinker-and-shift is replatform's nickname, and swapping in a managed cache is exactly the kind of tinker it describes. Application logic remaining untouched rules out refactoring.

q: A DNS administrator explains to a junior engineer why the company's domain, registered elsewhere years ago, can still use Route 53 for all its records. Which statement captures how Route 53 hosting works?
options: You create a hosted zone in Route 53 and point the registrar's name servers to it, regardless of where the domain was registered
Each hosted zone must live in a different AWS Region to function
Hosted zones are stored inside an S3 bucket you manage
Route 53 can only host domains that were purchased through Amazon
explain: Hosted zones are portable: create the zone in Route 53, then delegate by updating the NS records at any registrar, and Route 53 becomes authoritative. Registration through Amazon is optional, no customer bucket stores the zone, and DNS is a global service rather than a per-Region construct.

q: A genomics firm submits thousands of containerized analysis jobs each evening; each job runs to completion and the queue drains by morning. Which service is designed to run these jobs efficiently at scale and then release the compute?
explain: AWS Batch dynamically provisions compute for batch jobs, runs them as containers, and releases resources when queues empty, which suits genomics and rendering pipelines. Beanstalk hosts long-running web apps, Lightsail is a simple VPS, and Connect is a contact-center service.

q: A company wants IAM user passwords to require at least 14 characters and to expire every 90 days. What should it configure?
explain: An IAM password policy enforces complexity, length, and rotation rules for IAM user passwords. SCPs are organization guardrails, not password rules; MFA adds a second factor rather than password rules; Access Analyzer flags unintended resource sharing.

q: What is the recommended treatment for the root user access keys?
options: Do not create root access keys and delete them if they exist
Store them in an S3 bucket
Create them and share with admins
explain: Root access keys give unrestricted programmatic control and should not exist. Delete them, protect root with MFA, and use IAM roles and users instead.

q: A cost review asks why the design uses a managed NAT gateway instead of a self-run NAT instance on EC2. Which answer reflects AWS's managed-service advantage here?
options: The NAT instance provides built-in DDoS response team access
The NAT gateway assigns public IPs to every private instance
The NAT gateway is managed by AWS with higher bandwidth and availability, with no instance to patch or scale manually
The NAT instance is free while the NAT gateway is not offered anymore
explain: AWS-managed NAT gateways scale bandwidth automatically, are highly available within an AZ, and need no patching, unlike a NAT instance the team must size, patch, and make highly available itself. NAT never assigns public IPs to the private fleet, and DDoS response teams belong to Shield Advanced.

q: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF), which perspective focuses on aligning IT strategy with business goals and measuring business value?
explain: The Business perspective ensures cloud investments deliver business outcomes and stakeholder alignment. CAF's six perspectives are Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, and Operations.

q: Which customer responsibility applies across EC2, RDS, and S3 alike?
options: Protecting credentials and controlling access to data
explain: Regardless of service, customers always protect their credentials, configure access, and safeguard their data. Hosts, drives, and hypervisors remain AWS duties.

q: An operator accidentally runs a bad update against a production RDS database at 2 p.m. and needs the database restored to its state at 1:45 p.m. that same day. Which RDS capability restores to an arbitrary point in time within the retention window?
options: Taking a manual snapshot after the incident
explain: Automated backups with transaction logs let RDS restore a new instance to any second within the backup retention period (up to 35 days). Read replicas hold current (bad) data, ElastiCache is a cache, and a snapshot taken after the incident captures the corrupted state.

Both the Pricing Calculator (estimate a new architecture) and Cost Explorer (explore what you have already spent) serve cost questions, at different stages. Trusted Advisor and CloudTrail do not perform either role.
q: A customer asks: 'What WILL this new system cost, and what DID we spend last quarter?' Which two tools answer these questions respectively? (Select TWO.)
A company is migrating from on-premises Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime, replicating changes continuously until cutover. Which service performs the migration?
explain: DMS migrates databases — including heterogeneous engines like Oracle to PostgreSQL — with minimal downtime via continuous replication. SCT only converts the schema (a DMS companion); snapshots restore within RDS; Snowball moves files, not live databases.

q: Two policies apply to a user: one allows EC2 actions and another explicitly denies EC2 termination. What happens when the user tries to terminate an instance?
options: Both policies cancel and root is required
The allow wins because it was created first
The explicit deny wins and termination is blocked
explain: An explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides all allows in IAM evaluation. Order of creation does not matter; deny always takes precedence.

q: Which service model gives the customer the LEAST to manage?
explain: With SaaS the provider runs the infrastructure, platform, and application, leaving the customer only usage and configuration. IaaS leaves the most management with the customer.

q: A factory keeps latency-sensitive robot controllers in its plant while sending production quality data to AWS for long-term analytics. Which deployment model fits?
explain: Splitting workloads between on-premises systems and AWS is a hybrid deployment. Multi-Region describes using several AWS Regions, not a mix of premises and cloud.

Activating cost allocation tags lets the tags appear in billing reports, so Cost Explorer and the CUR can break down spend by tag values such as project or cost center. Tags must be activated before they show in reporting.
q: A finance team wants to break down AWS costs by project using metadata attached to resources. Which billing feature makes spend reportable by this metadata?

A hospital system in a large metro area needs imaging workstations to reach AWS compute with noticeably lower latency than the nearest Region, which is several hundred miles away. Which infrastructure option places AWS compute and storage inside major population centers for exactly this gap?
explain: Local Zones extend an AWS Region's compute, storage, and database services into large metros so latency-sensitive applications sit close to end users. Wavelength targets 5G carrier networks, Outposts installs AWS inside your own facility, and Snowball is offline data transfer hardware.

The AWS Partner Network (APN) is the global program for technology and consulting partners whose AWS expertise is validated. Customers use the partner directory to find firms by industry, service, and region.
options: AWS Service Delivery Program listings in Artifact
q: A company wants to find a consulting firm with proven AWS expertise to help design its migration. Which program certifies and lists such third-party firms?
A project migrates a MySQL database from on-premises to RDS for MySQL: the engine stays MySQL on both sides. Which statement about tooling is correct for this homogeneous move?
options: SCT must first rewrite every MySQL query into a new dialect
The database must pass through S3 Glacier before loading
Only Snowball can perform homogeneous migrations
DMS can replicate the data directly; schema conversion between engines is not required
explain: When source and target share an engine, DMS alone handles replication because schemas and SQL dialects already match. SCT exists for heterogeneous moves between different engines, and neither offline shipping nor archive staging is part of a standard online homogeneous migration.

q: An architect must choose between CloudFront and Global Accelerator for a voice-over-IP application whose media streams cannot be cached and must reach the best-performing Region. Which reasoning leads to the right pick?
options: CloudFront, because it caches voice packets at edge locations
Global Accelerator, because it improves the network path for non-cacheable traffic using static anycast IPs and the AWS backbone
CloudFront, because voice requires an S3 origin
Global Accelerator, because it stores copies of media files worldwide
explain: Global Accelerator optimizes the path itself: two anycast IPs route traffic over the AWS backbone to the healthiest endpoint, which suits uncacheable protocols like VoIP. CloudFront's value is caching HTTP content, and Global Accelerator stores no content copies at all.

q: An architect deletes idle EBS volumes and rightsizes over-provisioned EC2 instances. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar does this support?
explain: Eliminating waste and paying only for what you need = Cost Optimization. (Sustainability is about reducing environmental impact — related, but the exam maps waste-reduction-for-the-bill to Cost Optimization.)

q: An architect shortlists AWS Global Accelerator for a worldwide application. Which TWO statements about the service are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: It replaces the need for any load balancer behind it in every design
It provides two static anycast IP addresses as a fixed entry point for applications
It caches web content at edge locations for later viewers
It routes user traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal healthy endpoint
explain: Global Accelerator gives applications a fixed pair of anycast IPs and steers traffic across the AWS backbone to the best healthy endpoint, improving availability and performance for TCP and UDP. Caching is CloudFront's job, and accelerator endpoints are commonly load balancers, which remain very much part of the design.

q: A developer deletes an EC2 instance for a side project but carefully keeps its detached EBS data volume. A week later the developer attaches the volume to a new instance and finds every file intact. Which property of EBS explains this?
options: EBS volumes are automatically converted to S3 objects at termination
EBS volumes persist independently of any single instance's lifecycle
EBS volumes replicate themselves into instance store
EBS volumes encrypt their contents into the AMI registry
explain: EBS is network block storage whose volumes live independently of instances, so data survives instance termination unless delete-on-termination is set for the root volume. Instance store is the ephemeral counterpart; EBS data is not converted to objects or AMIs automatically.

q: After every significant incident, a platform team holds a review, updates its runbook, and automates one manual step it performed during the outage. Which pillar does this habit most support?
explain: Continually improving operations by learning from incidents and refining procedures is Operational Excellence. Reliability concerns the workload recovering from failure, not the team's process improvement loop.

AWS Budgets can alert on actual spend and on forecasted spend, and can also trigger actions (e.g., notifications or applying an IAM policy / stopping instances through Budget Actions) when thresholds are crossed.
options: It can alert on both actual and forecasted spend before the month ends
It lowers the prices of services when limits are near
It prevents any spending above the budget automatically
Because Budgets only reports on historical costs
q: Why might a forecasted-spend alert from AWS Budgets be more useful than waiting for the final bill?
A service automatically creates a KMS key labeled for that service in the account, and AWS handles its rotation. Which key type is this?
explain: AWS managed keys are created by AWS services on the customer behalf and rotated by AWS. The customer can view their use but cannot change their rotation or policies.

q: What is the role of a KMS key policy?
options: It defines TLS versions for browsers
It controls who can use and administer the key, working with IAM policies
It sets the price of encryption
It replaces S3 bucket policies for objects
explain: A key policy is the primary resource policy for a KMS key, defining administrators and users of the key. IAM policies can also delegate access when the key policy allows it.

q: Why do architects deploy a workload across multiple Availability Zones in one Region?
options: To reduce the number of resources the workload needs
To automatically satisfy every country's data laws
To eliminate the need for backups entirely
So the failure of one data center facility does not take the workload offline
explain: AZs are physically separate facilities, so spreading across them protects against a facility-level failure. Backups are still required, and multi-AZ placement grants no legal compliance by itself.

q: A global firm needs a single attestation that its cloud provider information security management system is certified to an international standard. Which program name should its vendor file reference?
options: PCI DSS Level 4 for small merchants
ISO 27001 certification for the provider ISMS
explain: ISO 27001 certifies an information security management system against the international standard, and customers obtain the AWS certificate through Artifact as provider evidence.

q: Instances in a private subnet need to download operating system patches from the internet each night, but the security team insists the instances must remain unreachable from the internet. An architect places a NAT gateway in a public subnet. What does the NAT gateway do for these instances?
options: It encrypts all traffic between the VPC and the internet
It caches patch files at edge locations worldwide
It assigns each private instance a public IP address
It lets them initiate outbound internet connections while blocking unsolicited inbound connections
explain: A NAT gateway performs address translation so private instances can reach out for updates and receive replies, while unsolicited inbound connections have no mapping and are dropped. Instances keep private addresses, traffic is not encrypted by NAT, and caching content is CloudFront's role.

q: Which TWO statements about decoupling with SQS are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: SQS requires producer and consumer to be online simultaneously for every message
Producers and consumers can scale and fail independently because the queue buffers work between them
If the consumer tier goes down, messages wait safely in the queue instead of being lost
SQS delivers each message to every consumer subscribed to a topic
explain: Queues decouple tiers: producers keep producing while consumers are down, messages persist in the queue, and each tier scales on its own schedule. Simultaneous availability is the tight coupling queues eliminate, and delivering to all subscribers describes SNS topics, not queues.

q: A DynamoDB table of device readings uses a sensor ID as its partition key so every lookup names the sensor directly. Which DynamoDB design principle does this reflect for fast, predictable reads?
options: Join readings across many tables at query time
Scan the entire table and filter results in the application
Access data through its primary key for single-digit millisecond lookups
Store readings as ledger entries verified by cryptography
explain: DynamoDB performance comes from key-based access: naming the partition (and sort) key locates items directly without joins or full scans. Scans read everything and are slow at scale, joins are a relational pattern, and cryptographic ledger verification describes QLDB instead.

q: Which service model gives the customer the MOST control over the computing stack?
explain: Of the three classic models, IaaS leaves the most layers with the customer, including operating system and runtime choices. PaaS and SaaS progressively hand more layers to the provider.

q: Which TWO are Security pillar design areas? (Select TWO.)
options: Selecting instance types by benchmark results
Maximizing utilization to cut carbon impact
Data protection in transit and at rest
explain: Identity management and data protection are named Security pillar design areas. Benchmark-driven selection is Performance Efficiency, and utilization for carbon is Sustainability.

q: An online course platform expects enrollment to triple over two years and chooses an architecture whose capacity can grow with that trend. Which property is it planning for?
explain: Designing so capacity can increase as the business grows over time is scalability. Nothing in the stem requires minute-by-minute automatic adjustment, which would be elasticity.

The AWS Pricing Calculator (formerly Simple Monthly Calculator) estimates costs for services and lets customers save and share estimates. It evaluates future designs; Cost Explorer evaluates incurred costs.
q: Which AWS tool replaced the Simple Monthly Calculator for estimating the cost of a planned architecture before deployment?

explain: The Cost and Usage Report is delivered to an S3 bucket you own, making it analyzable with Athena, QuickSight, or third-party BI tools. Cost Explorer itself has no export-to-S3 CUR-style pipeline.
options: It emails the report to the root user weekly
It opens a Support case with the report attached
It delivers the report files to an Amazon S3 bucket
It stores the report in DynamoDB automatically
q: How is the AWS Cost and Usage Report delivered to customers?
An e-commerce firm is layering web protections. Which TWO pairings are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: Macie to block SQL injection at the edge
WAF to block XSS payloads in requests
Shield to mitigate volumetric DDoS floods
explain: WAF handles application-layer payloads like XSS, and Shield handles volumetric DDoS. Macie classifies S3 data and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities; neither does the other jobs.

q: Which property is measured by how well a system continues to operate when individual components fail?
explain: Continued correct operation despite failed components is the definition of fault tolerance. Elasticity and agility measure demand response and delivery speed instead.

The public AWS Service Health Dashboard reports the general status of AWS services by Region. The Personal Health Dashboard is the private, account-specific companion showing events affecting only your resources.
q: A customer wants to verify AWS service health for a region-wide incident affecting many customers, not just their own account. Which resource shows general public status?
A game server is hit by a massive UDP flood saturating its network capacity. Which AWS service is designed to absorb this kind of volumetric attack?
explain: Shield protects against network-layer DDoS (volumetric floods, SYN floods). WAF is a Layer 7 firewall for SQL injection and XSS — it won't stop a UDP flood. Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities; Macie finds sensitive data in S3.

q: Which statement about IAM groups is correct?
options: A group can be nested inside another group
Groups are only for billing organization
A user can belong to multiple groups and inherits all their policies
Groups can be used to log in to the console
explain: Users can be in multiple groups and accumulate permissions from each. Groups cannot be nested, cannot sign in, and exist purely to attach policies to collections of users.

q: A company replaces a nightly all-at-once deployment with small automated changes released many times a day, each easy to undo. Which design principle supports this shift?
options: Automate to make architectural experimentation and change easier
explain: Automation of building, deploying, and testing makes change cheap, safe, and reversible, which the design principles encourage. Manual quarterly bundles make experimentation slower and riskier.

q: A broadcaster configures replication so finished shows stored in Ohio appear automatically in an Oregon bucket minutes later for a regional editing team. Which prerequisite must both buckets satisfy for S3 replication to work?
options: Object Lock must be disabled permanently on the source
Both buckets must be in the same Availability Zone
Both buckets must use the Glacier Deep Archive class
Versioning must be enabled on both the source and destination buckets
explain: S3 replication requires versioning enabled on source and destination buckets so object versions can be tracked and copied. Replication works across Regions and classes, buckets are regional rather than AZ constructs, and Object Lock buckets can in fact be replication sources.

q: An operations group defines dashboards and alarms around customer-visible outcomes and reviews them in a daily stand-up. Which pillar does this observability work serve?
explain: Understanding workload health through telemetry and acting on it operationally is Operational Excellence. Performance Efficiency uses similar data to choose resources, but ownership of day-to-day monitoring is operations.

q: A network ACL contains rule 100 allowing port 80 and rule 50 denying a specific hostile network on all ports. A packet from that hostile network arrives on port 80. Which rule decides its fate, and why?
options: Rule 50, because NACL rules are evaluated in number order and the lowest number wins
Neither rule, because NACLs ignore source addresses
Both rules apply and the packet passes with logging
Rule 100, because allow rules always beat deny rules
explain: NACLs process rules from the lowest number upward and stop at the first match, so the rule-50 deny takes effect before the rule-100 allow is ever considered. Allows do not inherently outrank denies, and source addresses are exactly what NACL rules match on.

q: A startup's API is fronted by API Gateway and suddenly receives ten times normal traffic from one misbehaving client app, threatening the small backend behind it. Which API Gateway control most directly shields the backend from this burst?
options: Throttling limits on the API and per-client usage plans
Adding a second hosted zone in Route 53
Enabling S3 Versioning on the deployment bucket
Switching the backend to a larger NAT gateway
explain: API Gateway throttling caps how many requests reach the backend, and usage plans enforce per-client quotas so one bad client cannot consume the whole API. Versioning, DNS zones, and NAT sizing govern storage, naming, and outbound networking, not inbound API request rates.

q: What should happen to IAM access keys that have not been used in many months?
options: Review and deactivate or delete unused keys
Keep them as a backup forever
Publish them for the team to share
explain: Unused keys are silent attack surface and should be removed after review. The credential report and last-used data help identify keys safe to deactivate.

q: A SaaS vendor offers its service to customers in other VPCs so their traffic reaches it entirely over private IP addresses, never the internet, and the vendor can serve hundreds of customer VPCs without peering to each one. Which technology is the vendor using to publish the service?
options: A public Application Load Balancer with a public DNS name
AWS PrivateLink with an interface endpoint service behind a Network Load Balancer
One VPC peering connection per customer
An S3 bucket policy granting cross-account access
explain: PrivateLink lets a provider expose a service through endpoint services fronted by an NLB, so many consumer VPCs connect privately without peering meshes or public exposure. Peering does not scale to hundreds of consumers, a public ALB contradicts the privacy requirement, and bucket policies govern storage rather than network services.

q: What does AWS Local Zones place near large metropolitan areas?
options: Full new Regions in every suburb
AWS compute and storage services closer to end users for latency-sensitive applications
explain: Local Zones extend select AWS services into metro areas outside a Region's home city, cutting latency for nearby users. They are an extension of a parent Region, not independent Regions.

q: Which service records AWS API calls — who did what, when — for security auditing?
explain: CloudTrail logs API activity (management events) for governance and auditing — 'who called what'. CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs; Config tracks configuration changes; Inspector finds vulnerabilities.

q: A company wants to recover previous versions of S3 objects after accidental overwrites or deletions. Which S3 feature enables this?
explain: Versioning keeps every variant of an object, so you can restore before an overwrite or delete. Lifecycle policies transition or expire objects; replication copies them to another bucket/Region; Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads — none keep prior versions.

q: A project team is sorting duties for an EC2 deployment. Which TWO duties belong to the customer? (Select TWO.)
explain: For EC2 the customer patches the guest OS and configures security groups. The hypervisor and physical data center are security of the cloud and belong to AWS.

q: An application needs an in-memory cache to reduce database load and speed up reads. Which service?
explain: ElastiCache provides managed Redis or Memcached for sub-millisecond in-memory caching. EFS/FSx are file systems; Storage Gateway connects on-premises to cloud storage.

q: What happens when an IAM user is added to a group that has a policy attached?
options: The user inherits the group policy permissions
The group policy replaces the user password
The user becomes the account root
explain: Group membership grants the user every permission in policies attached to that group, in addition to any policies attached directly to the user.

q: A compliance officer wants to disable weak protocols by ensuring every CloudFront distribution uses an ACM certificate with a modern security policy. Which service issues that certificate?
explain: CloudFront uses certificates issued or imported into ACM, where the viewer security policy is selected. KMS and CloudHSM manage keys, not distribution certificates.

q: Which AWS Config feature lets a team require that all EBS volumes be encrypted and see which volumes violate the rule?
options: Config rules with managed rule for encrypted volumes
explain: Config managed rules such as encrypted-volumes evaluate every matching resource and list noncompliant ones, giving continuous conformance visibility.

q: A private internal service needs TLS certificates from a private certificate authority rather than public certificates. Which service can issue private certificates?
options: AWS Certificate Manager with private CA
explain: ACM can work with a private certificate authority to issue private certificates for internal services, in addition to its free public certificates for integrated services.

q: A production workload needs 24/7 phone and chat support with under-1-hour response for urgent issues. Which plan is the minimum fit?
explain: Business ($100/month minimum) provides 24/7 technical support with <1-hour response for production-system-down cases, plus IEM eligibility and the full Trusted Advisor suite. Developer is business-hours email only.

q: Which question would a customer choosing SaaS NOT need to answer?
options: What data will we migrate into the application?
Which operating system patch level will the application servers run?
Which subscription tier includes the reporting feature?
How many user seats does the team need?
explain: Operating system patching belongs to the SaaS provider, so the customer never decides it. Seats, tiers, and data migration are genuine customer concerns when adopting SaaS.

Cost Explorer can be filtered and grouped by member account within an organization, giving per-account views of the consolidated spend while the management account handles payment. SCPs govern permissions, not billing views.
options: AWS Cost Explorer filtered by linked account
q: How can a department see only its own AWS account's costs inside an organization using Consolidated Billing?
Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs and matching supply with demand?
explain: Cost Optimization = pay only for what you need, measure efficiency, stop spending on undifferentiated heavy lifting. The six pillars are Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.

q: A company wants its application to survive the complete loss of one facility while staying in a single geographic area for legal reasons. Which deployment pattern fits?
options: Deploy to one Region per continent regardless of law
Deploy across multiple Availability Zones within one Region
Deploy everything into a single AZ with larger instances
explain: Multiple AZs in one Region give facility-level fault isolation without moving data to another geographic area. A single AZ, however large its instances, remains one failure domain.

q: A media company wants to train deep-learning models on EC2 using hardware acceleration for parallel floating-point work. Which EC2 instance family provides GPUs for this purpose?
explain: Accelerated computing instances include GPUs and other hardware accelerators built for machine learning training, inference, and graphics workloads. The other families optimize CPU, RAM, or local disk, but none provides GPU acceleration.

q: An EC2 instance must call DynamoDB without storing long-term keys on the instance. What should be attached to the instance?
options: An IAM role with an instance profile
An IAM user access key saved in a text file
explain: An IAM role attached via an instance profile delivers temporary credentials automatically and rotates them. Storing long-term keys or root credentials on instances is unsafe.

q: A retailer must show its payment flows meet PCI DSS. Which combination is most relevant?
options: Use Artifact for the AWS PCI attestation and secure its own cardholder environment
Ask AWS to process cards without any customer duties
Rely on Shield Standard alone for PCI compliance
Publish card numbers in a private bucket
explain: The retailer combines the AWS PCI attestation from Artifact with securing its own cardholder data environment, since compliance is shared between platform and workload.

q: Which strategy removes applications from the portfolio entirely because they are no longer useful?
explain: Retire means turning off and removing workloads that deliver no remaining value. Retain also avoids migration, but the workload keeps running and serving a purpose.

q: Which TWO statements correctly contrast security groups and network ACLs? (Select TWO.)
options: Security groups operate at the instance (ENI) level; network ACLs operate at the subnet level
Security groups are stateful; network ACLs are stateless
Security groups support deny rules; network ACLs support only allow rules
Security groups apply to subnets; network ACLs apply to individual instances
explain: The canonical contrast: security groups are stateful and attached to instances/ENIs with allow-only rules, while NACLs are stateless, subnet-level, and support both allow and deny. The middle options invert facts that the exam loves to test directly.

q: A web tier of stateless servers in three Availability Zones all need to read and write the same set of shared configuration files and uploads over NFS. Which storage service provides one file system they can all mount concurrently?
options: Amazon EBS with one volume per server
explain: EFS is a managed NFS file system that many instances across multiple AZs can mount at the same time, growing and shrinking elastically. Separate EBS volumes or instance stores would fragment the shared data, and Deep Archive is object archive storage, not a mountable file system.

q: Before any data moves, a migration team must convert thousands of Oracle PL/SQL procedures and schema objects into PostgreSQL equivalents for Aurora. Which tool analyzes the source and generates the converted target schema?
explain: SCT converts database schemas and code objects between engines, flagging items needing manual work, and pairs with DMS, which then moves the data. DMS alone does not convert code, and CloudWatch and Trusted Advisor monitor and advise rather than convert schemas.

q: Which protects data while it travels between a user and an application over the internet?
explain: TLS encrypts data in transit. S3 versioning protects against overwrite/deletion (at rest, operationally); MFA proves identity; security groups filter network traffic but don't encrypt it.

q: A German insurer must keep policyholder data inside the European Union. Which Region-selection factor dominates its choice?
options: The number of edge locations nearby
explain: Data residency law dictates where data may be stored and processed, making compliance the controlling factor. Latency and price matter only among Regions that already satisfy the legal constraint.

q: After tightening a network ACL, an admin finds that web responses to clients stop arriving even though the inbound rule allows port 443. Knowing NACLs are stateless, what did the admin most likely forget?
options: An outbound rule allowing traffic to the clients' ephemeral ports
A Route 53 record for the subnet
An S3 bucket policy for the web content
A second internet gateway for return packets
explain: Because NACLs are stateless, return traffic must be allowed explicitly, and responses flow to the client's ephemeral ports (typically 1024-65535), so a missing outbound rule silently drops them. Security groups would have handled this automatically; no extra gateway, DNS record, or bucket policy is involved.

q: Legal review shows a claims application must stay on its current mainframe for at least two more years because of an unresolved regulatory question, though everything else migrates. Which strategy applies to that application?
explain: Retain keeps a workload in its source environment, often due to compliance, dependency, or readiness reasons. It may be revisited later; retire would mean switching it off.

q: A gaming backend speaks a custom binary protocol over UDP and needs connection handling at extreme scale with consistent low latency. Which load balancer type is designed for Layer 4 protocols including UDP?
explain: NLB operates at Layer 4 for TCP, UDP, and TLS traffic, sustaining millions of requests per second with ultra-low latency, which suits custom game protocols. ALB only understands HTTP/HTTPS, GWLB inserts third-party appliances, and the Classic generation lacks NLB's performance profile.

q: Heavy read traffic is overwhelming a primary RDS database. Which feature offloads read queries to separate copies?
explain: Read replicas are asynchronous copies that serve read traffic, relieving the primary. Multi-AZ is for failover (the standby takes no reads); autoscaling grows storage, not read capacity.

q: A clinic transmits appointment data between a browser and its AWS-hosted app. Protecting that data while it moves across the network is called what?
explain: Encryption in transit protects data as it travels, typically with TLS. Encryption at rest protects stored data on disk or in object storage.

q: A new CIO wants to know the single biggest economic difference between cloud and a traditional data center in one sentence. Which answer is best?
options: Traditional data centers cannot run modern applications
Cloud converts computing from an upfront owned asset into metered consumption you can turn up, down, or off
Cloud eliminates the need for an IT budget
Cloud bills are identical every month for fairness
explain: The core economic difference is the shift from owning depreciating assets bought in advance to metered consumption that flexes with need. Budgets remain necessary and bills vary with use.

AWS Managed Services (AMS) operates a customer's AWS infrastructure on their behalf — patching, monitoring, backups, and incident management — rather than merely advising, which is what support plans and IQ engagements do.
q: A company wants AWS itself to operate its cloud infrastructure day-to-day following AWS best practices, on an ongoing managed basis. Which offering fits?
A startup CTO asks for the quickest way to know if any EC2 instance is running software with critical vulnerabilities today. Which service answer is most direct?
options: Enable Amazon Inspector and review its findings by severity
explain: Inspector findings rank vulnerable instances, images, and functions by severity, giving an immediate view of critical software exposure across the fleet.

q: A law firm stores documents in S3. Who decides how long documents are retained and when they are deleted?
options: AWS Backup for all data by default
explain: Retention, lifecycle, and deletion of customer data are customer decisions. AWS provides features like Lifecycle policies and Object Lock but does not choose retention.

q: A firm changes its application's data layer from a licensed commercial database to Aurora and splits services apart specifically to gain scalability the old design lacked. Which strategy is this?
explain: Changing engines and decomposing the architecture to gain new capabilities goes beyond tinkering; it is refactoring. Replatform keeps the same engine family and architecture.

q: Which description matches an on-premises deployment, also called a private cloud?
options: All applications run as SaaS products from vendors
Data is cached at edge locations for viewers
Infrastructure runs in the company's own data center using virtualization and resource automation
Workloads are split between a plant and AWS Regions
explain: On-premises or private cloud deployments use cloud-like virtualization inside the company's own facility. SaaS consumption and workload splitting describe different models.

q: Driven by a need for real-time features its monolith cannot deliver, a retailer decomposes the application into event-driven services using Lambda and API Gateway. Which strategy is this?
explain: Rebuilding an application with a new cloud-native architecture to unlock features is refactor / re-architect. It is the highest-effort strategy and is justified by business capability, not speed.

q: AWS serves millions of customers from shared physical infrastructure, dynamically assigning and reassigning resources as demand shifts. Which essential characteristic of cloud computing describes this?
explain: Resource pooling = the provider's resources are pooled to serve many customers (multi-tenant), with resources dynamically assigned. Rapid elasticity is about scaling quickly; on-demand self-service is about provisioning without tickets; broad network access is about device reach.

q: A compliance archive is copied to EBS volumes that are touched maybe twice a year; the team wants the cheapest EBS option and accepts HDD performance for this cold data. Which volume type should the team pick?
explain: sc1 Cold HDD is the lowest-cost EBS type, designed for infrequently accessed, throughput-oriented cold data. The SSD options and st1 all cost more per gigabyte to deliver performance this rarely touched archive does not need.

q: An accessibility team converts a library of written safety manuals into natural-sounding audio in several voices and languages so field workers can listen hands-free. Which service turns text into lifelike speech?
explain: Polly synthesizes speech from text with a range of voices and languages, ideal for audio versions of documents and app narration. Transcribe does the reverse (speech to text), Lex powers conversational bots, and Personalize generates product recommendations, not audio.

q: An engineering firm runs Auto Scaling EC2 fleets. Who ensures the launch template uses a patched AMI?
explain: AMIs and launch templates are customer artifacts. The firm must keep its images patched; Auto Scaling launches what the template specifies, patched or not.

q: Which pillar is about using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand and technologies change?
explain: That sentence defines Performance Efficiency: efficient resource use matched to requirements, sustained over time. Sustainability overlaps on efficiency but centers environmental outcomes.

q: Which situation most strongly justifies keeping a workload on-premises rather than migrating it?
options: A regulation requires the data and processing to remain inside the company's own facility
The team wants to experiment quickly with new features
The workload has unpredictable traffic spikes
The company wants to avoid maintaining hardware
explain: A hard facility-bound regulatory requirement can force an on-premises deployment. Unpredictable traffic, experimentation, and avoiding hardware upkeep are all arguments for cloud, not against it.

q: A hospital group's reporting team needs a HIPAA-friendly analytics store for population-health studies over billions of encounter records, refreshed nightly from the clinical systems. Which service is the analytical half of this architecture?
options: Amazon RDS read replica used as the only store
explain: Population-health analytics over billions of records is warehouse work, and Redshift is the OLAP store built for it, loaded by nightly extracts from transactional systems. A read replica is still an OLTP engine, ElastiCache is a volatile cache, and DocumentDB stores documents rather than running warehouse analytics.

q: Which purchase would be CapEx rather than OpEx?
options: Paying the monthly charge for object storage used
Paying per million API requests in a month
Paying per hour for a virtual server
Buying a storage array for the company's server room
explain: Purchasing physical equipment is a capital outlay. Per-hour, per-gigabyte, and per-request cloud charges are all operating expenses because they buy consumption, not assets.

q: A company exposes a partner-facing API and wants usage plans with per-partner quotas and API keys, throttling to protect the backend, and a managed front door that never requires running servers. Which service assembles all of these controls natively?
explain: API Gateway provides the managed API front door with API keys, usage plans, throttling, caching, and authorization built in, fronting Lambda or other backends without servers to run. A load balancer distributes traffic but offers no usage plans or keys, and DNS or private links do not manage APIs.

q: A migration from SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL involves two different engines. Which pairing of tools covers both halves of this heterogeneous migration?
options: DataSync converts the schema; EventBridge replicates the data
CloudFormation converts the schema; S3 copies the data
Systems Manager converts the schema; Backup replicates the data
SCT converts the schema and code; DMS replicates the data with ongoing change capture
explain: Heterogeneous migrations split the work exactly this way: SCT translates schemas, stored procedures, and code to the target engine, then DMS moves the data and keeps it in sync until cutover. The other pairings assign conversion or replication jobs to tools that do not perform them.
Cost Explorer shows up to the last 12-13 months of cost and usage data with daily or monthly granularity (plus forecasts). The hourly-level raw detail lives in the Cost and Usage Report instead.
q: A team wants to view cost trends for the past year in the console without any setup or exports. Which tool shows historical cost data by default?

A photo service stores originals in S3 Standard but keeps a derived set of resized thumbnails in S3 One Zone-IA. An AZ outage destroys the thumbnails. Why did the design team accept this risk in advance?
options: One Zone-IA data is backed up nightly to Glacier Deep Archive by default
One Zone-IA replicates thumbnails to three Regions automatically
Thumbnails stored there are covered by an availability SLA equal to Standard
Thumbnails are infrequently accessed and can be regenerated from the originals
explain: One Zone-IA stores data in a single AZ at lower cost and is intended for infrequently accessed data that can be recreated, like thumbnails derivable from originals. It has no automatic cross-Region replication or default Glacier backup, and its availability design target is lower than Standard.

q: A news site is overwhelmed by a SYN flood aimed at exhausting connection capacity. Which AWS protection is built for this network-layer attack class?
explain: Shield mitigates volumetric and protocol attacks at Layers 3 and 4 such as SYN floods. WAF works at Layer 7 on HTTP content, not raw connection floods.

q: Who patches the operating system for EC2 instances launched from a customer-built AMI?
options: The customer who built and launches the AMI
AWS, because it hosts the AMI
explain: A customer-built AMI produces customer-managed instances. OS patching after launch belongs to the customer, just like any EC2 guest operating system.

q: A grocery distributor predicts next month's demand for thousands of products from years of sales history to plan warehouse stock, needing time-series forecasts rather than per-user suggestions. Which service is built for demand forecasting?
explain: Forecast applies machine learning to time-series data (sales history, plus related signals like promotions) to predict future demand quantities. Personalize ranks items for individuals, Ground Truth labels training data, and Kendra searches documents; forecasting quantities over time is Forecast's specific job.

q: Which TWO analytics services let a team start analyzing data without provisioning and managing server clusters themselves? (Select TWO.)
options: A self-installed Hadoop cluster on EC2
Amazon EMR with a manually tuned cluster
AWS Glue, which runs serverless ETL jobs
Amazon Athena, which runs serverless SQL over S3
explain: Athena and Glue are serverless: queries and ETL jobs run on AWS-managed capacity with no clusters for the team to size or patch. EMR still involves choosing and managing cluster configurations, and self-installed Hadoop on EC2 is the most management-heavy option listed.

q: Which is an example of a variable expense in AWS?
options: The purchase price of a company-owned SAN
The construction cost of a private data hall
The five-year depreciation schedule of a server
Charges for the gigabytes of data stored this month
explain: Per-gigabyte storage charges vary month to month with consumption, the definition of a variable expense. The other items are fixed capital costs of owned infrastructure.

Dedicated Hosts give visibility into sockets and physical cores and let customers bring eligible existing licenses (such as Windows Server or SQL Server) that are tied to physical hardware, a compliance-driven feature rather than a discount program.
q: A customer must run software whose license terms are bound to physical cores and needs visibility into the underlying server. Which EC2 option should they use?
A video-rendering job needs temporary high-speed scratch space on an EC2 instance. Losing the data when the instance stops is acceptable. Which storage should be used?
explain: Instance store is physically attached, ephemeral storage — blazing fast and free with the instance, but data is lost on stop/terminate. Perfect for temporary scratch. EBS persists (and bills) independently; EFS is shared network storage; S3 is object storage, not a local disk.

q: What is the difference between CloudTrail and AWS Config in one sentence?
options: CloudTrail records who did what, Config records what resources look like over time
Config logs user passwords, CloudTrail logs costs
CloudTrail encrypts data, Config issues certificates
explain: CloudTrail is about actions and actors through API events, while Config is about resource configuration state and how it changes and conforms over time.

q: A monthly AWS bill for compute hours and data transfer is best classified as what type of expense?
explain: Recurring consumption charges paid as you use services are operating expenditure. No asset is purchased or depreciated when you pay for metered cloud usage.

q: Applications in a VPC must call Amazon S3 and DynamoDB without their traffic ever traversing the public internet, even though the applications have internet access for other purposes. Which VPC feature keeps those service calls on the AWS private network?
options: Gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB
A NAT gateway in every subnet
explain: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB add route-table entries that steer traffic to those services over the AWS network at no hourly charge, and they are the only two services with the gateway type. Extra gateways and NAT devices still send traffic outward, and DNS records do not change the network path.

q: Backups sitting in an S3 bucket must be unreadable to anyone who obtains the underlying storage media. Which protection applies?
explain: Encryption at rest renders stored data unreadable without the keys, protecting backups and objects on media. TLS only protects data while it is moving.

q: A company measures the emissions per thousand API calls its platform produces and sets a yearly reduction target for that metric. Which pillar owns this target?
explain: Tracking and reducing environmental impact per unit of work is the Sustainability pillar's core measurement approach. Performance Efficiency tracks speed per resource; sustainability tracks impact per outcome.

q: Which TWO statements describe AWS Lambda accurately? (Select TWO.)
options: Each function needs a dedicated EC2 instance that runs continuously
It requires the customer to patch the underlying operating system
It scales automatically in response to incoming events
A single invocation can run for up to 15 minutes
explain: Lambda is fully serverless: AWS manages the servers and patching, functions scale automatically with event volume, and each invocation is limited to 15 minutes. No EC2 instance is provisioned or kept running by the customer.

q: A team lead wants the one-line summary of Redshift's scaling approach for a design review: how does a warehouse cluster process a huge query faster when more nodes are added?
options: It caches the query result in browser memory
It stores the data once in a single AZ with no distribution
It splits the query across many nodes that work in parallel (massively parallel processing)
It converts the query into Lambda invocations limited to 15 minutes
explain: Redshift uses massively parallel processing: the leader node distributes work across compute nodes that scan their data slices simultaneously. Browser caching, Lambda conversion, and single-location storage describe none of Redshift's architecture and would not speed warehouse queries.

AWS Cost Explorer visualizes historical usage and costs with filters and grouping (service, account, tags) and provides forecasts of future spend. It analyzes the past; the Pricing Calculator estimates hypothetical architectures.
q: A finance manager needs charts of the last six months of AWS spend broken down by service, plus a forecast of next month's costs. Which tool fits?
A gaming company wants to stop credential-stuffing style HTTP floods at the edge of its web API while keeping legitimate players online. Which service inspects and rate-limits the requests?
explain: WAF can apply rate-based rules and bot-focused managed rules at the application layer to throttle abusive HTTP request patterns while allowing normal traffic.

q: Before migrating, a company wants to estimate what its planned architecture will cost per month on AWS. Which tool?
explain: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs for a planned architecture before anything is deployed. Cost Explorer and Budgets work with actual usage; Artifact holds compliance reports.

q: A startup's first architecture uses simple managed services, and the team deliberately leaves room to re-architect hot spots later as traffic data accumulates. Which principle are they honoring?
explain: Starting simple with an explicit expectation of redesign as knowledge grows is evolutionary architecture. The team is planning for change itself, not for a specific failure, coupling, or scaling event.

q: A travel platform decides to require TLS between its app and AWS. Whose design responsibility is that decision?
options: AWS for every account by default
explain: AWS provides TLS endpoints and certificate tooling, but requiring encryption in transit for its application architecture is a customer design decision.

q: A company discovers its workload uses a service that is not HIPAA-eligible for storing patient data. What should it do?
options: Move that data to a HIPAA-eligible service configured under the BAA
Delete the BAA to remove the restriction
Encrypt the data with any key and continue
Keep using it because the account has a BAA
explain: A BAA only covers eligible services, so regulated data must move to an eligible service. Encryption alone does not make a non-eligible service covered.

q: A startup needs EC2 instances that stay running for a month-long data cleansing project and then disappear; the team will create and destroy them repeatedly as scripts run. Which purchasing option matches paying for compute by the second with a 60-second minimum on Linux and no long-term commitment?
options: Spot Instances with a guaranteed runtime
explain: On-Demand Linux billing is per-second with a 60-second minimum and no commitment, suiting short projects that come and go. Reserved Instances require a 1- or 3-year commitment, Dedicated Hosts are about physical servers and licensing, and Spot offers no guaranteed runtime.

q: A public website relies on free, automatic protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks. Which offering provides this by default?
explain: Shield Standard is included at no extra cost and defends against common Layer 3 and Layer 4 DDoS attacks for resources such as CloudFront and load balancers.

q: A Python application must upload receipts to S3 as part of its own checkout logic at runtime. Which AWS tool gives the application native library calls for that integration?
explain: SDKs provide language-native libraries, such as Boto3 for Python, so application code can call S3 and other services directly at runtime. The console is for humans, CloudFormation provisions infrastructure, and Route 53 manages DNS; none embeds API calls inside running code.

q: An IAM role trust policy controls what?
options: Which services the role can call
The price of assuming the role
How long S3 objects are stored
Who or what is allowed to assume the role
explain: A trust policy is attached to a role and lists the principals, such as users, accounts, or AWS services, that are allowed to assume that role.

q: A charity uses S3 static website hosting. A misconfigured bucket policy exposes donation data. Under shared responsibility, fixing that policy is whose job?
explain: Bucket policies are customer configuration, so correcting an overly permissive policy is the charity job. AWS tools can flag it, but ownership stays with the account.

AWS Budgets lets customers set custom cost, usage, reservation, or Savings Plans budgets and get alerts (email/SNS) when actual or forecasted amounts exceed thresholds. Cost Explorer only displays data.
q: Which AWS tool lets a customer set a monthly spending threshold and receive alerts when actual or forecasted costs exceed it?
A manager wants a report of unused IAM roles and users with excessive permissions to clean up. Which IAM feature surfaces unused access information?
options: IAM Access Analyzer and last-accessed information
explain: IAM provides last-accessed data and Access Analyzer unused-access findings that highlight stale users, roles, and permissions so they can be removed under least privilege.

q: A training company sells streaming courses; only paying subscribers may watch the videos, and shared links circulating on forums must stop working. Which CloudFront feature restricts viewing to authorized users with expiring access?
options: Standard caching with a long TTL
Origin access through a second Region
explain: CloudFront signed URLs and signed cookies let you require proof of entitlement and an expiration time before content is served, defeating casually shared links. Making buckets public or lengthening cache lifetimes does the opposite of restricting access, and a second Region adds availability, not authorization.
