q: A tax preparation site knows traffic surges every morning at 9 a.m. and fades by noon, so its Auto Scaling group adds instances on a recurring timetable rather than reacting to metrics. Which scaling approach is being used?
explain: Scheduled scaling changes capacity on a predictable timetable, ideal for known daily or seasonal patterns. Target tracking and step scaling react to metrics or alarms, and manual scaling requires a person to change the desired count.

q: A development shop writes infrastructure in TypeScript because its engineers prefer real programming languages with loops and libraries over raw YAML, yet the resulting deployments still run through CloudFormation. Which tool are they using?
explain: The CDK lets you model infrastructure in languages like TypeScript and Python using constructs, then synthesizes CloudFormation templates for deployment. Beanstalk deploys application code, Lightsail sells simple servers, and CodeCommit hosts Git repositories; none turns code into CloudFormation stacks.

q: Which TWO database scenarios point to a relational database on RDS or Aurora rather than a NoSQL store? (Select TWO.)
options: A leaderboard updated millions of times per hour with single-key reads
An accounting system that must join customers, invoices, and payments with strong transactional consistency
A human-resources system with complex ad hoc queries across many related tables
A product catalog of unrelated JSON items fetched only by ID
explain: Accounting and HR systems rely on joins, relationships, and ACID transactions, the home ground of relational engines on RDS or Aurora. Leaderboards and ID-only catalog lookups are classic NoSQL patterns served better by ElastiCache or DynamoDB.
The AWS Support API is included starting with the Business plan (and higher). Developer and Basic plans do not include programmatic case management through the Support API.
q: A company wants programmatic access to create and manage support cases through the AWS Support API. Which is the minimum Support plan required?

A product team needs to publish a new version of its API, keep the old version live for existing customers, and roll traffic between versions in stages it controls. Which API Gateway concept organizes versions and staged deployments?
explain: API Gateway stages represent named deployment snapshots (such as dev, test, and prod or v1 and v2) that can be served simultaneously and tuned independently. Security groups filter network traffic, hosted zones hold DNS records, and placement groups arrange EC2 instances physically.

q: After a developer deletes the wrong items from a DynamoDB table, the team wants protection that lets it roll the table back to any moment in the previous 35 days. Which DynamoDB feature provides that continuous backup?
explain: Point-in-time recovery continuously backs up a DynamoDB table so it can be restored to any second within the last 35 days. Capacity modes, caching, and scaling govern performance and cost; none of them records the history needed for rollback.

q: A retailer runs its point-of-sale systems in stores but central reporting, backups, and its online storefront on AWS, connected over a private link. Which model is this?
explain: Coexisting store systems and AWS workloads joined by connectivity is the hallmark of hybrid deployment. The retailer plainly has not gone all-in or stayed fully on-premises.

q: A mobile game streams millions of gameplay events per second that must be captured in order per player and processed in real time by several analytics consumers. Which service ingests and stores this high-velocity stream for real-time processing?
explain: Kinesis Data Streams ingests streaming data at massive scale, retaining it in shards so multiple consumers can process the same records in real time. SQS queues discrete messages without stream replay semantics, Glacier is archive storage, and Batch executes scheduled jobs, not continuous streams.

q: A new analyst joins a support team and needs read-only access to S3 for two weeks of training. What is the best way to grant it?
options: Give the analyst the root credentials temporarily
Attach a read-only policy limited in scope and remove it after training
explain: Least privilege means granting only the access needed, for only the time needed. Root sharing, permanent admin rights, and shared keys all violate IAM best practices.

q: Which service scans EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities?
explain: Inspector performs vulnerability assessments (unpatched CVEs, misconfigurations) on EC2, ECR images, and Lambda. GuardDuty detects active threats; Macie finds sensitive data.

q: Which TWO findings would Amazon GuardDuty be expected to produce? (Select TWO.)
options: A list of expiring TLS certificates
A monthly estimate of S3 storage costs
An EC2 instance querying a known crypto-mining domain
Unusual API calls indicating compromised credentials
explain: GuardDuty produces threat findings such as malicious domain activity and anomalous API behavior. Certificate expiry belongs to ACM and cost estimates to billing tools.

q: A two-person software team wants to push a new version of its Java web application and have AWS create the servers, load balancing, and health monitoring automatically. The team does not want to write infrastructure templates. Which service fits this workflow?
explain: Elastic Beanstalk is a platform service: upload the code and it provisions capacity, load balancing, scaling, and monitoring while you keep control of the underlying resources. Lightsail is a simple VPS bundle, Batch runs batch jobs, and manual EC2 leaves everything to the team.

q: A trading firm already runs Apache Kafka producers and consumers and wants the Kafka brokers operated by AWS without re-platforming the streaming applications. Which service is the managed Kafka offering?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for all Kafka clients unchanged
explain: Amazon MSK runs Apache Kafka clusters as a managed service, so existing Kafka APIs and tools keep working. Amazon MQ covers ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ protocols, Kinesis uses its own APIs rather than Kafka's, and EventBridge is an event bus, not a Kafka broker.

q: A company wants its S3 objects encrypted at rest but does not want to manage, rotate, or even see any encryption keys. Which option should it choose?
explain: SSE-S3 encrypts objects with keys fully managed by S3 — zero key management for you. SSE-KMS gives you key control and an audit trail but you manage the keys; SSE-C means you supply the keys yourself; CloudHSM is dedicated hardware where you manage everything.

Reserved Instances reward a 1- or 3-year commitment with up to 72% savings versus On-Demand, making them ideal for steady-state workloads. Spot is cheaper hourly but interruptible, and Savings Plans work on dollars-per-hour commitments.
q: A company runs a database on an EC2 instance continuously for the next 3 years with predictable usage. Which EC2 pricing option gives the lowest cost?
A team wants to test whether a policy accidentally allows deleting a production table. Which tool simulates the request without executing it?
explain: Policy Simulator evaluates sample requests against policies and reports allow or deny without making real calls, ideal for validating sensitive permissions safely.

q: An e-commerce firm is choosing between keeping product images in S3 Standard and moving them to Standard-IA. Traffic data shows each image is viewed dozens of times daily. Which decision follows from the access pattern?
options: Keep the images in S3 Standard because they are accessed frequently
Store them on instance store volumes attached to web servers
Move them to One Zone-IA for the same durability at lower cost
Move them to Deep Archive to cut retrieval fees
explain: Standard-IA and the archive classes charge retrieval fees and are priced for rare access, so frequently viewed images belong in S3 Standard. One Zone-IA also reduces resilience, and instance store data vanishes when instances stop, making both poor homes for popular product imagery.

q: A firm's architect argues for cloud by noting the on-premises alternative needs two full-time infrastructure engineers just to keep hardware running. In TCO terms, those salaries are what?
options: Irrelevant because staff are not hardware
Part of the true cost of the on-premises option that must be counted
A cloud cost that transfers unchanged to AWS
Revenue offsets for the migration business case
explain: Labor to run and maintain facilities is a real ownership cost and belongs in any honest TCO comparison. Ignoring it makes the on-premises option look artificially cheap.

q: A retail chain's innovation team launches three different storefront pilots in one month, keeping the winner and deleting the other two the same day results arrive. Which advantage best fits?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explain: Rapidly creating and removing environments to learn what works is speed and agility. The emphasis is the pace of experimentation, not capacity forecasting or expense classification.

q: After load testing shows a database is the bottleneck, engineers switch its storage to a faster provisioned option and remove an unnecessary application tier. Which pillar's review would praise these changes?
explain: Removing bottlenecks and choosing storage performance matched to measured need is Performance Efficiency. The decisions came from performance measurement and target throughput, not price or recovery.

q: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following is ALWAYS AWS's responsibility?
options: Patching guest operating systems on EC2
Physical security of AWS data centers
explain: AWS is responsible of the cloud: physical facilities, hardware, and the virtualization/networking infrastructure. Customers are responsible in the cloud: their data, access management, OS patching on EC2, and firewall configuration.

q: A company needs a dedicated Technical Account Manager and a 15-minute response for business-critical outages. Which support plan is required?
explain: Enterprise = dedicated TAM + under 15 minutes for business-critical cases. Enterprise On-Ramp offers a pool of TAMs with a 30-minute response. Business tops out at 1 hour for production-down with no TAM.

q: A platform owner is documenting how the team key service behaves for a design review. Which TWO documented behaviors are accurate? (Select TWO.)
options: KMS issues public TLS certificates for websites
KMS key usage is recorded in CloudTrail for auditing
KMS stores and rotates database passwords automatically
Customer managed keys can be disabled by the customer to block decryption
explain: KMS customer managed keys can be disabled by their owner and every KMS API use is logged in CloudTrail. Certificates come from ACM and password rotation from Secrets Manager.

q: A news site sees traffic jump twentyfold when a major story breaks, then fall within the hour. Its infrastructure follows both swings automatically, so costs track the audience. Which property matters most here?
explain: Rapid, short-lived demand swings in both directions are exactly what elasticity handles. Long-term growth planning would be scalability; this pattern is about minutes, not years.

q: Rather than one large server doing every job, an architect runs many small workers in parallel so a big image batch finishes in minutes. Which classic cloud design principle is applied?
options: Think parallel and distribute the work
Keep work on a single instance
explain: Parallelism - splitting work across many resources that run simultaneously - is a core cloud design principle enabled by on-demand capacity. Serial single-instance processing wastes that capability.

q: A company runs a public website tier and a private data tier in one VPC. Which layout matches the standard two-tier pattern the exam expects?
options: Databases in public subnets; web servers in private subnets
Web servers in public subnets behind the internet gateway; databases in private subnets with no direct internet route
Both tiers in one subnet in a single Availability Zone
Both tiers in public subnets for simplicity
explain: The canonical design puts internet-facing resources in public subnets (route to the internet gateway) and sensitive resources in private subnets reachable only from inside the VPC. Reversing the tiers or collapsing everything into one public subnet discards the isolation the pattern exists to provide.

q: Application servers write log files that the team wants searchable in one central place, with alerts when the word ERROR appears more than a set number of times. Which CloudWatch component collects and monitors log data this way?
explain: CloudWatch Logs centralizes log streams from applications and services, and metric filters turn log patterns (like ERROR counts) into metrics that alarms can watch. Billing alarms track spend, CloudTrail logs API calls rather than application output, and Config records resource configurations.

q: A team is hardening IAM for production. Which TWO controls should it apply? (Select TWO.)
options: Give every service full access to simplify debugging
Remove unused users, roles, and credentials
Require MFA for privileged console sign-ins
explain: Requiring MFA for privileged access and removing unused identities shrink the attack surface. Blanket full access and disabling logging do the opposite.

q: A healthcare company runs a patient portal on AWS. Who is responsible for ensuring the application itself is configured to meet HIPAA requirements?
options: Responsibility transfers to AWS once BAA paperwork is signed
AWS, because it offers HIPAA-eligible services
explain: AWS provides HIPAA-eligible services and compliance reports (via Artifact), but how you configure and use them — your application's compliance — is always the customer's job. "HIPAA-eligible" means the service can be used in a compliant architecture, not that AWS makes your app compliant.

q: A company must retain compliance archives for 7 years at the lowest possible cost and can wait hours for retrieval. Which S3 storage class?
explain: Glacier Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 class, built for long-term archival with retrieval in hours. Standard-IA and Intelligent-Tiering cost more per GB; Standard is for hot data.

q: A large enterprise wants employees to self-serve only pre-approved, compliant stacks (a standard web app pattern, a standard data pipeline) from an internal catalog, never free-form infrastructure. Which service publishes these governed portfolios of products?
options: Amazon S3 with a folder of templates
explain: Service Catalog lets administrators curate portfolios of approved products with constraints, so users launch compliant, standardized stacks on demand. A folder of raw templates has no governance or launch controls, Marketplace sells third-party software, and DNS zones play no provisioning role.

q: Which TWO are advantages of cloud computing? (Select TWO.)
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Own and operate physical data centers in every market
Predict capacity needs years in advance
explain: Going global in minutes and massive economies of scale are core AWS-stated advantages. Owning data centers, predicting capacity years out, and heavy lifting are exactly what the cloud lets you stop doing.

q: A team moves its application to AWS and, during the move, swaps its self-managed database for Amazon RDS and its file storage for EFS, but rewrites no application features. Which strategy is this?
explain: Making a few cloud optimizations during migration without changing core architecture is replatform, or lift-tinker-and-shift. No rewrite occurred, so it is not refactoring.

q: Before pushing a new IAM policy to production, an admin wants to preview its effect on a user. Which tool previews policy behavior?
explain: The IAM Policy Simulator tests how a policy would evaluate for a user, group, or role against selected actions, helping catch errors before production use.

q: A company creates a CloudTrail trail delivering to S3. What is the main governance benefit over console event history alone?
options: Automatic blocking of unwanted API calls
Long-term, retained audit logs under the company control for investigations and compliance
explain: A trail persists API activity logs to an S3 bucket the company controls, enabling long retention, analysis, and evidence beyond the default 90-day history window.

q: Which TWO are essential characteristics of cloud computing? (Select TWO.)
explain: The NIST five characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service (pay for what you use, with usage metering). Manual procurement and fixed capacity are the on-premises world.

q: An HR department drops its self-hosted personnel system and subscribes to a commercial HR SaaS product, importing employee records into it. Which strategy is this?
explain: Abandoning the old system for a different, usually SaaS, product is repurchase. The workload is replaced by a purchase, not migrated or decommissioned outright.

q: A machine-learning team chooses GPU instances for model training and Graviton-based instances for its web tier so each workload gets the most work done per unit of compute. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar guides these choices?
explain: Performance Efficiency = using computing resources efficiently by selecting the right resource types for each workload. Cost Optimization is about minimizing spend (related, but the question is about efficient resource use, not the bill). Sustainability targets environmental impact; Operational Excellence targets operations and process improvement.

q: A hospital group wants to run AWS infrastructure inside its own facility because certain systems cannot leave the building, while using the same AWS services and tools. Which offering fits?
explain: Outposts delivers AWS-designed infrastructure into a customer's own premises, managed consistently with the cloud. CloudFront and Route 53 are global services, and Local Zones are AWS-owned metro sites.

q: An airline's CIO notes the company no longer budgets for uninterruptible power supplies, fire suppression systems, or data-center floor space. Which advantage has the airline realized?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explain: Power, suppression, and floor space are data-center operating costs that disappear when AWS runs the facilities. That is precisely the stop-spending-money-running-data-centers advantage.

q: A platform group wants every new AWS account vended with baseline logging, password policies, and network defaults already applied, then governed continuously with guardrails that detect drift from company policy. Which service is purpose-built to orchestrate this landing zone lifecycle?
explain: Control Tower's account factory vends standardized accounts and its guardrails (built on Organizations, Config, and related services) continuously enforce the landing zone's baselines. CloudFormation deploys stacks but does not govern accounts, GuardDuty detects threats, and Artifact supplies compliance paperwork.

q: A manufacturer wants to retire its physical tape library while keeping the same backup software and its virtual tape workflow, sending backup data to AWS instead. Which Storage Gateway type presents itself as a virtual tape library?
explain: Tape Gateway emulates a physical tape library (a virtual tape library) so existing backup applications keep working while tapes are stored in S3 and archived to Glacier. File and Volume Gateways expose file and block interfaces respectively, not tape semantics.

q: A hosting customer installs its own database engine on rented virtual machines and tunes the storage volumes itself. Which model is in use?
explain: Installing and tuning your own database on rented VMs is IaaS usage - the provider supplies compute and storage, you build the stack. A managed database service would shift more of that work to AWS.

q: Which option best describes AWS Wavelength?
options: It is a pricing plan for long-running instances
It is a satellite internet service for ships at sea
It embeds AWS infrastructure inside telecommunications providers' 5G networks for ultra-low-latency mobile applications
It lengthens the distance between Availability Zones
explain: Wavelength zones sit inside carriers' 5G networks so mobile and edge applications reach AWS resources with minimal hops. It concerns network placement, not pricing or satellites.

q: A retailer wants vulnerability findings for Lambda functions it deploys, in addition to EC2 scanning. Which service covers Lambda vulnerability scanning?
explain: Inspector coverage includes EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions, scanning their dependencies for known vulnerabilities.

q: Who creates and manages IAM users for a consulting firm AWS account?
explain: Identity and access management for an account belongs to the customer. AWS provides IAM as the tool, but the firm decides who gets access and at what level.

q: Why should access keys never be committed to a public code repository?
options: Exposed keys can be harvested within minutes and used to consume or compromise the account
explain: Publicly exposed keys are rapidly discovered by scanners and abused for resource theft and data access. They must be revoked immediately and replaced with roles.

q: When a new user signs up, three independent things must happen: a welcome email is sent, a record is written to the CRM, and a fraud-check job starts, all triggered by the same event without the signup code calling each system. Which pattern and service deliver this fan-out?
options: Amazon SQS queue polled by a single consumer
Amazon RDS triggers inside the user table
AWS Step Functions state machine with one step
Amazon SNS topic publishing one message to multiple subscribers
explain: SNS fan-out publishes one event to many subscribers (email endpoint, Lambda for the CRM, an SQS queue for fraud checks) simultaneously. A single SQS queue delivers each message to one consumer, Step Functions orchestrate sequential workflows, and database triggers do not fan out to external systems this way.

q: Why does envelope encryption improve performance for large files?
options: Data keys encrypt data locally so large payloads are not sent through the KMS API
KMS stores a copy of every file
explain: Only the small data key goes through KMS, while bulk data is encrypted locally with fast symmetric encryption, avoiding API limits and network transfer of large files.

q: A streaming service facing advanced, large-scale DDoS campaigns wants enhanced detection, 24/7 response experts, and protection against attack-driven bill spikes. Which plan fits?
explain: Shield Advanced adds enhanced detection, the DDoS Response Team around the clock, and cost protection for scaling charges caused by confirmed attacks.

q: A company moves its applications to AWS with almost no code changes, using a "lift and shift" approach. Which migration strategy is this?
explain: Rehost = lift and shift with minimal changes — the fastest migration path. Replatform makes small optimizations ('lift, tinker, and shift'), repurchase moves to a different product (often SaaS), and refactor/re-architect rebuilds for the cloud.

q: A fast-growing analytics product built on Aurora finds storage expanding on its own as data pours in, with no volume resizing tasks for the team. Which Aurora characteristic explains the hands-off growth?
options: Aurora requires a new cluster for every additional terabyte
Aurora stores all data on instance store volumes
Aurora caps every cluster at exactly 1 TB
Aurora storage automatically grows in increments up to 128 TB as needed
explain: Aurora's distributed storage layer grows automatically in 10 GB increments up to 128 TB and replicates data across three AZs, removing manual volume management. It does not need new clusters per terabyte, does not use ephemeral instance store, and is not capped at 1 TB.

q: A video analytics team benchmarks several instance families, picks the one that processes the most frames per core, and revisits the choice quarterly as new types launch. Which pillar is it practicing?
explain: Selecting the resource type that does the most work for the workload, and re-evaluating as options evolve, is Performance Efficiency. The metric is work per unit of compute, not dollars saved.

q: A nightly job takes about 45 minutes to transform video files, and an engineer suggests running it as a single Lambda function. Why will that approach fail?
options: Lambda cannot read files from Amazon S3
Lambda functions stop after a maximum run time of 15 minutes
Lambda only supports one programming language
Lambda charges a flat monthly fee that makes it too expensive
explain: Every Lambda invocation is capped at 15 minutes, so a 45-minute job will be terminated; a container or EC2-based service fits instead. Lambda reads S3 natively, bills per request and duration, and supports many runtimes.

q: Which advantage describes shifting effort away from racking servers, replacing failed drives, and maintaining power and cooling systems?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explain: AWS absorbs the undifferentiated heavy lifting of facility and hardware upkeep, which is the stop-spending-on-data-centers advantage. The stem lists physical maintenance tasks, not speed, geography, or unit pricing.

q: Six months after launch, an auditor wants the full history of how one particular security group changed over time: every rule edit, with the configuration as it existed on each date. Which service keeps this configuration history?
explain: AWS Config continuously records resource configurations and presents a timeline of changes for each supported resource, exactly the history requested. CloudTrail complements it with the API-call view of who made changes, but the configuration snapshots themselves are Config's record.

q: To stop a single overloaded queue from cascading failures through its order pipeline, a team adds backoff, queues, and limits on request rates. Which pillar is it strengthening?
explain: Managing failure isolation and graceful degradation so one stressed component cannot topple the whole system is Reliability work. The techniques protect correct operation under stress.

q: A company wants to be alerted when a bucket policy accidentally grants an external AWS account access to an S3 bucket. Which service identifies this unintended sharing?
explain: Access Analyzer analyzes resource policies and flags access granted outside the account (or zone of trust). GuardDuty detects threats like compromised credentials; Macie discovers PII in S3; Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities — none evaluate who your policies share with.

q: A company has just created its first AWS account. What should it do FIRST to secure the account?
options: Enable MFA on the root user and create an admin via IAM Identity Center
explain: The root user can't be deleted — lock it down with MFA, don't use it daily, and administer through an IAM Identity Center admin instead. Disabling CloudTrail would destroy your audit trail.

q: A resource policy grants a different AWS account access to a KMS key. The owning team wants a finding for any such external grant. Which service generates it?
explain: Access Analyzer evaluates KMS key policies and other resource policies and creates findings when a resource is shared with an external principal.

q: A photo-sharing startup pays almost nothing for Lambda during quiet overnight hours, then pays only for the milliseconds its functions run during daytime peaks. Which Lambda billing characteristic explains this?
options: A reserved capacity charge applies around the clock
A per-instance hourly fee applies like Amazon EC2
Charges accrue per request and per duration of execution, with no charge when idle
A minimum one-year commitment is billed monthly
explain: Lambda is billed per request plus the duration functions actually run, measured in milliseconds, and idle functions cost nothing. There is no hourly instance fee, no reservation requirement, and no capacity charge for simply existing.

q: A CFO asks why the cloud bill changes every month while the old hardware budget was flat. What is the best explanation?
options: Cloud charges follow actual consumption, so the bill varies with usage
AWS adds random surcharges to monthly bills
Variable billing means charges are unpredictable and unmeasurable
The flat hardware budget also changed monthly
explain: Variable expense means the amount tracks measured usage, rising with consumption and falling when usage drops. It is variable but fully metered and visible, not random.

q: Which pairing is correct?
options: Elasticity - surviving component failure; Agility - uptime percentage
Elasticity - resources automatically track demand; Agility - speed of experimenting and delivering change
Elasticity - adding one bigger server; Agility - caching content at the edge
Elasticity - owning spare hardware; Agility - signing longer contracts
explain: Elasticity is demand-tracking capacity, and agility is organizational speed of change. The distractors attach failure, uptime, and ownership meanings that belong to other concepts.

AWS Savings Plans apply a committed $/hour of compute usage across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda for 1 or 3 years in exchange for lower prices. Reserved Instances commit to specific instance configurations in a Region instead.
q: Which pricing model commits to a consistent amount of compute usage (measured in $/hour) for 1 or 3 years across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda in exchange for lower prices?

explain: Data transfer INTO AWS (ingress) from the internet is free. Charges generally apply to data transferred out to the internet, between Regions, and in some inter-AZ cases, depending on the service.
options: Data transferred out of AWS to the internet
Data transferred out of Amazon S3 to CloudFront in another continent
Data transferred into AWS from the internet
q: Which data transfer is FREE of charge on AWS?

A team defines its entire application stack (network, load balancer, instances, and database) in one YAML file and creates or destroys the whole stack with a single action, identically every time. Which service is executing that template?
explain: CloudFormation treats a template as a stack blueprint, provisioning and tearing down all defined resources together in the right order, reproducibly. Systems Manager operates running resources, CloudWatch observes them, and Service Catalog curates approved products rather than executing arbitrary templates.

q: In the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework, executives define the migration's target business outcomes and the investment case for cloud adoption. Which perspective are they working in?
explain: The Business perspective covers strategy, business outcomes, and the financial case for adoption. People, Governance, and Platform perspectives handle workforce, oversight, and architecture respectively.

q: A firm copies its virtual machines into EC2 exactly as they are, with the same operating systems and application versions, planning improvements later. Which strategy is this?
explain: Moving workloads unchanged, lift-and-shift, is rehosting. Any optimization would move it toward replatform, and relocation is a hypervisor-level move to VMware Cloud on AWS.

q: Which tool visualizes historical AWS spending patterns and forecasts future costs?
explain: Cost Explorer graphs and analyzes past spend with forecasting. Budgets alerts on thresholds; the Pricing Calculator estimates before you deploy; Trusted Advisor gives optimization recommendations.

q: A solutions architect explains the physical makeup of a single Availability Zone to a new hire. Which description should she give?
options: A single server dedicated to one customer
A set of edge locations in one country
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within a Region
explain: An AZ is one or more physical data centers engineered as an isolated failure domain inside a Region. Regions, not AZs, are the larger geographic grouping.

q: A steering group sets up how cloud risks will be reviewed, how benefits will be tracked against the business case, and which policies govern account use across the portfolio. Which CAF perspective is this?
explain: Governance perspective work includes risk management, benefit realization, and portfolio-level oversight of cloud initiatives. It coordinates how adoption is directed and controlled.

q: A freelance designer wants to host a portfolio site and a WordPress blog for a flat, predictable monthly price that bundles a virtual server, storage, and data transfer. Which service is marketed for exactly this simplicity?
explain: Lightsail bundles a virtual private server, SSD storage, and data transfer into one low, predictable monthly price aimed at simple projects. EKS runs Kubernetes, Beanstalk deploys custom code platforms, and EMR processes big data.

q: A policy allows s3:GetObject on one bucket only. A user requests GetObject on a different bucket with no other policies. What is the result?
options: Denied by implicit deny since no policy allows that resource
explain: IAM starts with an implicit deny: if no applicable policy allows an action on a resource, the request is denied even when a similar action is allowed elsewhere.

q: An application needs ultra-low-latency Layer 4 load balancing with static IP addresses. Which load balancer?
explain: NLB handles millions of requests per second at Layer 4 with ultra-low latency and provides static IPs/Elastic IPs per AZ. ALB is Layer 7; WAF is a web firewall, not a load balancer.

q: What does AWS Audit Manager primarily help a company do?
options: Continuously collect evidence mapped to compliance frameworks for audits
explain: Audit Manager automates evidence collection from AWS usage and maps it to frameworks and standards, producing audit-ready reports with less manual sampling work.

q: A company will run a database server on EC2 24/7 for the next three years. Usage is fully predictable. Which pricing model gives the LOWEST cost?
explain: A 1- or 3-year commitment earns up to 72% off On-Demand — ideal for steady, predictable workloads. Spot is cheaper per hour but can be interrupted (terrible for a database). On-Demand has no discount; Dedicated Hosts serve compliance/licensing needs, not cost savings.

q: A small web app runs on burstable EC2 instances that idle at low CPU overnight and burst to full CPU during business hours, earning credits while idle to spend during bursts. Which instance concept describes this credit-based burst model?
options: Burstable performance instances with CPU credits
explain: Burstable instances (the T family) accumulate CPU credits during low utilization and spend them to burst above baseline, matching spiky small workloads economically. The other options concern storage performance, instance placement, or capacity reservations rather than CPU credit economics.

q: A platform team has standardized on Kubernetes manifests and kubectl across all its projects and now wants the Kubernetes control plane operated by AWS. Which service should the team choose?
explain: Amazon EKS is the managed Kubernetes service, so existing manifests, tooling, and skills carry over while AWS runs the control plane. ECS is AWS's own orchestrator without the Kubernetes API, Fargate is a launch type rather than an orchestrator, and Lightsail is a simple VPS offering.

q: A startup wants to add a customer-support assistant powered by large language models, choosing among several foundation models through one managed API, without hosting or training the models itself. Which service provides fully managed access to foundation models for generative AI?
explain: Bedrock offers a single API to foundation models from multiple providers, fully managed, with tools for customization on your data and guardrails, so teams build generative AI apps without running model infrastructure. Lex and Comprehend are single-purpose AI services, and notebook tooling is not the managed model-access layer described.

q: An organization wants a guardrail so no member account can disable CloudTrail, even account administrators. Which mechanism can enforce that ceiling?
options: A service control policy denying the action
explain: An SCP can deny actions such as stopping CloudTrail across member accounts, and not even account administrators can exceed an SCP deny in their own account.

q: An insurance carrier keeps claim photos that adjusters open only a few times each quarter, but when a claim is reopened the photos must appear instantly, with no restore wait. Which S3 storage class fits both constraints?
options: S3 Standard-IA only with expedited retrieval jobs
explain: Glacier Instant Retrieval archives data at low cost while keeping millisecond access for quarterly-use data such as images and medical records. Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive require restore operations measured in minutes to hours before objects can be read.

q: A factory's sensor data cannot leave the building for regulatory reasons, but the team wants to use AWS services and APIs locally. Which service puts AWS infrastructure inside their own facility?
explain: Outposts = AWS-designed racks installed in your data center, running AWS services on-premises. Local Zones are AWS's own metro-area extensions (not in your building); Direct Connect is just a network link; Storage Gateway is hybrid storage, not compute.

q: A company wants every IAM user to enter a code from their phone in addition to their password when signing in to the console. What should it enable?
explain: MFA adds a second factor (something you have, like a phone code) on top of the password. A password policy strengthens the first factor but doesn't add a second one; access keys are for programmatic access; roles provide temporary credentials, not a second factor.

q: Which tool would a governance lead use to prove which S3 buckets were noncompliant last month and how they changed?
options: AWS Config with its configuration timeline and rules
explain: AWS Config records resource configurations over time and evaluates rules, so it can show a bucket compliance state and change history for a past period.

q: Two project summaries land on a review desk for classification. Which TWO describe hybrid deployments? (Select TWO.)
options: A firm decommissions an unused internal application
A bank keeps card processing in its data center while running its mobile app on AWS
A startup runs its entire product on AWS with no premises systems
A factory runs plant-floor systems locally and sends quality analytics to AWS
explain: Both correct scenarios split live workloads between premises systems and AWS, which defines hybrid deployment. Running everything on AWS is all-in cloud, and decommissioning is not a deployment model.

q: Which AWS service is designed specifically to manage WAF, Shield Advanced, and Network Firewall protections across an organization from one policy?
explain: Firewall Manager is the central firewall administration service for an organization, distinct from Security Hub which aggregates findings rather than administering rules.

q: A logistics firm picks a Region by weighing four candidate Regions against where its warehouses and drivers are, the local data laws, and monthly pricing differences. According to AWS guidance, which set names the recognized factors in that decision?
options: The number of letters in each Region code and its launch date
Latency to users, compliance and data residency, cost, and service availability in the Region
Whether the Region's name appears first alphabetically
Only the Region's distance from AWS headquarters
explain: The documented Region-selection factors are proximity/latency, compliance with data laws, cost differences between Regions, and whether the services you need are offered there. Headquarters distance, naming trivia, and launch dates play no part in the framework the exam expects.

q: A data lead contrasts Athena and EMR for a one-off investigation: the team needs answers from S3 files today without standing up or tuning any cluster. Which reasoning correctly favors Athena here?
options: EMR is serverless and Athena requires a cluster
Athena is serverless and queries S3 in place, while EMR means provisioning and managing a cluster
EMR queries run with no infrastructure behind them at all
Athena can only query data stored inside Redshift
explain: Athena's serverless model suits immediate, occasional queries over S3 data; EMR's power comes with cluster provisioning and tuning responsibilities the one-off task does not justify. The remaining options swap the two services' models or invent storage restrictions that do not exist.

q: Which service uses machine learning and threat intelligence to detect compromised EC2 instances and unusual API activity?
explain: GuardDuty = intelligent threat detection ("am I being attacked?"). Inspector = vulnerability scanning ("am I vulnerable?"). Macie finds PII in S3. Artifact provides compliance reports.

q: A disaster recovery plan calls for the application to survive the complete loss of one data center while staying within a single Region and budget. Which design element delivers that survival?
options: Registering extra DNS names for the same server
Using a single large EC2 instance with an attached EBS volume
Running the application across multiple Availability Zones in the Region
Storing backups in S3 Glacier Deep Archive only
explain: Availability Zones are physically separate data centers within a Region, so a multi-AZ deployment keeps running when one facility fails, without the cost of a second Region. Backups alone require a rebuild, a single instance is a single point of failure, and extra DNS names cannot resurrect a lost server.

q: A company with 30 AWS accounts wants employees to sign in once and receive appropriate access in each account, without managing 30 separate sets of credentials. Which service provides this?
options: IAM users created separately in each account
explain: IAM Identity Center (successor to SSO) gives the workforce single sign-on across multiple accounts and applications. AWS Organizations manages the accounts themselves, not sign-in; Cognito is for customer-facing app authentication; per-account IAM users would multiply credentials.

q: A manufacturer must keep production data inside its factory for local regulations, yet wants to run its analytics with the same AWS APIs and services its cloud team uses everywhere else. Which offering installs fully managed AWS infrastructure physically inside the factory?
explain: Outposts delivers AWS-designed racks, installed and managed by AWS, into your own facility so workloads run on-premises with cloud-consistent APIs and services. Local Zones sit in AWS-operated metro sites, Wavelength lives inside carrier 5G networks, and CloudFront only caches content at edge points.

q: Data from actual usage shows customers mostly browse on mobile in the evening, so a team reshapes its architecture and scaling schedule around those observed patterns. Which principle is this?
options: Assume the first design is final
explain: Well-Architected guidance says to gather data on how choices affect workloads and let evidence drive design. Guessing or copying without measurement abandons that principle.

q: A logistics company receives shipment manifests from hundreds of carriers through managed file transfer protocols, and compliance requires the files in S3 with user-level access control per carrier. Which service should the architects select?
explain: Transfer Family supports per-user authentication and directory controls for SFTP and related protocols depositing files into S3, matching the carrier-by-carrier access requirement. Snowball is offline bulk transfer, Batch Operations runs jobs on existing objects, and Backup manages recovery points.

q: Which description of how Regions relate to each other is accurate?
options: Deleting a Region removes customer data worldwide
A Region shares its Availability Zones with neighboring Regions
Each Region is completely independent and isolated from the others, and data does not move between Regions unless you configure it
Resources replicate automatically to every Region for safety
explain: Regions are isolated by design; cross-Region movement happens only through services or replication the customer configures. Nothing about a Region automatically copies data elsewhere.

q: A team needs short-lived database access for a reporting job and wants credentials fetched at runtime rather than baked into an image. Which service should the job call?
explain: Fetching secrets from Secrets Manager at runtime with an IAM-scoped role avoids baking credentials into images and lets rotation happen without redeploying.

q: A global SaaS provider hosts identical application stacks in Ohio, Ireland, and Singapore and wants each customer directed to whichever stack answers fastest from the customer's location. Which Route 53 routing policy automates that choice?
explain: Latency-based routing uses measurements of latency between users and AWS Regions to return the record for the Region expected to respond fastest. Weighted splits by fixed percentages, failover switches only on failure, and multivalue returns several healthy records without latency logic.

q: Which statement about AWS Shield Standard is correct?
options: It blocks SQL injection in HTTP requests
It includes a dedicated response engineer for every attack
It is automatically included and protects against common infrastructure layer attacks
It requires a monthly subscription per resource
explain: Shield Standard is automatic and free, covering common Layer 3 and 4 attacks. The response team and advanced features belong to Shield Advanced; SQLi blocking is WAF.

q: Which TWO services help with governance and compliance auditing? (Select TWO.)
explain: CloudTrail answers 'who changed what and when' (audit trail); Config answers 'is everything configured compliantly right now' (compliance state). CloudFront, SQS, and SNS are delivery/messaging services.

q: A telecom carrier is building augmented-reality features that run on its 5G network and need single-digit millisecond latency for phones connected to that network. Which AWS infrastructure embeds compute inside the carrier's 5G network itself?
explain: Wavelength embeds AWS compute and storage at the edge of communications providers' 5G networks, so mobile applications reach servers without traffic crossing the public internet. Local Zones serve metro areas generally, CloudFront caches content, and Direct Connect links facilities with private circuits.

q: Which TWO factors should a company weigh when selecting an AWS Region for a new workload? (Select TWO.)
options: The favorite color scheme of the local data center
Latency between the Region and the workload's users
Compliance rules governing where the data may reside
Whether the Region's name is easy to pronounce
explain: Latency and compliance are two of the four recognized Region-selection factors, alongside cost and service availability. Cosmetic properties of a Region play no role in the decision.

q: An online bookstore wants 'readers also enjoyed' suggestions tailored to each visitor's own history, like the recommendation engines of large retailers, without hiring an ML team. Which service generates these individualized recommendations?
explain: Personalize builds real-time, per-user recommendation models from your interaction data using the same technology lineage as Amazon.com's suggestions. Forecast predicts aggregate quantities over time, Comprehend reads text, and Rekognition reads images; none personalizes item suggestions per user.

q: An order service publishes completed orders to a queue so the billing service can process them at its own pace, and a billing outage never blocks checkout. Which design principle is demonstrated?
explain: Placing a queue between producers and consumers decouples them, so each scales and fails independently. Tight coupling would make a billing outage break checkout directly.

q: A security engineer wants to explicitly block all traffic from one abusive IP address range at the boundary of an entire subnet, something security groups cannot do. Which VPC control supports explicit deny rules?
explain: Network ACLs support both allow and deny rules evaluated at the subnet level, so an abusive source can be explicitly blocked. Security groups are allow-only, route tables steer packets rather than filter them, and DHCP options configure instance networking settings like DNS servers.

q: Which service runs code in response to events without provisioning servers, billing only per execution?
explain: Lambda is serverless: upload code, trigger it via events (S3 uploads, API calls, schedules), pay per request and compute time. Functions can run up to 15 minutes per invocation.

AWS Marketplace is the curated digital catalog for third-party software that runs on or with AWS; purchases appear on the customer's AWS bill. Service Catalog is for an organization's own approved internal products.
q: Where do AWS customers buy and deploy third-party software (for example, a vendor's firewall appliance or SaaS product) with billing consolidated onto their AWS bill?
A company wants one place to define permission sets once and assign them to workforce users across many accounts. Which service provides permission sets?
explain: IAM Identity Center uses permission sets, which are policy templates assigned to users and groups for specific accounts, simplifying multi-account workforce access.

q: A systems team must apply operating-system patches to 800 EC2 instances across accounts on a schedule, with compliance reporting on which instances are patched and which are not. Which service is the operational hub built for this fleet-wide patching?
explain: Systems Manager provides Patch Manager and fleet-wide operational tools (run commands, automation, inventory, compliance views) across instances and accounts. CloudWatch observes performance, Config records configuration history, and Inspector reports vulnerabilities; none orchestrates patching at fleet scale.

Standard RIs can be modified in limited ways — Availability Zone, instance size within the same family, networking type, and scope. Changing the instance family requires a Convertible RI (exchange) instead.
options: The Availability Zone within the same Region
The AWS Region of the reservation
q: Which change CAN be made to a Standard Reserved Instance after purchase?

An operations team configures an Auto Scaling group to hold average CPU utilization near 50 percent across the fleet, letting AWS add or remove instances automatically. Which scaling policy type is this?
explain: A target tracking policy behaves like a thermostat: it adjusts capacity to keep a chosen metric, such as average CPU, at the target value. Scheduled scaling follows a clock, not a metric, and the other two options are not Auto Scaling policy types.

q: What is an IAM role best described as?
options: An identity with permissions that can be assumed temporarily
explain: An IAM role is an identity whose permissions are obtained by assuming it for a session, yielding temporary credentials. It is not a person, token device, or firewall.

q: A corporation is lifting Windows file shares used by desktop applications that expect SMB protocol and Active Directory authentication. Which AWS file storage service is built for this Windows-native pattern?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explain: FSx for Windows File Server provides fully managed Windows file shares with SMB access and Active Directory integration. EFS speaks NFS for Linux workloads, FSx for Lustre targets HPC scratch workloads, and S3 is object storage rather than a file share protocol.

q: A research lab runs tightly coupled high-performance computing simulations where CPU performance matters far more than memory or storage. Which EC2 instance family is designed for this kind of workload?
explain: Compute optimized instances deliver a high ratio of vCPU to memory for CPU-bound work such as HPC, batch processing, and gaming servers. Memory optimized suits large in-memory datasets, storage optimized suits local-disk throughput, and general purpose balances all three resources.

q: Employees should reach several business applications and AWS accounts with one workforce login managed by the company. Which service is designed for workforce single sign-on?
explain: IAM Identity Center is the workforce SSO service for AWS accounts and business apps. Cognito targets the application own customers, not the company workforce.

q: After an alert about a possibly compromised instance, investigators need to visualize relationships between principals, IPs, and resources over time. Which service supports this investigation?
explain: Detective builds behavior graphs from log data so investigators can trace security issues, related entities, and timelines during incident investigation.

q: A company's primary requirement is automatic failover of its RDS database if an Availability Zone fails. Which feature meets this requirement?
explain: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby in another AZ and fails over automatically — that's high availability. Read Replicas are asynchronous copies for scaling reads (manual promotion). Snapshots are point-in-time backups, not failover. ElastiCache is an in-memory cache.

q: A company wants discounted compute pricing but needs flexibility to switch instance families, committing to a fixed $/hour spend for 1–3 years. Which should it choose?
explain: Compute Savings Plans discount any EC2 usage (any family, size, Region, even Fargate/Lambda) in exchange for a $/hour commitment. Standard RIs lock you to an instance family and AZ for a bigger discount.

q: A team runs its code on Lambda and Fargate so it never manages servers. A critical operating-system vulnerability is announced affecting the underlying hosts. Who patches them?
options: No patching is needed for serverless workloads
explain: On Lambda and Fargate, AWS owns the entire execution environment including host OS patching — the customer only manages code, configuration, and IAM. (Contrast EC2, where the customer patches the guest OS.) Serverless still runs on hosts; AWS just manages them.

q: A data team must clean, join, and reformat raw files landing in S3 every hour and record the resulting tables in a central catalog that other tools can query. Which AWS service provides serverless ETL jobs plus that Data Catalog?
explain: Glue is the serverless ETL service: crawlers catalog your data, and jobs transform it with the catalog as the shared metadata store. Athena queries but does not transform pipelines, QuickSight visualizes, and DataSync moves files without ETL or cataloging.

Enterprise Support includes proactive services delivered through the dedicated TAM, such as scheduled operations reviews and guidance that can extend to third-party software configuration. Lower tiers provide reactive case support only.
options: Technical Account Manager proactive services and operational reviews
q: Which Support plan feature lets Enterprise customers get help with third-party software configuration questions and infrastructure operations reviews on a scheduled basis?
A hospital must keep patient records on-premises for compliance but wants to burst analytics workloads to AWS. Which deployment model is this?
explain: On-premises + AWS working together = hybrid (via Direct Connect, Storage Gateway, or Outposts). Public-only would move everything to AWS; on-premises-only uses no cloud at all.

q: An analyst wants to run standard SQL queries directly against log files sitting in S3, paying per query, with no servers or database to load the files into first. Which service is purpose-built for this serverless, query-in-place pattern?
explain: Athena queries data in place in S3 using SQL, serverlessly, charging for data scanned per query, perfect for ad hoc log analysis. EMR runs managed clusters, RDS is a transactional database you must load data into, and a provisioned warehouse cluster runs (and bills) continuously.

q: A retailer runs its own firewall appliance on EC2. Who configures the firewall rules inside that appliance?
explain: Anything the customer deploys on EC2, including a self-managed firewall and its rules, is customer configured. AWS only secures the infrastructure below the guest OS.

q: Alerts appear about an EC2 instance communicating with a known malicious IP and making unusual DNS requests. Which service most likely generated these threat findings?
explain: GuardDuty analyzes VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events with threat intelligence to flag malicious IPs, compromised instances, and unusual API behavior.

q: A manufacturer deploys containers on AWS Fargate. Who patches the underlying host operating system that runs those containers?
explain: Fargate is serverless for containers, so AWS manages and patches the hosts. The customer still secures its container images, task roles, and application code.

q: A biotech lab uses S3 for research data. AWS protects the storage service itself from infrastructure attacks. Deciding which lab members may read each dataset is whose duty?
explain: Access decisions for customer data always belong to the data owner. AWS secures the service platform, while Macie can only help discover sensitive content.

q: A nonprofit photo archive used to budget a lump sum every four years to replace aging storage arrays. After moving to AWS it pays a small amount per gigabyte stored each month. Which advantage is most evident?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Per-gigabyte monthly billing instead of periodic lump-sum hardware replacement is the fixed-to-variable expense trade. The scenario says nothing about new countries, faster releases, or provider purchasing power.

q: A consultant lists candidate categories for a cloud adoption plan. Which TWO belong to the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework? (Select TWO.)
explain: Business and Governance are two of the six CAF perspectives. Reliability and Cost Optimization are Well-Architected Framework pillars, a common exam confusion with CAF perspectives.

q: Which service tracks configuration changes to AWS resources over time and evaluates them against compliance rules?
explain: AWS Config records resource configurations and their change history, then checks them against rules (e.g., 'S3 buckets must not be public'). CloudTrail logs the API calls that caused changes; Config tracks the resulting state.

q: A retailer keeps its live order database on RDS and wants nightly business-intelligence extracts without slowing order processing; the BI team queries a separate analytical store refreshed from the transactional data. Which architecture follows the standard OLTP/OLAP separation?
options: Replace RDS with S3 Glacier Deep Archive for live orders
Store orders in ElastiCache as the system of record
Run all reporting directly against the production RDS primary at peak hours
Keep orders on RDS and load extracts into Amazon Redshift for analysis
explain: Extracting transactional data into Redshift lets analysts run heavy queries on a store built for them without contending with live order traffic on RDS. Hammering the production primary risks the business, and neither a cache nor an archive class can serve as the live transactional store.

q: A transport company stores backups in Glacier. AWS maintains the archive storage hardware. What must the company still manage?
options: Vault access policies and retention decisions
explain: For archive storage the customer manages vault policies, access, and retention. Hardware, facilities, and firmware are operated by AWS as the provider.

q: An IoT platform ingests sensor readings from millions of meters using an existing Cassandra driver and query language, and wants AWS to run the clusters. Which managed service keeps the Cassandra API while removing node operations?
explain: Keyspaces is the Cassandra-compatible managed service, so existing CQL and drivers carry over while AWS operates the fleet. DocumentDB speaks MongoDB APIs, RDS for PostgreSQL speaks SQL, and Neptune speaks graph query languages.

q: A security team wants full lifecycle control of its encryption keys — creating them, defining the rotation schedule, and revoking them instantly if compromised. Which key type in KMS gives this control?
explain: Customer managed keys = you create and fully control them, including rotation schedules and instant disable. AWS managed keys are created and rotated by AWS on your behalf; AWS owned keys are used internally by AWS services; S3-managed keys are entirely S3-managed.

q: A company with 50 AWS accounts wants to manage WAF rules and security group policies centrally from one place. Which service does this?
explain: Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall rules (WAF, security groups, Shield Advanced) across accounts in an organization. Security Hub aggregates security findings; GuardDuty detects threats; Organizations manages the accounts and billing, not firewall rules.

Cost allocation tags appear in billing data only after activation in the Billing console, and they take up to 24 hours to appear; historical data before activation is not re-tagged. This is a classic billing gotcha tested by CLF-C02.
options: Within about 24 hours, applying from activation onward
Only at the start of the next calendar year
q: After activating cost allocation tags in the Billing console, when do the tags begin appearing in cost reports?
In CAF terms, a team works on visibility, auditability, and control of identities and data as the organization adopts cloud. Which perspective is this?
explain: The CAF Security perspective focuses on visibility, auditability, controllability, and agility of security during adoption. Governance is broader oversight; Security is its own named perspective in CAF.

q: A European retailer runs its storefront database in Frankfurt and opens a read-heavy storefront for Asia-Pacific shoppers served from Singapore. Which RDS capability places a readable copy of the data in the second Region to cut read latency there?
explain: RDS supports cross-Region read replicas that asynchronously copy data to another Region so nearby readers get low-latency reads. A Multi-AZ standby stays in the home Region and accepts no reads, and exports or imports do not maintain a live replicated copy.

Trusted Advisor checks fall into categories including cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits. It evaluates your AWS resources only; it does not assess employees or market data.
q: Which categories does AWS Trusted Advisor check? (Select TWO.)

A company will run steady workloads for a year and wants a commitment discount, but it may need to switch EC2 instance families mid-term as requirements change. Which Reserved Instance type allows changing the instance family?
explain: Convertible RIs can be exchanged for a different instance family mid-term (for a smaller discount than Standard). Standard RIs lock the instance attributes for the maximum discount; On-Demand and Spot involve no commitment at all.
The AWS Personal Health Dashboard (part of AWS Health) shows events relevant to your own accounts and resources. The public Service Health Dashboard shows only general, region-wide service status.
q: Which AWS Support feature gives a personalized view of AWS service health events that specifically affect YOUR resources, including scheduled maintenance?
What is true about IAM in AWS?
options: IAM is a global service and identities work across Regions
IAM only applies to EC2 instances
IAM is configured separately in each Region
explain: IAM is global, not regional, so users, groups, roles, and policies are created once and apply across Regions. Resource policies still exist alongside IAM policies.

q: A small genomics lab obtains storage pricing far lower than any quote it could negotiate alone, because its provider aggregates demand from millions of customers when buying hardware. Which advantage is the lab benefiting from?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: AWS buys hardware and power at enormous volume and passes lower unit prices to customers, which is benefiting from massive economies of scale. The lab did nothing global or faster; the point is provider-scale purchasing.

q: A junior admin accidentally attaches an overly broad policy. Reviewing and correcting IAM policies in the account is whose ongoing responsibility?
explain: Customers own the policies they create and attach. AWS provides analyzers and simulators to help, but review and correction remain the customer job.

q: A retail chain's data warehouse must answer a query that scans two years of receipts; engineers note Redshift reads only the columns a query names instead of whole rows. Which warehouse design trait produces this scan efficiency?
explain: Redshift stores data by column, so analytical queries read just the columns they aggregate, massively reducing I/O on wide tables. Graph, purely in-memory, and ledger designs describe Neptune, ElastiCache-style caching, and QLDB rather than warehouse storage layout.

q: A startup wants to host a simple static marketing website — just HTML, CSS, and images — with no servers to manage and minimal cost. Which option fits?
options: An EBS volume attached to EC2
explain: S3 can directly host static websites: upload the files, enable website hosting, done — no servers, tiny cost. EBS and EFS are block/file storage for EC2; RDS is a relational database; none serve websites by themselves.

q: An engineer designs a payment flow so that if the recommendation engine is down, checkout still completes without recommendations. Which principle guided this?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explain: Graceful degradation when a non-essential component fails is design for failure in action. The system anticipates the fault and preserves its core function.

q: Before applying a risky CloudFormation update, a team generates a preview listing exactly which resources will be added, modified, or replaced, and only proceeds after review. Which CloudFormation feature produces this preview?
explain: Change sets summarize the proposed modifications a stack update will make, including replacements, so teams can approve changes with full knowledge of their blast radius. Drift detection compares live resources to the current template, stack policies guard resources during updates, and rollback triggers watch update health rather than previewing changes.

q: How does envelope encryption work in AWS KMS?
options: KMS generates a data key, the data is encrypted locally with it, and the data key is stored encrypted
Keys are emailed to the application owner
Data is compressed instead of encrypted
The data is sent to KMS for every encrypt operation
explain: In envelope encryption, KMS returns a plaintext and encrypted copy of a data key; data is encrypted locally with the plaintext key, which is then discarded and stored only encrypted.

q: Which AWS Support plan is free and includes 7 core Trusted Advisor checks?
explain: Basic = free for every account: 7 core Trusted Advisor checks, Personal Health Dashboard, and 24/7 customer service for billing. Paid plans start at Developer ($29/month).

q: An architect spreads a checkout service across three Availability Zones and adds health-based routing so one zone's loss does not interrupt orders. Which pillar drove this design?
explain: Distributing a workload across multiple AZs to survive a facility failure is a Reliability design decision. Any performance or cost effects are secondary to surviving the failure.

q: The finance team needs the most granular billing data available — hourly, line-item usage per resource — to feed a custom chargeback system. Which provides it?
explain: The CUR is the raw, most-detailed billing dataset, delivered to S3 for custom analysis. Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes spend; Budgets alerts on thresholds; the Pricing Calculator estimates costs before you build — none give raw line-item data.

q: A message keeps failing processing because its data is malformed; after several retries the team wants it parked somewhere for inspection instead of looping forever and blocking the queue. Which SQS feature captures these poison messages?
explain: Dead-letter queues receive messages that exceed a queue's maximum receive count, isolating failures for debugging while healthy messages keep flowing. Deduplication IDs prevent duplicates in FIFO queues, a zero visibility timeout would cause instant redelivery loops, and SNS filters route notifications rather than quarantine queue messages.
AWS re:Post is the community question-and-answer service (successor to the AWS Forums) where customers post technical questions answered by community members and AWS experts.
q: Where can AWS customers ask technical questions and get answers from the AWS community and AWS experts on a public forum?
An auditor wants continuous, automated collection of evidence showing that the company's AWS usage meets its compliance requirements. Which service is built for this?
explain: Audit Manager continuously gathers evidence and produces audit-ready reports mapped to compliance frameworks. Artifact is where you download AWS's own compliance reports; Config tracks resource configuration compliance; CloudTrail logs API activity — both feed evidence, but neither generates the audit report.

q: A retail conglomerate orders Outposts for two distribution centers. Which statement about what arrives and who operates it is accurate?
options: The customer assembles commodity servers and AWS only ships software licenses
AWS delivers, installs, monitors, and maintains the rack hardware, and the customer runs workloads on it with familiar AWS tools
Outposts hardware is owned and patched entirely by the customer's facilities team
Outposts is a virtual appliance downloaded onto existing VMware hosts only
explain: Outposts is a fully managed on-premises extension: AWS provides the physical rack, manages its health, patching, and replacement, while customers provision resources with the same console and APIs as in a Region. It is not a do-it-yourself hardware kit or a mere software download.

q: Which service would alert a team that an S3 bucket contains unencrypted credit card numbers uploaded by mistake?
explain: Macie scans S3 content for sensitive data patterns such as payment card numbers and alerts on discovery, especially when buckets are public or shared.

q: A database team wants RDS storage encrypted and needs to choose the key at creation time because it cannot be changed later. Which service manages that key?
explain: RDS encryption at creation uses a KMS key to encrypt the underlying storage. The choice is made at creation and the encrypted instance cannot be converted in place.

q: A warehouse operator uses DynamoDB. Which patching duty does the operator NOT have?
explain: DynamoDB is fully managed, so AWS patches all service hosts and software. The operator still controls access policies, data classification, and configuration choices.

q: A multiplayer game uses a custom TCP protocol. It needs two static IP addresses that route players to the nearest healthy AWS Region with automatic failover. Caching is not needed. Which service should be used?
options: Route 53 with a latency routing policy
explain: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and routes traffic to the optimal healthy endpoint — no caching, works for TCP/UDP including non-HTTP. CloudFront is a CDN that caches HTTP content. An ALB is regional, not global.

q: A company uses AWS Organizations with consolidated billing. It purchases Reserved Instances in the management account, but one member account doesn't use its full share. What happens to the unused reservation discount?
options: It is lost at the end of the month
It automatically applies to matching usage in other member accounts on the consolidated bill
It can only be used by the management account
explain: With consolidated billing, unused Reserved Instance discounts float across the organization — any member account's matching usage picks them up automatically. Nothing is lost or locked to the purchasing account.

q: Can customers perform penetration testing against their own EC2 instances and other eligible AWS resources?
options: Yes — permitted on most services without prior approval, following the AWS penetration testing policy
Only with written approval requested 30 days in advance
Only on weekends between midnight and 6 AM
No — penetration testing is never allowed on AWS
explain: AWS allows security assessments and pen tests against your own resources on eligible services without pre-approval, as long as you stay within the published policy (e.g., no DDoS or DNS zone-walking).

q: A network team uses Transit Gateway route tables to keep the production VPCs able to reach shared services while development VPCs cannot route into production at all. Which Transit Gateway capability enforces this segmentation?
options: Security groups attached to the Transit Gateway itself
S3 bucket policies on a central bucket
Separate route tables per attachment controlling which networks each attachment can reach
explain: Transit Gateway supports multiple route tables and association/propagation controls, letting architects segment which attachments can reach which networks through the hub. Security groups do not attach to the gateway, and storage policies or CDN signatures do not govern network routing.

q: Which TWO services decouple application components so they can scale and fail independently? (Select TWO.)
explain: SQS (message queues) and SNS (pub/sub notifications) decouple producers from consumers — the core of resilient, event-driven architectures. EC2, EBS, and VPC are compute/storage/network building blocks, not decoupling services.

q: A migration project must move a live Oracle database into Aurora PostgreSQL while the source keeps serving customers, with changes replicated continuously until a short cutover window. Which service performs the ongoing data migration with minimal downtime?
explain: DMS replicates data from source to target continuously, including change data capture, so the source stays online until cutover. SCT converts schemas but does not move live data, DataSync moves files, and Snowball ships bulk data without continuous replication.

Lambda pricing = number of requests plus compute duration measured in GB-seconds (memory allocated x runtime). There is no hourly instance charge because Lambda is serverless and runs only when invoked.
options: Number of requests and GB-seconds of compute duration
Number of developers deploying the function
Per gigabyte of data stored in the function
q: How is AWS Lambda priced?

A software team's continuous-integration runners are perfect for spare capacity: builds queue up, tolerate interruption, and restart cheaply if a runner disappears mid-job. Which EC2 purchasing option gives the deepest discounts for this fault-tolerant work?
options: Reserved Instances with full upfront payment
explain: Spot Instances sell unused EC2 capacity at up to 90 percent off in exchange for a two-minute interruption warning, which CI fleets absorb by requeuing jobs. Reserved pricing suits steady commitments, Dedicated Hosts address licensing and isolation, and On-Demand forfeits the deep discount the workload's flexibility earns.

q: A mobile app backend running on Lambda needs to write logs and read one S3 bucket. How should those permissions be granted?
options: Attach an execution role scoped to those actions and resources
Embed the developer access keys in the function
explain: Lambda functions use an execution role with scoped permissions. Embedding developer keys or granting admin or public access all expose far more than the function needs.

q: Which element in an IAM policy states whether the listed actions are permitted?
options: Sid set to a random string
Version set to the policy date
Effect set to Allow or Deny
Principal set to the account number
explain: The Effect element is where a policy declares Allow or Deny for its actions and resources. Version, Sid, and Principal serve other structural purposes.

q: During portfolio analysis, a team finds three overlapping legacy survey tools with a combined handful of users and consolidates everyone onto one kept system. The two dropped tools follow which strategy?
explain: Workloads eliminated during rationalization, with users absorbed elsewhere or simply ended, are retired. The kept system might itself be rehosted or repurchased, but the dropped ones are retirements.

q: A pharmaceutical knowledge base links compounds, trials, researchers, and publications into a web of facts that researchers explore by following connections. Which AWS database is designed for building and querying such a knowledge graph?
explain: Neptune is built for knowledge graphs and other highly connected datasets, supporting graph query languages for exploring relationships. QLDB is a ledger, ElastiCache is an in-memory cache, and RDS for Oracle is a conventional relational engine without graph-native traversal.

q: A company deploys its application across three Availability Zones in the same Region. Which cloud concept does this primarily achieve?
explain: Spreading across AZs means the application stays available even if an entire data center fails — the definition of high availability. It does not automatically scale (elasticity) or cut cost by itself.

q: A small firm has one web server and needs its domain name to resolve to that server's address with no special logic of any kind. Which Route 53 routing policy is the default, no-frills choice?
explain: Simple routing is the standard DNS behavior: one name maps to the configured values with no health-based, geographic, or proportional decision-making. Every other listed policy adds a decision layer that a single-server setup does not need.

q: A content team asks how edge locations compare with Regions in number. Which response is accurate?
options: A customer chooses one edge location as its primary deployment target
There are more edge locations than there are Regions
Edge locations are another name for Regions
Every edge location contains three Availability Zones
explain: The edge network is far larger than the Region footprint, which is how content gets close to users worldwide. AZs belong inside Regions, not inside edge locations.

q: A company disables an employee departing IAM user but the employee also had access keys. What else must be done for full revocation?
options: Delete the S3 buckets the user accessed
Change the account root password only
Deactivate or delete the user access keys as well
explain: Console sign-in and programmatic access keys are separate credentials. Both must be disabled or removed, otherwise the keys can still call AWS APIs.
