Which service would a bank use to meet a requirement that FIPS-validated, dedicated cryptographic modules generate its keys?
explain: CloudHSM clusters provide FIPS-validated dedicated hardware modules where the customer generates and controls keys for strict regulatory workloads.

q: A streaming startup launches in one Region, proves its product, then opens identical deployments on three other continents within a week using its infrastructure templates. Which global-infrastructure property of AWS makes this expansion speed possible?
options: S3 buckets replicate compute services between Regions automatically
Availability Zones can be reassigned to other continents when needed
Edge locations automatically convert into full Regions on demand
Regions exist worldwide, so the same stack can be deployed close to users in minutes rather than building data centers
explain: AWS operates Regions around the world, so proven stacks can be redeployed near new audiences quickly with templates; no construction project is required. Edge locations never become Regions, AZs are fixed to their Region, and buckets store objects rather than replicating running services.

q: An operations team wants Route 53 to return up to eight healthy records for a name so clients can pick one and retry another if a connection fails, improving resilience without a load balancer change. Which policy returns multiple values with health checks applied?
explain: Multivalue answer routing returns up to eight records and omits any that fail health checks, giving clients resilient choices at the DNS layer. Simple routing returns values without health filtering, and weighted or geolocation policies solve proportion and location problems instead.

q: A media startup founded last year has no servers of its own and runs its entire product on AWS from day one. Which deployment model describes it?
explain: A company with no premises infrastructure whose workloads all run in the cloud is all-in cloud, sometimes called cloud-native in deployment terms.

q: During a migration review, an engineer summarizes the ELB family for executives in one line per type. Which summary line for the Gateway Load Balancer is accurate?
options: It routes HTTP requests by URL path to different services
It provides static IPs for TCP gaming traffic
It is the retired first-generation balancer for EC2-Classic
It deploys and scales third-party virtual network appliances such as firewalls
explain: GWLB's single purpose is running fleets of partner virtual appliances with transparent traffic steering. Path routing is the ALB's signature, static-IP Layer 4 scale is the NLB's, and the retired-generation description belongs to the Classic Load Balancer.

q: A climate research center runs HPC jobs that need a temporary shared file system delivering sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s throughput, integrated with S3 for input and output data. Which service fits this scratch-space role?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon EFS with general purpose mode only
explain: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance file system for compute-intensive workloads such as HPC and machine learning, and it links natively to S3 repositories. EFS and the Windows variant do not target this throughput class, and a tape gateway is an archival backup interface.

q: Which credential type is intended for command-line and API access for an IAM user when a role cannot be used?
options: Access key ID and secret access key pair
explain: Programmatic access for an IAM user uses an access key pair. The console password is for browser sign-in only, and MFA devices provide second factors, not API credentials.

q: A security lead discovers the root user has no second factor enabled. What is the most urgent remediation?
options: Enable MFA on the root user
explain: The root user has unrestricted access and cannot be deleted, so enabling MFA on it is the urgent first step, then avoiding its use for everyday work.

q: A data team loads multi-terabyte datasets onto EBS and scans them sequentially all day; the workload cares about throughput in MB/s, not small random IOPS, and cost must stay low. Which EBS volume type matches?
explain: st1 volumes deliver low-cost, high sequential throughput for big-data, log processing, and warehouse-style scans. The SSD types optimize for IOPS and latency at higher cost, while sc1 is for cold, infrequently accessed data rather than all-day active scanning.

q: A telecom analytics team runs Apache Cassandra workloads today and wants the same wide-column model as a serverless, managed service on AWS without operating nodes. Which database is the Cassandra-compatible option?
explain: Amazon Keyspaces is the managed, serverless Cassandra-compatible database service, accepting existing Cassandra query language and drivers. DocumentDB mimics MongoDB, Neptune is graph, and Redshift is a relational warehouse, so only Keyspaces matches the Cassandra requirement.
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class, designed for long-term retention and compliance archives that are rarely accessed and tolerate retrieval times measured in hours.
q: Which Amazon S3 storage class has the LOWEST storage cost and is intended for data accessed once or twice a year with hours-long retrieval?
A team validates its architecture by simulating a full production-scale load test in the cloud for one afternoon, then tears the environment down. Which principle lets it test this way?
options: Skip load testing for cloud systems
Test systems at production scale on demand
Buy permanent hardware equal to production
explain: Cloud design principles endorse testing at production scale because the environment can be created on demand and discarded afterward. Owning permanent test hardware at that scale is rarely economical.

q: A bank's internal audit system must show, for every account adjustment ever made, who made it, when, and that the sequence has never been rewritten. Which database should the architects shortlist first?
explain: QLDB's append-only journal with cryptographic verification is designed for exactly this system-of-record audit trail, proving sequence integrity. Ordinary databases allow updates and deletes by design, and disciplined habits cannot substitute for a ledger's built-in proof.

q: Which description best fits Amazon ECS on its own terms?
options: A highly scalable container orchestration service from AWS that schedules Docker containers across managed infrastructure
A simple virtual server bundle with a flat monthly price
A managed Kubernetes service using upstream tooling
A serverless function runtime billed per millisecond
explain: ECS is AWS's native container orchestrator for running and scaling Docker containers. EKS is the Kubernetes offering, Lambda is the function runtime, and Lightsail is the flat-price VPS bundle, so each distractor names a neighboring service's role.

q: A security team must insert a fleet of third-party firewall and intrusion-prevention appliances into the traffic path for all VPC traffic, scaling and load balancing them transparently. Which load balancer type exists for exactly this appliance deployment pattern?
explain: Gateway Load Balancer distributes traffic to pools of virtual appliances (firewalls, IDS/IPS, deep packet inspection) and scales them while staying transparent to the traffic flow. ALB and NLB balance application targets rather than inserting middlebox appliances into routed paths.

q: A subscription service reviews its bill monthly, tags every resource by product line, and shuts down development environments overnight and on weekends. Which pillar does this routine serve?
explain: Visibility into spend plus eliminating idle-time costs is Cost Optimization. Sustainability might applaud the shutdowns, but the stem's stated purpose is managing the bill.

q: A team documents runbooks for common incidents, reviews operational metrics daily, and improves its deployment process after every outage. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar does this work support?
explain: Operational Excellence = running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continually improve processes — runbooks, observability, and learning from incidents. Reliability is about the workload surviving failure; Cost Optimization is about the bill; Security is about protecting data and systems.

q: A company needs server-side encryption for S3 with AWS-managed keys and an audit trail of every key usage. Which option fits?
explain: SSE-KMS uses KMS keys, and every encrypt/decrypt call is logged in CloudTrail — giving the audit trail. SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys with no per-use audit log; SSE-C means you manage the keys yourself.

q: An RDS database needs automatic failover to a standby in another Availability Zone if the primary fails. Which feature provides this?
explain: Multi-AZ = a synchronous standby in another AZ with automatic failover for high availability. Read replicas are asynchronous and for scaling reads, not failover; backups are for point-in-time restore.

q: Which TWO tools help monitor and control AWS costs? (Select TWO.)
explain: Budgets alerts on spend thresholds; Cost Explorer analyzes and forecasts spend. Shield (DDoS), Macie (sensitive data), and WAF (web firewall) are security services, not cost tools.

q: What is the purpose of AWS compliance programs documentation in Artifact and the compliance center?
options: To show which AWS services are in scope for programs such as HIPAA, PCI, and ISO
explain: Compliance program resources identify in-scope AWS services and provide reports and whitepapers so customers can design workloads within each program rules.

q: A DynamoDB-backed shopping cart slows down because every read goes to the table itself; the team adds an in-memory caching layer that sits in front of DynamoDB and serves popular carts in microseconds. Which feature did the team enable?
explain: DAX is a fully managed in-memory cache for DynamoDB that cuts read latency to microseconds without application rewrites beyond a client change. Global tables replicate across Regions, Streams capture changes for processing, and Auto Scaling adjusts provisioned capacity; none caches reads in memory.

q: A hospital archives MRI scans. They are accessed a few times a year but must be available within minutes when requested. The scans cannot be recreated. Which S3 storage class is the best fit?
explain: Standard-IA = infrequently accessed with millisecond retrieval. Deep Archive takes hours to retrieve. One Zone-IA lives in a single AZ — only for data you can recreate, which these scans are not. Standard works but costs more than needed.

q: Which TWO statements describe customer responsibilities that do NOT disappear when using managed services? (Select TWO.)
options: Protecting data and controlling who can access it
Configuring access policies for the service
explain: Managed services remove host and hypervisor patching, but data protection and access policy configuration always stay with the customer.

q: A retailer notices that a newly launched subnet's instances cannot reach the internet even though an internet gateway is attached to the VPC and the instances have public IPs. Which missing configuration most likely explains it?
options: The VPC has no CloudFront distribution
The subnet's route table has no route directing internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway
The subnet needs a second DHCP option set
The instances lack an S3 bucket policy
explain: Attaching an internet gateway is only half the setup: the subnet route table must also contain a route (typically 0.0.0.0/0 to the gateway) or packets have no path out. Bucket policies, CloudFront, and DHCP options play no role in instance internet routing.

q: A tax software firm archives prior-year return documents in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval; an auditor occasionally needs a document back within a few hours, never within seconds. Which property makes Flexible Retrieval acceptable here that would rule it out for a live application?
options: Objects cannot exceed 5 GB in size
Objects are automatically deleted after 30 days
Objects must be restored before they can be read, and retrieval takes minutes to hours
Objects are stored in only one Availability Zone
explain: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is archive storage: a restore request copies the object to a temporary readable state over minutes to hours, so it suits audit archives but not interactive workloads. It still stores data redundantly across AZs and does not impose the deletion or size limits described.

q: Which task belongs to AWS when a customer runs workloads on Amazon EC2?
explain: AWS owns the virtualization layer and physical infrastructure for EC2. IAM, application code, guest configuration, and data backups remain customer duties.

q: A CFO asks which CAF perspective she belongs to when building the cloud business case and defining success measures with other executives. Which is correct?
explain: Building the business case and defining expected business outcomes with executive stakeholders is Business perspective work in CAF. Finance participates in Governance too, but the case itself is Business.

q: A retailer finds its servers average 12 percent utilization because the fleet was sized for the December peak. From a cloud economics view, what is the core problem?
options: It pays for peak capacity all year while using only a fraction of it
Its customers shop mostly in December
Its servers use the wrong operating system
It has too many retail stores
explain: Low average utilization means money is locked in idle capacity for most of the year. Cloud economics favors matching provisioned capacity to actual demand instead of owning the peak year-round.

q: A workload is quiet at night but sees 10x traffic at noon. Which approach keeps costs lowest while meeting demand?
options: Buy 3-year Reserved capacity sized for peak
Automatically scale capacity up and down with demand
Provision for peak traffic and run it 24/7
explain: Automatic scaling (elasticity) means paying for peak only during peak — the 'stop guessing capacity' benefit. Provisioning for peak 24/7 wastes money 20 hours a day; Reserved for peak over-commits.

q: Employees access company applications hosted on AWS from laptops, tablets, and phones over the internet, with nothing installed locally. Which essential characteristic of cloud computing describes this?
explain: Broad network access = services available over the network and reachable from many device types. Resource pooling is shared infrastructure; measured service is metering for billing; rapid elasticity is fast scaling.

q: An SCP denies S3 access in an organizational unit, but an IAM policy attached to a user in a member account of that unit allows it. What is the effective result for that user?
options: The SCP only restricts the management account, so the user keeps access
The SCP grants S3 access to every user in the unit
The IAM policy wins because it is more specific
S3 access is denied — the SCP sets the maximum permissions ceiling
explain: SCPs are guardrails that set the maximum allowed permissions — an explicit SCP deny overrides any IAM allow. SCPs never grant permissions themselves, and they apply to member accounts (not the management account).

q: A firm imports its own key material into KMS for regulatory reasons. What extra duty does importing create?
options: ACM must renew the material monthly
The material becomes an AWS owned key
The customer is responsible for the durability and availability of the imported material
None, AWS backs up imported material forever by default
explain: With imported key material the customer retains responsibility for its security and durability outside AWS; if it is lost and no copy exists, data may be unrecoverable.

q: A student wants a simple virtual server with bundled storage and networking at one predictable low monthly price for a class project — no complex options. Which service is the simplest fit?
explain: Lightsail bundles compute, storage, and networking into simple, predictable-price VPS plans — ideal for small projects. EC2 offers far more options and knobs; Outposts is AWS hardware on-premises; Wavelength is carrier 5G edge.

q: A company uses a vendor's complete email application delivered over the internet, with no infrastructure to manage. Which service model is this?
explain: Software as a Service = a finished application consumed over the internet (email, CRM, file sharing). The customer manages only their data and user accounts.

q: Which statement best distinguishes elasticity from scalability?
options: Elasticity is about adding disk space, scalability is about adding servers
Scalability happens automatically, elasticity requires manual tickets
They are identical terms with no distinction
Elasticity automatically matches resources to current demand up and down, while scalability is the broader ability to handle growth
explain: Scalability is the capacity to grow; elasticity adds automatic, timely expansion and contraction that tracks demand. Manual processes can scale a system but cannot make it elastic.

q: Which statement about automatic rotation of customer managed KMS keys is correct?
options: Rotation changes the key ID and breaks old data
Rotation deletes all previously encrypted data
Automatic rotation creates new key material yearly while keeping the same key ID and old material for decryption
Customers must re-encrypt every object manually after rotation
explain: KMS automatic rotation adds new backing key material about yearly under the same key ID; older material is retained so existing ciphertext remains decryptable.

q: Which service uses machine learning to detect threats such as compromised credentials and unusual API activity?
explain: GuardDuty is intelligent threat detection — it analyzes CloudTrail, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs with ML. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities; WAF filters web traffic; Shield mitigates DDoS.

CloudWatch alarms on the EstimatedCharges billing metric (published to us-east-1) are a traditional method for threshold billing alerts. They observe spend, they cannot cap it — AWS has no 'hard spending cap' switch for standard accounts.
options: A CloudWatch alarm on the EstimatedCharges billing metric
A Support case requesting a cap
q: A customer wants an alert when estimated AWS charges pass a dollar amount, independent of Budgets. Which mechanism provides this?
A publisher uses CloudFront to deliver articles. Who chooses whether viewer connections require HTTPS?
explain: Viewer protocol policy is a distribution setting the customer chooses. AWS operates the edge infrastructure, but HTTPS enforcement is the publisher configuration.

q: A backup review asks what EBS snapshots make possible. Which TWO capabilities do snapshots provide? (Select TWO.)
options: A snapshot captures the full volume again on every backup, never incrementally
Snapshots exist only while the original volume exists
A snapshot can be copied to another Region for disaster recovery
Snapshots can be shared with other AWS accounts
explain: EBS snapshots are incremental point-in-time backups that can be copied across Regions and shared with other accounts, and they persist independently of the source volume. Only the first snapshot is full; later ones store changed blocks only.

q: A security engineer wants Security Hub findings sent automatically to a ticketing workflow when severity is high. Security Hub integrates with which event and response ecosystem?
explain: Security Hub publishes findings to EventBridge and integrates with ticketing and response tools, enabling automated triage workflows for high-severity findings.

q: A bank wants a chat and voice assistant that understands customers asking about balances and card blocks, built on the same conversational technology family as Alexa. Which service builds such conversational interfaces?
explain: Lex provides automatic speech recognition and natural-language understanding to build chatbots and voice bots that grasp intents and slots in conversation. Comprehend analyzes text sentiment and entities, Textract reads documents, and Forecast predicts time series; only Lex is the conversational interface builder.

q: Employees waste hours hunting through wikis, tickets, and shared drives; the company wants a search box that understands natural questions and returns precise answers drawn from its internal documents. Which service provides this ML-powered enterprise search?
explain: Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that indexes connected document sources and answers natural-language questions with relevant passages. OpenSearch can power keyword search you build yourself, CloudFront distributes content, and Glue catalogs data for analytics rather than answering employee questions.

q: Which example shows security OF the cloud?
options: A customer sets an S3 bucket policy
A customer enables MFA for users
explain: Security of the cloud covers what AWS builds and operates, such as hypervisor patching. Bucket policies, data classification, and MFA are security in the cloud.

q: Regulations require that data stored on EBS volumes be unreadable if a physical drive is stolen from the data center. Which protection addresses this?
explain: Encryption at rest protects data on disk — a stolen drive holds only ciphertext. TLS protects data in transit on the wire; security groups and IAM policies control access but don't encrypt the stored data.

q: A software asset manager must track Microsoft and Oracle license usage across EC2 and on-premises servers to stay within purchased entitlements and simplify true-ups. Which AWS service is built to manage software licenses centrally?
explain: License Manager lets you define licensing rules, attach them to resources, and track consumption across AWS and on-premises environments to prevent overuse. Service Catalog curates launchable products, Parameter Store holds settings, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities rather than counting licenses.

q: A European retailer must give customers the right to have personal data erased and must protect EU residents data. Which regulation drives this?
explain: The GDPR is the EU data protection regulation granting rights such as erasure and requiring lawful handling of EU residents personal data wherever it is processed.

q: A regional bank closes a leased data hall and redeploys its infrastructure technicians to customer-facing digital projects because AWS now houses and maintains the hardware. Which advantage is most evident?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Exiting facility operations and hardware maintenance is the data-center advantage. The bank's staff time moves from maintaining buildings and machines to higher-value work, which is the core of this benefit.
Standard Reserved Instances can be resold on the Reserved Instance Marketplace when no longer needed. Spot capacity cannot be resold, and On-Demand has no commitment to transfer.
q: A company downsizes and no longer needs the full term of a commitment it purchased. Which commitment can it sell to another AWS customer through an AWS marketplace?
How can a company track and categorize AWS costs by project, team, or department across shared resources?
explain: Cost allocation tags (e.g., Project=Website) label resources so bills break down by tag. Consolidated billing merges accounts; SCPs restrict permissions — neither categorizes spend.

q: Compliance rules require that every object uploaded to an S3 bucket in us-east-1 is automatically copied to a bucket in eu-west-1. Which feature does this?
explain: Cross-Region Replication asynchronously copies new objects to a destination bucket in another Region as they arrive. Versioning keeps old versions in the same bucket; lifecycle policies change storage class or expire objects; Object Lock prevents deletion.

q: An auditor wants evidence that a control, such as MFA enforcement, operated throughout the quarter, not just today. Which service assembles time-based evidence like this?
explain: Audit Manager continuously collects evidence from AWS sources over the assessment period, which suits operating-effectiveness questions better than a one-time screenshot.

q: An architect draws the VPC design on a whiteboard: web servers accept connections from the internet, reply to those same connections, and nothing extra must be configured for the replies to flow back. Which component's stateful behavior guarantees the return traffic is allowed?
options: Network ACLs on the database subnet
Security groups attached to the web servers
explain: Security groups are stateful: once inbound traffic is allowed in, the return traffic of that connection is automatically permitted regardless of outbound rules. NACLs are stateless and need explicit rules both ways, while DNS zones and bucket policies do not filter instance traffic at all.

q: Federated users signing in through an external identity provider typically obtain AWS access by doing what?
options: Creating local IAM users with same passwords
Assuming an IAM role mapped to their federated identity
explain: Federation maps external identities to IAM roles, and users assume those roles to receive temporary credentials, avoiding duplicate local accounts and passwords.

q: A company launches a public-facing web server that must accept inbound traffic from customers on the internet. Which VPC component connects the VPC to the internet for this two-way traffic?
explain: An internet gateway attaches to the VPC and routes traffic between the public subnet and the internet in both directions. A NAT gateway allows only outbound internet from private subnets; VPC endpoints reach AWS services privately; a virtual private gateway terminates VPN connections.

q: A product manager confuses two S3 numbers in a planning document. Which pairing correctly separates durability from availability for S3 Standard?
options: Both durability and availability are 11 nines
explain: Durability measures whether objects survive intact (11 nines by design), while availability measures how often the service answers requests, which is 99.99 percent for S3 Standard. Mixing the two is a classic exam trap the question is designed to catch.

q: What is the effect of an IAM permissions boundary on a user?
options: It caps the maximum permissions the user can receive from other policies
It grants the user administrator access
It replaces the need for identity policies
It applies only to the root user
explain: A permissions boundary sets a ceiling: identity policies can only grant up to that limit. It never grants permissions by itself and works alongside identity policies.

q: A company needs a private, managed place to store its Docker container images, with vulnerability scanning and tight integration with ECS and EKS. Which service provides this registry?
explain: ECR (Elastic Container Registry) is AWS's private container image registry with scanning and ECS/EKS integration. EFS is shared file storage; S3 stores objects, not container images with Docker semantics; public Hub repos aren't private.

q: Engineers design the landing zone, networking standards, and shared services that every migrating application will build on. Which CAF perspective owns that design?
explain: The Platform perspective covers the architecture and engineering of the cloud platform itself, including landing zones and standards. Operations perspective runs the platform after it exists.

q: A firm wants employees to use their existing corporate directory credentials for AWS workforce access without creating separate passwords. Which combination fits best?
options: Local IAM users mirroring directory passwords
Root user linked to the directory
IAM Identity Center federated with the corporate directory
explain: Identity Center supports federation and directory integration so workforce users sign in with existing corporate credentials and receive permission sets per account.

The Developer plan (from $29/month) adds business-hours email access to cloud support engineers with general-guidance responses in under 24 business hours. Basic Support has no technical support case access at all.
q: A startup needs business-hours email support from cloud support engineers with a response time under 24 hours for general guidance. Which is the LOWEST-cost plan that meets this need?

After several manual console fixes, an engineer wants to know whether the live stack still matches its CloudFormation template or has drifted away from it. Which CloudFormation capability answers that question?
explain: Drift detection compares the actual configuration of stack resources against the template's expected configuration and reports differences caused by out-of-band changes. Change sets preview updates before applying them, deletion protection guards stacks, and nested stacks compose templates; only drift detection audits live-versus-template state.

q: A startup's VPC design places the NAT gateway inside the private subnet by mistake, and outbound patching fails completely. What is wrong with the placement?
options: A NAT gateway must sit inside the database tier for security
A NAT gateway requires one unit per EC2 instance
A NAT gateway only works when placed in an edge location
A NAT gateway must sit in a public subnet with a route to the internet gateway so it can reach the internet itself
explain: The NAT gateway itself needs internet access to forward traffic, so it belongs in a public subnet whose route table points to the internet gateway; private instances then route to the NAT. Placing it in a private subnet strands it with no path out, and it is shared infrastructure, not a per-instance or edge component.

q: Which pairing of migration scenario to strategy is correct?
options: Moving servers unchanged to EC2 - Refactor; switching to a SaaS CRM - Retain
Shutting down an unused app - Repurchase; keeping an app on-premises - Retire
Moving servers unchanged to EC2 - Rehost; moving a database to RDS with minor tweaks - Replatform
Moving VMware estates at hypervisor level - Replatform; rebuilding as microservices - Rehost
explain: Rehost is unchanged lift-and-shift, and replatform adds small managed-service optimizations. Every other pairing swaps definitions, such as calling a shutdown a repurchase.

q: A consultancy wants DNS answers to shift gradually toward a nearby Region as it expands capacity, biasing more traffic to closer endpoints over time while still using some distant capacity. Which Route 53 policy routes by geographic distance with an adjustable bias?
explain: Geoproximity routing sends traffic based on the geographic distance between users and resources, and a bias setting expands or shrinks a resource's effective catchment area. Failover is binary active-passive, weighted ignores distance, and multivalue simply returns a set of healthy records.

q: A logistics firm runs its routing software on Amazon EC2. Who must apply security patches to the Windows operating system inside those instances?
explain: With EC2 the customer owns security in the cloud, including patching the guest operating system, while AWS patches the hypervisor and physical hosts underneath.

q: During a migration assessment, a company discovers several applications that are no longer used at all. Which migration strategy applies to them?
explain: Retire = decommission applications that are no longer needed — it cuts cost and scope. Retain means keeping an app on-premises for now (e.g., due to compliance or latency).
AWS publishes whitepapers and prescriptive documentation that capture best-practice guidance from AWS and its community. They are free references, distinct from billing reports and audit logs.
q: A customer needs official AWS architecture guidance documents on topics such as security best practices and cost optimization frameworks. Which resource publishes these?

A ride-hailing app stores each rider's in-progress trip state so any app server can fetch it in under a millisecond; the state is worthless after the trip ends. Which service is the classic home for this disposable, ultra-fast session data?
explain: In-memory caches like ElastiCache are the textbook session store: microsecond-to-millisecond reads, shared by all app servers, with data that can expire harmlessly. Redshift targets analytics, RDS is durable transactional storage with slower access, and S3 is object storage, not session state.

q: A company will run a database steadily, 24/7, for the next 3 years. Which pricing option gives the largest discount?
explain: A 3-year Reserved Instance commitment for steady-state workloads delivers the deepest EC2 discount (up to ~72% vs. On-Demand). Savings Plans also discount but trade some discount depth for flexibility; Spot doesn't suit a database that can't be interrupted.

q: A team chooses SSE-KMS for S3 objects instead of SSE-S3. What extra benefit does SSE-KMS provide?
options: Separate key permissions and a CloudTrail audit trail of key use
explain: SSE-KMS lets the customer control a KMS key with its own policy and see every use in CloudTrail, unlike SSE-S3 where S3 manages keys with no per-use key audit trail.

q: A bank needs a consistent, private, low-latency connection between its data center and AWS for steady, high-volume traffic. Which service meets this requirement?
explain: Direct Connect is a dedicated private connection with consistent bandwidth. A Site-to-Site VPN runs encrypted over the public internet (faster to set up, less consistent). Client VPN is for remote users; an internet gateway attaches to a VPC, not a data center. Domain 2 — Security and Compliance

q: A company runs NFS file shares on-premises and wants applications there to store and retrieve files in S3 through the familiar file protocols, with a local cache for frequently used files. Which service presents S3 as a file share to on-premises systems?
explain: File Gateway exposes S3 buckets through NFS or SMB mounts for on-premises applications, caching recently used files locally for low-latency access. DataSync copies data rather than presenting a live share, EFS serves workloads inside AWS, and Transfer Family serves SFTP-style transfers for external users.

q: A weather-data company faces unpredictable spikes whenever a hurricane makes landfall. It values that it no longer commits to a fixed fleet sized for a storm that might not happen. Which advantage is this?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explain: Avoiding a fixed commitment based on an unknowable future peak is stop guessing capacity. The company acquires resources when the event actually occurs rather than guessing beforehand.

q: Which list contains the four commonly cited factors for choosing an AWS Region?
options: CPU brand, disk brand, rack height, and cable length
Color, size, age, and ownership of data centers
Compliance, latency, cost, and service availability
Number of airports, highways, rivers, and power plants nearby
explain: Region selection weighs data-residency compliance, proximity-driven latency, regional pricing, and whether needed services are offered there. The other lists are not AWS selection criteria.

q: A platform team wants operating-system and package vulnerabilities scanned on its EC2 fleet and container images in ECR. Which service performs this scanning?
explain: Inspector scans EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions for known software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

q: A retailer wants shoppers to always reach its storefront, even during a data-center problem, accepting that a rare brief reconnect is tolerable. Which property should it optimize?
explain: Keeping the service reachable nearly all the time, tolerating only brief disruption, is the high availability goal. Zero-interruption survival of failures would be the stricter fault-tolerance bar.

q: A holding company acquires three firms, each with its own VPCs and data centers, and the CIO wants every network reachable from every other through one managed attachment point instead of dozens of tunnels and peerings. Which service is the CIO describing?
options: A mesh of VPC peering connections
explain: Transit Gateway replaces meshes with a hub: each VPC and on-premises connection attaches once and can route to all others, subject to its route tables. A peering mesh grows quadratically and stays non-transitive, while internet gateways and CloudFront do not provide private network routing.

q: A gaming company stores save files in S3 and reads that S3 returns success for a write only after the data is stored durably across multiple facilities. Which S3 behavior for read-after-write is the exam-correct description today?
options: S3 overwrites are never visible until the next day
S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for all operations
S3 reads are always eventually consistent for new objects
S3 lists may show deleted objects for up to a week by design
explain: S3 offers strong consistency for PUT, GET, DELETE, and LIST operations, so a successful write is immediately readable. The old eventual-consistency caveats for new-object reads no longer apply, and deletions or overwrites do not linger by design.

q: When selecting a Region for a new batch workload, a team weighs the carbon intensity of local electricity grids alongside technical fit. Which pillar introduces that criterion?
explain: Considering the emissions profile of a Region's energy supply is a Sustainability pillar behavior. Cost and security reviews would not introduce grid carbon intensity as a factor.

q: A customer stores files in Amazon S3. Under the shared responsibility model, the customer is responsible for:
options: Managing data classification and access permissions
Replacing failed disks in the S3 fleet
explain: AWS runs the S3 service (durability, physical security, patching). The customer owns what goes in it: classifying the data and controlling access via IAM and bucket policies.

q: A media site configures a CloudFront distribution and is asked what the term origin means in this setup. Which answer is correct?
options: The origin is the viewer's web browser
The origin is the Route 53 hosted zone for the domain
The origin is the edge location closest to the viewer
The origin is the source location, such as an S3 bucket or a web server, from which CloudFront fetches content to cache
explain: The origin is the authoritative source (an S3 bucket, EC2 instance, load balancer, or external server) that CloudFront pulls from on a cache miss. Edge locations are the cache points near viewers, browsers are the clients, and hosted zones only map names to the distribution.

q: A nonprofit adopts Amazon RDS and wonders who backs up the physical storage hardware failures. Which party handles hardware resilience for RDS?
explain: AWS operates the hardware and managed-service resilience for RDS. The nonprofit still manages database access, backups configuration, and its application data.

q: A claims process needs a human adjuster to approve payouts above a threshold, pausing mid-workflow for hours until the approval arrives, then branching to payment or denial steps. Which service models this stateful, branching workflow with a visual state machine?
options: AWS Lambda alone with no orchestration
explain: Step Functions state machines coordinate multi-step workflows with branching, retries, parallelism, and long pauses for human approval (via callback tasks), visualizing each state. Queues and topics move messages but do not model workflow state, and bare Lambda has no built-in orchestration across steps.

q: Two clinics merge their imaging workloads onto AWS and find the combined cost per stored scan is lower than either clinic achieved with its own small storage array. The discount comes from the provider's sheer purchasing volume. Which advantage is this?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explain: Lower unit costs driven by the provider's aggregate scale are massive economies of scale in action. Neither clinic changed its expense timing, capacity forecasting, or facility duties in the way the stem describes.

Basic Support, free with every account, includes 24/7 customer service for billing and account questions and requests such as service limit increases. Paid plans are needed for technical troubleshooting support, not billing help.
q: A small business needs help with a billing question and with increasing a service limit at no extra cost. Which Support plan already covers both needs?
A company sets a minimum length and symbol requirement for console passwords. Which IAM feature enforces this?
explain: An account password policy sets complexity, length, expiration, and reuse rules for IAM user console passwords. SCPs limit permissions, not password composition.

q: An auditor asks: "Which IAM user deleted the production S3 bucket last Tuesday?" Which service answers this?
explain: CloudTrail logs API activity — who did what, when. CloudWatch monitors metrics and alarms; Config tracks configuration compliance over time; GuardDuty detects threats.

q: A fleet of delivery-tracking servers boots from volumes that need balanced price and performance for a mix of small random reads and writes. Which EBS volume type is the general-purpose SSD choice for most such workloads?
explain: gp3 volumes are the general-purpose SSD workhorse for boot volumes, virtual desktops, and medium databases, with independently tunable IOPS and throughput. st1 and sc1 are HDD types for throughput or cold data, and io2 targets the most IOPS-critical workloads at higher cost.

q: Contributors on five continents upload hour-long video files to one S3 bucket and complain that transfers across the public internet are slow. Which S3 feature speeds up long-distance uploads by routing traffic through edge locations onto the AWS network?
explain: Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront edge locations as nearby upload entry points, then moves data over the optimized AWS backbone to the bucket. Replication copies data after upload, versioning tracks revisions, and Inventory reports on objects; none accelerates the upload path.

q: An auditor needs the AWS SOC 2 report and the PCI DSS attestation of compliance. Where are these downloaded on demand?
explain: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for downloading AWS compliance reports such as SOC and PCI attestations under NDA for auditors.

q: Thousands of records containing names and card numbers may be hidden somewhere in a company S3 estate. Which service discovers and classifies this sensitive data?
explain: Macie uses machine learning to discover sensitive data such as PII and payment data in S3, alerting when it is exposed or shared unexpectedly.

q: A pharmaceutical firm moves every workload, including its research analytics and customer portal, into AWS and decommissions its data center entirely. Which deployment model is this?
explain: Running everything on cloud infrastructure with nothing left on-premises is an all-in cloud deployment. Hybrid requires a mix, and on-premises means no cloud usage at all.

q: How are Availability Zones within a Region connected to each other?
options: By physical transport of backup tapes
Only by public internet connections via other continents
By low-latency links that support synchronous replication between them
They are not connected in any way
explain: AZs are linked by fast, low-latency connections, which is what makes synchronous standby designs like Multi-AZ databases practical. They are separate facilities but tightly networked.

q: An architect wants encryption key creation, rotation policies, and a tamper-evident log of every key use in one managed service. Which service is it?
explain: KMS creates and controls encryption keys, supports automatic rotation for customer managed keys, and logs every use in CloudTrail for auditing.

q: An architect designs a system so every API call is attributable to an identity, data is encrypted in transit and at rest, and access is reviewed quarterly. Which pillar is most directly addressed?
explain: Traceability, encryption, and access governance are Security pillar design areas. Cost, performance, and operations practices may benefit, but the listed controls are security controls.

q: How does responsibility shift when moving from EC2 to a managed service such as Amazon RDS?
options: All security becomes the customer job
The customer gains more patching duties
AWS takes on more tasks such as engine patching
explain: Managed services shift more of the stack to AWS, for example RDS engine and host patching, while the customer keeps data, access, and configuration responsibilities.

q: A software company localizes its help center into twelve languages and needs fast, neural machine translation of thousands of articles. Which service translates text between languages as a managed API?
explain: Translate is the managed neural machine translation service for localizing content at scale. Comprehend can detect a document's language and sentiment but does not translate it, Lex builds bots, and Kendra searches documents in their existing language.

q: Access patterns are unknown and change unpredictably over time. Which S3 storage class automatically moves data between tiers to optimize cost?
explain: Intelligent-Tiering monitors access and automatically shifts objects between frequent, infrequent, and archive tiers — no lifecycle rules to manage, ideal when patterns are unknown.
Retrieving data from Glacier storage classes incurs retrieval fees (and requests have their own charges), so Deep Archive is cheap to store but not free to read back. Ingress into AWS is free.
options: Listing the objects in a bucket console
q: Which action would incur an additional charge for data in Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

A startup expects database demand to be near zero most nights with brief bursts at lunch, and wants an Aurora configuration that scales capacity up and down and charges accordingly. Which option matches this bursty pattern?
options: RDS Multi-AZ with a permanently sized standby
Aurora read replicas fixed at fifteen
A single large provisioned Aurora instance running constantly
explain: Aurora Serverless automatically starts, scales, pauses, and resumes database capacity based on application demand, suiting intermittent workloads and billing for capacity actually used. Fixed provisioned instances and replicas charge for capacity held around the clock.

q: A team moves infrequently used data to cooler storage tiers and deletes data its retention policy no longer requires, reducing the storage hardware footprint behind its account. Which pillar does this serve?
explain: Shrinking the physical footprint of stored data by tiering and deleting what is no longer needed is a Sustainability practice. Retention rules also touch governance, but the footprint reduction is the sustainability angle.

q: Two Regions both meet a firm's legal and latency needs, so it picks the one where compute prices are lower for its instance family. Which factor decided the final choice?
options: The alphabetical order of Region names
The number of time zones covered
explain: When compliance and latency are already satisfied, price differences between Regions are a legitimate deciding factor. Region pricing genuinely varies by location and service.

q: A retailer migrates email to a third-party SaaS provider that runs on AWS. Compared with running EC2 mail servers, the retailer now has FEWER duties for which task?
options: Patching the mail server operating system
explain: Moving toward SaaS shifts server OS patching to the provider. The retailer still provisions mailboxes, classifies data, and enforces its internal access policies.

q: Discovery finds a reporting application that nobody has logged into for 18 months, and the business owner confirms it is safe to shut down instead of migrate. Which strategy applies?
explain: Decommissioning an unused application rather than spending effort migrating it is retire. Retiring such workloads often funds the rest of the migration program.

q: What is the recommended way to grant human users access to an AWS account?
options: Email access keys to each person
Create an individual IAM user for each person
Share a single IAM user among the team
explain: One IAM user per human enables individual accountability, least-privilege policies, and clean offboarding. The root user should be locked down with MFA and used only for tasks that require it.

q: A team defines how migrated services will be monitored, how incidents will be handled, and how service levels will be met day to day after go-live. Which CAF perspective is this?
explain: The Operations perspective concerns running cloud services day to day: monitoring, incident management, and service management. Platform builds the foundation; Operations runs on it.

q: An Australian gaming company complains that players in Sydney experience high ping to servers hosted in Virginia. Which Region-selection factor should drive moving the game servers closer?
explain: Distance drives latency, so placing the workload in a Region near the players addresses the ping problem. The stem gives no legal or feature-availability constraint.

q: A research group processes multi-terabyte genomics datasets with Apache Spark and Hadoop jobs that need a managed cluster framework they can tune themselves. Which service runs these big-data frameworks as managed clusters?
explain: EMR provisions managed Hadoop-ecosystem clusters (Spark, Hive, Presto, and friends) for large-scale data processing with deep configuration control. Glue is serverless ETL without cluster management, Athena is serverless SQL over S3, and QuickSight is business intelligence.

q: A SaaS product needs public TLS certificates for its load balancer that renew without manual purchase each year. Which service issues and renews them?
explain: Certificate Manager provisions public and private SSL and TLS certificates and handles automatic renewal for integrated services such as load balancers and CloudFront.

q: A support engineer only needs to view CloudWatch dashboards. Which policy approach follows best practice?
options: Attach a policy allowing all actions on all resources
Attach a read-only policy limited to the needed viewing actions
Create a new root user for support
explain: Scoped read-only access matches the job need and follows least privilege. Full administrator or wildcard policies grant dangerous, unnecessary permissions.

q: A company needs a dedicated private network connection from its data center to AWS with consistent bandwidth. Which service?
explain: Direct Connect = dedicated private fiber into AWS with consistent throughput and lower data-transfer rates (takes weeks to provision). Site-to-Site VPN runs over the public internet — faster to set up but variable performance.

q: A university department stores lecture recordings that students stream every day throughout each semester. Which S3 storage class matches this frequent, ongoing access pattern at standard performance?
explain: S3 Standard is built for frequently accessed data with 99.99 percent availability and millisecond retrieval. The Glacier classes trade instant access for lower archive cost, and One Zone-IA targets infrequent access in a single AZ.

q: A recently acquired subsidiary's systems cannot be touched until its contracts are renegotiated next year, so the migration plan leaves them in place. Which strategy is recorded for those systems?
explain: External constraints forcing a workload to stay put map to retain. The systems still run and serve users, which separates retain from retire.

On-Demand has no commitment and no upfront payment: you pay per second/minute of use, making it best for short-term, spiky, or unpredictable workloads. Commitments are what Reserved Instances and Savings Plans require.
q: Which EC2 pricing model requires NO upfront commitment and charges only for the compute capacity actually used?
A biotech startup pivots its data platform to a new analysis approach in a single week because it can stand up entirely different resources immediately. Which advantage supports the pivot?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explain: The ability to change direction quickly because resources are available on demand is increased speed and agility. The pivot speed, not billing shape or facility work, is the deciding detail.

q: Data crossing the public internet between a remote office and an AWS application should be protected with which mechanism?
options: An unencrypted HTTP connection with strong passwords
explain: TLS over HTTPS encrypts data in transit across untrusted networks. Passwords, versioning, and snapshots do not encrypt the traffic itself.

q: Which pricing principle means heavy users of a tiered-priced service pay a lower rate per unit for later units than for the first units?
options: Pay less with more volume through tiered pricing
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Pay less when you reserve capacity
explain: Tiered pricing lowers the per-unit rate as volume grows, one of AWS's stated pricing principles. Reserving is a separate principle based on commitment rather than volume tiers.

q: A compliance officer asks how a workload can privately connect to an AWS service's API through an elastic network interface with a private IP inside the VPC, rather than through a route to a gateway endpoint. Which technology provides interface-style private connectivity?
explain: PrivateLink creates interface VPC endpoints: ENIs with private IPs inside your subnets that front AWS services, partner services, or your own services in other VPCs. CloudFront and Global Accelerator are public-edge services, and an internet gateway is by definition the public path.

q: A team inherits a VPC and must document, for every subnet, where traffic for 0.0.0.0/0 is sent. Which VPC component holds that destination decision for each subnet?
explain: Route tables associated with each subnet define where packets for each destination range go, including the default 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway, NAT gateway, or other target. Security groups filter traffic, DHCP options set resolver settings, and endpoint policies govern one endpoint's permissions.

q: Under GDPR, a company using AWS Regions outside Europe for EU customer data must consider what?
options: Only the cost of cross-Region transfer
Data transfer and residency requirements for personal data leaving the EU
explain: GDPR restricts and conditions transfers of EU personal data, so Region choice and transfer mechanisms matter. Keeping data in EU Regions is the simplest residency pattern.

q: A team grants engineers only the permissions each role needs, encrypts stored customer data, and logs who accessed sensitive records. Which pillar gathers these practices?
explain: Identity and access management, data protection through encryption, and traceability of access are all Security pillar topics. The other pillars do not organize these particular controls.

q: A developer comparing platform services asks which claim about PaaS she should trust. Which claim is the trustworthy one?
options: The customer receives only a finished application with no code deployment
The customer patches the hypervisor and host operating systems
The provider manages the underlying infrastructure and runtime while the customer deploys and configures its own applications
explain: PaaS sits between IaaS and SaaS: customers bring applications and data, providers run everything underneath including runtimes. Finished-application consumption is SaaS, and PaaS platforms do scale apps.

q: Which duty does AWS retain even when a customer uses a fully managed analytics service?
options: Physical security and environmental controls for facilities
explain: Facility physical and environmental controls are never transferred to the customer. Data classification, IAM policies, and retention decisions remain customer owned.

q: VPC peering connections are non-transitive. What should a company with dozens of VPCs use for central, transitive routing between them?
explain: Transit Gateway = hub-and-spoke transitive routing for VPCs and on-premises networks. Peering is 1:1 and non-transitive, so N VPCs would need N·(N−1)/2 peerings — unmanageable at scale.

q: A fintech startup labels its transaction records as confidential, internal, or public. Whose job is this classification under the shared responsibility model?
explain: Data classification is always the customer responsibility. AWS protects the infrastructure that stores data but does not know the business sensitivity of customer content.

q: A photo site's capacity rises automatically for a viral post and releases servers when the surge passes, with no engineer touching a console. Which design principle is at work?
explain: Automatic provisioning and release tied to real demand is elasticity as a design principle. Permanently holding peak capacity is the legacy pattern elasticity replaces.

q: A team exposes several Lambda functions as a REST API and needs throttling, API keys, and request validation at the front door. Which service sits in front of the functions?
explain: API Gateway is the managed front door for APIs: throttling, API keys, validation, and usage plans. An ALB routes HTTP traffic but lacks API-management features; CloudFront is a CDN; Route 53 is DNS.

q: Which TWO pairings of regulation and workload are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: HIPAA and a hospital patient portal handling health records
GDPR and a game for children with no personal data at all
PCI DSS and a checkout service processing credit cards
FedRAMP and a private photo-sharing hobby app
explain: HIPAA governs health records workloads and PCI DSS governs card processing. FedRAMP targets government systems and GDPR targets personal data processing.

q: What does SSE-C mean for S3 encryption?
options: The customer provides the key with each request and S3 does not store it
S3 creates and rotates the keys
explain: With SSE-C the customer supplies the encryption key on each request over TLS; S3 uses it and does not retain it, placing full key custody on the customer.

q: A support team needs to give one customer a download link to a private invoice stored in S3 that works for the next 24 hours and then stops working, without making the bucket public. Which mechanism provides this?
options: Copying the invoice to a public folder
Changing the bucket policy to allow everyone
A presigned URL generated for the object
explain: A presigned URL grants time-limited access to a specific private object using the generator's permissions, expiring automatically. Making the bucket public or copying to a public location would expose the invoice permanently, and website hosting does not create expiring private links.

q: A contractor needs console access for a single project. What is the recommended identity approach?
options: Create a unique IAM user or federated identity for the contractor
Use the root user with MFA shared by the team
Give the contractor administrator access permanently
explain: Every person should have a unique identity so actions are attributable and access can be revoked individually. Shared logins and permanent admin access violate best practice.

q: An events platform is busy three weekends a month and nearly idle on weekdays. Which economic approach fits it best on AWS?
options: Buy capacity for the busiest weekend and run it continuously
Purchase a second data center for overflow
Keep weekday resources running to avoid configuration work
Provision for weekend demand and scale down or stop resources on weekdays
explain: Matching provisioned capacity to a repeating demand pattern avoids paying for peak resources during idle weekdays. Running peak capacity continuously recreates the waste cloud economics is meant to remove.

q: A team is designing encryption for a new workload. Which TWO decisions are the customer responsibility? (Select TWO.)
options: Choosing whether data at rest is encrypted and with which key type
Selecting TLS for data in transit to the application
explain: Customers choose at-rest encryption and key types and decide on TLS for transit. KMS hardware patching and data center operations belong to AWS.

q: An application needs Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS routing with host- and path-based rules. Which load balancer?
explain: ALB operates at Layer 7, routing by host, path, headers, and query strings — built for modern HTTP apps and containers. NLB is Layer 4 for extreme performance; GWLB chains third-party virtual appliances.

q: A consultancy asks who secures the AWS management console infrastructure itself against attacks on the service endpoint. Which party does that?
explain: The AWS service endpoints and console infrastructure are operated and secured by AWS. Customers secure their own credentials and how they sign in to that console.

q: A product team needs to query product records by exact product ID and by exact SKU, each in well under a millisecond at peak, with documents that vary in fields from item to item. Which database family on AWS is purpose-shaped for this access style?
options: Key-value and document NoSQL, such as DynamoDB
explain: Exact-key lookups over flexible, self-describing items at extreme scale define the key-value and document NoSQL pattern that DynamoDB serves. Graph stores optimize relationships, ledgers optimize verifiable history, and warehouses optimize large analytical scans rather than point lookups.

q: A gaming company based in Europe notices players in Australia suffer high latency on its European servers. Which global-infrastructure move most directly cuts the Australian players' latency?
options: Deploy the game servers in an Asia-Pacific Region close to those players
Increase the size of the European EC2 instances
Enable S3 Versioning on the asset bucket
Add edge locations for DNS lookups only
explain: Latency falls when compute sits physically near users, so adding a deployment in a nearby Region is the direct fix for distant players. Bigger instances do not shorten the network path, DNS edges do not host the game, and versioning protects objects rather than accelerating gameplay.

q: A company needs continuous proof that no S3 bucket is publicly accessible, plus a history of configuration changes. Which service provides this?
explain: Config records resource configuration changes and Config rules continuously evaluate compliance (e.g., "no public buckets"). CloudTrail audits API calls; CloudWatch alarms on metrics; Macie finds PII in S3.

q: A platform team wants a rule that continuously flags any EBS volume that is not encrypted and any S3 bucket without versioning, across all its accounts, so violations surface the day they appear. Which service's rules engine performs this continuous compliance evaluation?
explain: Config rules evaluate resource configurations continuously (or on change) against desired conditions like encryption and versioning, marking resources compliant or noncompliant. Metric alarms watch numbers, CloudTrail queries past API events, and GuardDuty hunts threats rather than configuration policy.

q: A news app must send breaking-news push notifications to millions of iOS and Android devices within seconds. Which service is built for this fan-out?
explain: SNS is pub/sub push messaging — one publish fans out to mobile push, SMS, email, and HTTP endpoints. SQS is a pull queue between components (consumers poll); SES sends email; EventBridge routes events between AWS/SaaS sources.
A 3-year term with All Upfront payment yields the deepest Reserved Instance discount (up to 72%). Partial and No Upfront options trade a smaller discount for less cash committed at purchase.
q: For a Reserved Instance, which term and payment option combination gives the LARGEST discount versus On-Demand pricing?
Which TWO pricing models require a 1- or 3-year commitment in exchange for lower prices? (Select TWO.)
explain: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans both trade a 1- or 3-year commitment for significant discounts. On-Demand and Spot have no commitment; Dedicated Hosts can be bought on-demand or reserved, but the host itself isn't the commitment vehicle.

Basic Support is free for all AWS accounts. It includes 24/7 customer service for billing and account questions, access to documentation and forums, the seven core Trusted Advisor checks, and the AWS Personal Health Dashboard.
q: Which AWS Support plan is free and included with every AWS account?
Which statement correctly contrasts all-in cloud with hybrid deployment?
options: Hybrid runs everything on cloud infrastructure, while all-in splits workloads
All-in cloud requires a company data center to remain open
All-in cloud runs everything on cloud infrastructure, while hybrid keeps some workloads on-premises connected to the cloud
Hybrid deployments cannot use AWS storage services
explain: The distinction is placement: all-in means no premises workloads remain, hybrid deliberately retains some. Hybrid environments commonly use AWS storage through gateways, so the last option is false.

q: Which TWO statements about AWS CloudTrail are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: Trails can deliver logs to S3 for long-term retention
It records API activity including caller, action, and time
It evaluates whether resources meet configuration rules
It discovers PII inside S3 objects
explain: CloudTrail is the API audit log and trails persist it to S3. Configuration rule evaluation is AWS Config and PII discovery is Amazon Macie.

q: Which TWO actions are IAM best practices for a new AWS account? (Select TWO.)
options: Create long-lived access keys for every application
Grant least privilege permissions to users and roles
Enable MFA for the root user
explain: Enabling MFA on root and applying least privilege are foundational IAM best practices. Sharing root credentials and scattering long-lived keys increase risk sharply.

q: Which pillar concerns a workload performing its intended function correctly and consistently, and recovering quickly when failures occur?
explain: Correct, consistent operation plus rapid recovery from failure defines the Reliability pillar. The definition is about dependability of function, not spend, protection, or speed.

q: A brokerage is lifting an existing message-driven application that speaks the ActiveMQ protocol and JMS APIs; rewriting it to native AWS messaging would take a year the business does not have. Which service runs a managed broker compatible with the existing protocols?
explain: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker for ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ, letting applications using standard protocols like JMS and AMQP migrate without code rewrites. SQS, SNS, and EventBridge use AWS-native APIs and semantics, which is precisely the rewrite the brokerage wants to avoid.

q: Before a product launch of unknown popularity, a toy maker avoids buying servers for the highest imaginable sales figure and instead plans to add resources only if orders materialize. Which advantage is it relying on?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
explain: Planning to obtain capacity as real demand appears, instead of pre-buying for a guessed maximum, is stop guessing capacity. No new market, facility closure, or release-speed claim is made in the stem.
The AWS Pricing Calculator builds pre-deployment estimates for services and configurations so teams can model costs before spending. Cost Explorer analyzes costs that have already been incurred.
q: Before deploying anything, a team wants to estimate what a proposed architecture will cost per month. Which tool should they use?
"Undifferentiated heavy lifting" refers to:
options: Routine IT work such as racking servers and patching that does not differentiate the business
Tasks that differentiate a company from its competitors
explain: Undifferentiated heavy lifting = the muck of running IT (racking, stacking, patching, power) that every company does but no customer pays for. The cloud's pitch: stop doing it and focus on what differentiates you.

q: A branch office needs an encrypted connection to its VPC working by tomorrow morning for a pilot project; there is no time to provision dedicated circuits. Which connectivity option can be established this quickly over existing internet service?
explain: A Site-to-Site VPN rides the public internet with IPsec encryption and can be configured in hours, making it the fast-start option. Direct Connect involves a dedicated circuit that typically takes weeks to provision, Snowball is data transfer hardware, and an internet gateway alone creates no tunnel.

q: An administrator discovers that interrupted multipart uploads are quietly consuming S3 storage and budget. Which S3 feature can automatically abort incomplete multipart uploads after a set number of days?
explain: A Lifecycle rule can abort incomplete multipart uploads after a defined period and can also expire objects and old versions. Versioning keeps versions rather than cleaning uploads, and access points and presigned URLs control access, not storage cleanup.

q: Financial records must be retained unchangeable for 7 years — not even an administrator may delete or alter them early. Which S3 feature enforces this?
explain: Object Lock in compliance mode makes objects WORM (write once, read many) — nobody, not even the root user, can delete them before retention expires. Versioning keeps old copies but doesn't block deletes; encryption and bucket policies don't enforce retention.

q: A student wants to experiment with 750 hours of EC2 and 5 GB of S3 storage per month at no charge during the first year of a new account. Which makes this possible?
explain: The Free Tier gives new accounts 12 months of free usage allowances (750 EC2 hours/month, 5 GB S3, and more). Savings Plans require a usage commitment; consolidated billing pools spend across accounts; Spot is cheap but not free.

q: A junior administrator prefers clicking through wizards, an automation engineer prefers scripted commands, and an application needs to call AWS from its own Java code. Which trio of access methods maps to these three needs in order?
options: Management Console, AWS CLI, and AWS SDKs
AWS CLI, Management Console, and AWS SDKs
AWS SDKs, Management Console, and AWS CLI
Management Console, AWS SDKs, and AWS CLI
explain: The console is the browser-based graphical interface for manual work, the CLI drives AWS from scripts and terminals, and SDKs let application code in languages like Java call AWS APIs directly. Any other ordering mismatches at least one person's stated need.

q: An administrator stores database connection strings and feature flags centrally so applications fetch the current values at startup instead of hard-coding them in deployment artifacts. Which Systems Manager feature is this central configuration store?
explain: Systems Manager Parameter Store provides secure, versioned storage for configuration data and secrets references that applications and automation retrieve at runtime. Run Command executes fleet commands, Inventory catalogs installed software, and Patch Manager schedules OS patching; none is a configuration value store.

q: Which TWO components must exist for instances with public IP addresses in a VPC to exchange traffic with the internet in both directions? (Select TWO.)
options: An internet gateway attached to the VPC
A route in the subnet route table pointing to the internet gateway
A NAT gateway in the same subnet
A Direct Connect connection to the VPC
explain: Two-way public internet access needs both an internet gateway attached to the VPC and a subnet route directing internet-bound traffic to it, plus public IPs on the instances. A NAT gateway serves private subnets for outbound-only access, and Direct Connect is a private link to on-premises networks.

q: A team wants an email alert when monthly spend reaches 80% of its $1,000 budget. Which service provides this?
explain: Budgets tracks against thresholds and notifies (and its budget actions can auto-remediate). Cost Anomaly Detection uses ML to flag unusual spikes, not fixed thresholds. Cost Explorer visualizes past spend; Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks.

q: A cloud center of excellence publishes the approved architecture patterns and infrastructure-as-code modules all teams must reuse. Which CAF perspective produced these?
explain: Reusable architecture patterns and platform engineering standards come from the Platform perspective. Operations consumes those patterns to run services; it does not define the platform.

q: An application team compares running MySQL themselves on EC2 versus using RDS. Which operational task does RDS remove from the team?
options: Installing, patching, and backing up the database software
explain: RDS is a managed service: AWS installs and patches the database engine, automates backups, and offers managed failover, while schema design, queries, and indexing remain application responsibilities. On EC2 the team would own every one of the operational tasks as well.

q: During a hardware maintenance window, AWS needs to replace a faulty physical host that is running customer EC2 instances. Who performs the host replacement?
options: The customer's IT team working with AWS guidance
The customer, during their own maintenance window
explain: Physical hosts and the virtualization layer are security OF the cloud — always AWS's responsibility. Customers handle security IN the cloud: their data, IAM, guest OS patching, and firewall rules.

Consolidated Billing in AWS Organizations combines usage across accounts into one bill, letting the organization share volume discounts and Reserved Instance/Savings Plans pricing benefits, while each account still pays only for its own usage share.
options: Every account pays the highest member's rates
Accounts lose their individual cost visibility
All Reserved Instances must be surrendered
One bill with combined usage counting toward volume discount tiers
q: What is the main billing benefit of AWS Organizations Consolidated Billing?
What is the safest default when creating a new IAM user who will use the console?
options: Share the team password policy document as access
Enable only billing access for everyone
Grant administrator access until their role is clear
Grant no permissions initially and add only what the job requires
explain: Starting with no access and adding permissions as needed enforces least privilege from day one and avoids standing excess privilege while roles are clarified.

q: A developer asks which service can automatically rotate RDS database credentials without downtime coordination in code. Which answer is correct?
options: AWS Secrets Manager with rotation enabled
explain: Secrets Manager supports automatic rotation for RDS and other database credentials using managed rotation, updating both the secret and the database together.

q: In CAF, one perspective owns the link between cloud spending and expected business value, including how that value will be quantified. Which perspective is it?
explain: Aligning IT strategy and investment with business outcomes is the Business perspective. Governance tracks and controls value delivery, but setting the value agenda is Business perspective work.

q: An organization wants Macie to evaluate all of its S3 buckets and report where personally identifiable information is stored. What will Macie produce?
options: Findings identifying sensitive data types and locations in S3
New IAM passwords for data owners
explain: Macie jobs scan S3 objects and produce findings that name the sensitive data types found, such as PII, and where they reside, to drive remediation.

q: Securing the global network infrastructure connecting AWS Regions is the responsibility of which party?
explain: The global network infrastructure, Regions, and Availability Zones are operated by AWS as part of security of the cloud. Customers secure what they build on top.

q: A developer asks why the team's cache sometimes serves a slightly old product price for a few seconds after an update. The architect explains the cache is filled only when data is requested, after a miss reaches the database. Which caching strategy is in use?
options: Read replication of the full database
explain: Lazy loading populates the cache on demand: a miss fetches from the database and stores the result, which is simple and efficient but can serve stale data briefly if the underlying record changes. Write-through updates the cache on every write, and replication or standby patterns describe database availability, not cache population.

q: Which approach best mitigates large-scale DDoS attacks against a web application?
options: Run the app on a single large EC2 instance
Open all security group rules to absorb traffic
Serve traffic through CloudFront with AWS Shield protection
explain: CloudFront's global edge network absorbs attack traffic far from the origin, and Shield provides DDoS mitigation — scale plus protection. A single instance is a single point of failure; open security groups invite attack.

q: A company must prove its web firewall rules are consistently applied in every member account and flag accounts missing them. Which service enforces that consistency?
explain: Firewall Manager uses policies to require and audit WAF and firewall configurations across organization accounts, remediating accounts that fall out of compliance.

q: A company expects large, sophisticated DDoS attacks and wants 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team plus cost protection if an attack causes scaling. Which should it use?
explain: Shield Advanced = paid protection with 24/7 DRT access, enhanced detection, and cost protection against attack-driven scaling. Shield Standard is free and automatic but has no DRT or cost protection; WAF is an application-layer firewall (SQLi/XSS), not a DDoS service; security groups are instance firewalls.
EC2 Savings Plans commit to usage of a specific instance family in a chosen Region, while Compute Savings Plans are broader, applying across instance families, Regions, and even Fargate and Lambda.
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans commit to an instance family in a specific Region
Compute Savings Plans apply only to one instance family in one Region
Savings Plans require full upfront payment
Savings Plans cannot be combined with On-Demand usage
q: Which statement about AWS Savings Plans is correct?
A solutions architect explains Aurora to a client whose team knows RDS well. Which statement highlights a genuine Aurora difference the client should plan around?
options: Aurora is a NoSQL key-value store with no SQL support
Aurora is AWS-built, separates compute from a distributed storage layer, and supports up to 15 low-lag replicas
Aurora stores its data on the instance store of one EC2 host
Aurora runs only a single instance with no replication
explain: Aurora re-architects the relational database: compute instances sit over a distributed, self-healing storage layer replicated across three AZs, and up to 15 replicas read with minimal lag. It remains fully SQL (MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible) and is neither single-instance nor tied to one host's ephemeral disk.
