The AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) is the most comprehensive billing dataset, with line-item detail by hour/day/month, delivered as files into an S3 bucket for analysis with tools like Athena or QuickSight.
q: Which AWS billing report provides the MOST detailed, granular line-item billing data and can be delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket for analysis?
An engineer wants to check whether a scheduled EC2 maintenance event will affect their specific instances. Where should they look?
options: The AWS Health Dashboard (Personal Health Dashboard)
explain: The Personal Health Dashboard shows events affecting YOUR resources, like scheduled maintenance on your instances. The public Service Health Dashboard shows regional service status; CloudTrail logs API calls; Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks.

q: Which statement about economies of scale in cloud pricing is correct?
options: Each customer gets lower prices by using fewer services
Unit costs rise as the provider grows because of complexity
Small private data centers always beat cloud unit prices
A provider serving millions of customers can achieve lower unit costs than a single small data center
explain: Aggregated demand gives the provider purchasing and operational efficiencies a lone small facility cannot match, producing lower unit costs for customers.

q: Which option lets a team run containers on ECS or EKS without managing the underlying EC2 servers?
explain: Fargate is serverless compute for containers — no EC2 instances to patch or scale; you pay per vCPU/memory used. With EC2 launch type, you manage the cluster's servers yourself.

q: A company keeps a minimal version of its critical systems always running in a second Region — just enough to take over and scale up quickly after a disaster. Which disaster recovery strategy is this?
explain: Pilot light = a minimal core (like a pilot light) always on in the recovery Region, ready to scale up — the middle ground on cost vs. recovery speed. Backup and restore is cheapest but slowest; warm standby keeps a scaled-down full copy; multi-site runs full production in both Regions.

Enterprise Support targets a response of less than 15 minutes for business- and mission-critical systems down. Enterprise On-Ramp targets less than 30 minutes for business-critical outages, and Business targets less than 1 hour for production down.
q: A mission-critical production system is completely down. Which Support plan guarantees an initial response in less than 15 minutes for this severity?
A company wants its on-premises backup software to write to S3 while keeping frequently accessed data cached locally for fast restores. Which service connects on-premises storage to AWS this way?
explain: Storage Gateway is a hybrid storage service — a virtual appliance on-premises that caches locally and tiers to S3. DataSync is a migration/sync tool; Snowball is a physical transfer device; Direct Connect is a private network link, not storage.

q: A media company deploys with Elastic Beanstalk and AWS handles platform patching. What does the company still own?
options: Its application code, data, and IAM access decisions
explain: Beanstalk reduces server management and AWS handles platform patching, but code, data classification, and who can access the environment stay with the customer.

q: A company replaces its self-run webmail servers with a subscription email application that staff open in a browser. Nothing about the application is hosted by the company. This is an example of what?
explain: Using a provider's complete email application by subscription is SaaS, the same pattern as the classic repurchase migration. No infrastructure or development platform is being consumed.

AWS IQ lets customers find, hire, and pay AWS Certified experts for on-demand project work. AWS Marketplace sells third-party software, and Managed Services operates infrastructure on an ongoing basis.
q: A customer needs an AWS expert for a short, project-based engagement (for example, help setting up a workload) and wants to hire through AWS. Which service connects customers with certified AWS freelancers and experts?
An admin attaches a policy to a role but workloads still cannot perform the action. The role also needs permission to be assumed by the workload. That permission lives in which policy?
explain: Even with a permissions policy, a principal can only obtain the role if the trust policy lists that principal as allowed to assume it via sts:AssumeRole.

q: A city library system pays less per gigabyte for archived catalogs after migrating, even though its own usage did not grow, because the provider's overall scale keeps driving unit prices down. Which advantage applies?
options: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Prices falling because of the provider's growing aggregate scale, not the customer's own growth, is the massive economies of scale advantage. Nothing in the stem involves capacity forecasts, facilities, or new countries.

q: A team sets recovery time and recovery point objectives for its order database and rehearses restoring it from backups twice a year. Which pillar do these objectives belong to?
explain: RTO and RPO targets and tested backup restoration are Reliability topics, since they quantify how the workload withstands and recovers from disruption. Security protects data but does not set recovery objectives.

q: A retailer wants a single service to require MFA delete on versioned buckets and check that setting continuously across accounts. Which service reports this posture check?
options: AWS Security Hub with config-backed standards checks
explain: Security Hub standards include checks backed by AWS Config rules, such as S3 MFA delete and other posture controls, reported centrally across accounts.

q: A clinic uses Amazon EC2 to host a records viewer. Who must harden and configure the guest operating system?
explain: Hardening and configuring the guest OS on EC2 is security in the cloud. AWS secures everything below the guest OS, including hardware and virtualization.

q: A company migrates its web tier to Elastic Beanstalk to shed server management but keeps the same application code and database schema. Which strategy is this?
explain: Changing the hosting platform to a managed one while the application itself stays essentially the same is replatforming. Refactoring would involve redesigning the application, which did not happen.
Business Support starts at $100 per month (or a percentage of monthly AWS usage, whichever is greater). Developer starts at $29, Enterprise On-Ramp at $5,500, and Enterprise at $15,000.
q: What is the minimum monthly price of the AWS Business Support plan?
What does a SOC 3 report offer compared with a SOC 2 report?
options: A detailed restricted report with test results
A billing summary for the account
A public summary of controls for general distribution
A list of AWS data center addresses
explain: SOC 3 is a general-use public summary based on the same trust services criteria as SOC 2, whose detailed report is restricted to parties under NDA.

q: An analyst needs to run ad-hoc SQL queries directly against CSV log files in S3, without loading them into a database or managing any servers. Which service does this?
explain: Athena is serverless: point it at S3 and run SQL immediately, paying per query. Redshift is a provisioned data warehouse (great for petabyte OLAP, overkill here); RDS is a managed relational database you must load; EMR runs Hadoop/Spark clusters you manage. Domain 4 — Billing, Pricing, and Support

q: What is an Availability Zone?
options: A content caching location at the network edge
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within a Region
explain: Each AZ is one or more discrete data centers with independent power, cooling, and networking. AZs in a Region are physically separated so a disaster in one is unlikely to affect the others.

q: A game studio prototypes a matchmaking feature on Friday, tests it with players over the weekend, and discards it on Monday after poor feedback, all without a procurement process. Which advantage enabled this fast experiment cycle?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Increase speed and agility means resources and experiments happen in minutes rather than through weeks of purchasing and installation. The studio iterated and abandoned an idea quickly, which is the agility advantage.

q: A consumer fitness app needs sign-up, sign-in, and password recovery for millions of app users. Which service provides customer identity for the app?
explain: Cognito provides user pools for customer-facing sign-up and sign-in, plus identity pools for AWS access, and is distinct from workforce SSO in Identity Center.

q: A critical production workload will run for just two weeks and cannot tolerate any interruption. Which EC2 pricing model is the best fit?
explain: On-Demand = pay by the second with no commitment and no interruptions — ideal for short, critical runs. Spot can be interrupted; Reserved Instances and Savings Plans need 1–3 year commitments, which makes no sense for two weeks.

q: A startup notices its EC2 instance has an outdated application library it installed. Who must update that library?
options: The AMI publisher in all cases
explain: Software the customer installs above the guest OS, including application libraries and dependencies, is the customer responsibility to maintain and patch.

q: A data platform team raises average fleet utilization from 15 percent to 60 percent and prefers managed services that scale to zero, specifically to cut the carbon footprint per query. Which pillar is it prioritizing?
explain: Utilization improvements chosen to reduce environmental impact per unit of work are Sustainability decisions. Cost may fall too, but the stem states the environmental goal explicitly.

q: An IAM user has one policy allowing S3 access and another policy explicitly denying it. What is the result?
options: Allowed, because Allow is listed first
Denied, because an explicit deny always overrides any allow
Allowed, but only during business hours
explain: Policy evaluation logic: an explicit Deny beats any Allow, always. This is how guardrails work — even an administrator's Allow can't override a Deny.

q: Which TWO services help a company monitor and control its AWS costs? (Select TWO.)
explain: Budgets alerts (and acts) on spend thresholds; Cost Explorer visualizes and analyzes spend with rightsizing recommendations. Artifact serves compliance reports; Inspector scans for vulnerabilities; Config tracks resource configuration compliance.

q: A school district launches a new enrollment portal without knowing whether 2,000 or 20,000 parents will register on day one, and simply obtains more capacity if registrations surge. Which advantage removes its upfront forecasting burden?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: Stop guessing capacity means you no longer provision for a predicted peak that may be wrong in either direction. The district can respond to real registrations rather than a months-old estimate.

q: What is the purpose of the IAM credential report?
options: To list users and the status of passwords, MFA, and access keys
explain: The credential report is a downloadable inventory of all users in the account with credential status, including MFA enablement and access key rotation details.

q: A developer needs an API key for a third-party service rotated every week and retrieved securely at runtime. Which AWS service should hold that key?
explain: Secrets Manager stores third-party API keys and other secrets, controls retrieval through IAM, logs use, and supports rotation through Lambda where needed.

q: A newly regulated subsidiary must be onboarded into the company's AWS estate with guardrails, centralized logging, and account baselines applied from day one, using the same landing-zone pattern as every other subsidiary. Which service sets up and governs this multi-account landing zone?
explain: Control Tower automates landing-zone setup across accounts: it applies preventive and detective guardrails, central logging, and account factory baselines through Organizations. Service Catalog governs product launches inside accounts, Macie classifies S3 data, and Firewall Manager centralizes firewall rules rather than account foundations.

q: A European bank must keep EU customer data subject to GDPR while expanding analytics. Which AWS decision most directly supports data residency?
options: Using the root user for analytics jobs
Choosing EU Regions for storage and processing of that data
explain: Processing and storing EU personal data in EU Regions supports residency commitments under GDPR. The other choices either spread data globally or weaken governance.

q: A social app must automatically flag uploaded photos that contain prohibited content and also detect faces to suggest photo tags. Which managed AI service analyzes images and video for objects, faces, and unsafe content?
explain: Rekognition performs image and video analysis: object and scene detection, facial analysis, celebrity recognition, and content moderation. Textract extracts text from documents, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Translate converts text between languages.

q: A startup needs business-hours email access to cloud support engineers at the lowest cost. Which plan?
explain: Developer ($29/month minimum) adds business-hours email support with under-24-hour response for general guidance. Basic is free but has no technical support; Business ($100/month) adds 24/7 phone/chat.

q: A German company must ensure customer data never leaves the EU to comply with data protection laws. What should it do?
options: Use any Region, since all AWS Regions follow EU law
Store and process the data in an EU AWS Region
explain: Data residency is controlled by Region choice — keep the data in an EU Region and it stays in the EU. Encryption protects data but doesn't control geography; CloudFront caches content globally (the opposite of residency); Regions follow the laws of their geography.

AWS Budgets supports alerting to email subscribers and to Amazon SNS topics (which can fan out to Lambda, SQS, and chat tools). CloudTrail records API calls; it is not a notification channel for budgets.
options: Email recipients and Amazon SNS topics
Only postal mail to the account address
q: Which notification channels can AWS Budgets use when a threshold is crossed?
A firm's only involvement with its accounting software is entering data and setting approval rules; the vendor hosts, patches, and upgrades the application. Which model is this and why?
options: IaaS, because the vendor owns the data center
PaaS, because the firm writes the application code
IaaS, because the firm manages the servers
SaaS, because the vendor operates the entire application stack
explain: When the vendor hosts, patches, and upgrades a finished application, it is SaaS regardless of whose data center is involved. The firm writes no code and manages no servers.

q: A video platform expects its container fleet to grow from 10 to 400 tasks during a championship match and shrink afterward, with no manual steps. Which capability of EC2 Auto Scaling and container services delivers this behavior?
options: Static provisioning of the peak fleet size year-round
Manual approval workflows for every new task
Automatic scaling of capacity in response to demand signals
Scheduled termination of tasks at midnight
explain: Auto Scaling adjusts capacity automatically as demand signals change, adding resources for the match peak and removing them afterward to control cost. Static peak provisioning wastes money, and manual approvals or fixed termination schedules do not follow demand.

q: Which provides automatic DDoS protection for AWS resources at no additional charge?
explain: Shield Standard is on by default for all AWS customers at no extra cost, absorbing common network-layer DDoS attacks. Shield Advanced is the paid tier with the DDoS Response Team and cost protection.

AWS positions Business Support for production workloads: it adds 24/7 phone/chat support, response under 1 hour for production-down cases, the full Trusted Advisor check set, and the Support API over the Developer tier.
q: Which AWS Support plan does AWS recommend for customers running production workloads who need full Trusted Advisor checks and 24/7 technical support?

A team replaces always-on servers for a batch report with a pay-per-run design, so the report that runs ten minutes a day no longer consumes a full day of compute charges. Which pillar benefits most directly?
explain: Moving to consumption pricing so you stop paying for idle hours is a Cost Optimization pattern. The primary win stated is eliminating paid idle time.

q: A SaaS vendor wants to reassure prospects by referencing AWS SOC 2. What is the honest scope of that claim?
options: The vendor product is SOC 2 certified
The AWS platform controls were audited; the vendor still needs its own SOC 2 for its product claims
Artifact issues SOC 2 to any account automatically
SOC 2 applies only to billing systems
explain: Referencing the AWS SOC 2 covers the infrastructure layer only. A vendor claiming product-level SOC 2 needs its own audit of its own controls.
On-Demand Linux instances are billed per second with a 60-second minimum, so short-lived jobs only pay for seconds actually consumed. Reserved pricing is a commitment model, not a per-second meter.
options: Per-hour billing rounded up to full hours
q: How are On-Demand EC2 Linux instances billed for a 90-second test run?
A university runs Lambda functions for grade processing and a flaw is found in the managed Lambda runtime environment. Who remediates it?
explain: For Lambda, AWS manages the execution environment, runtime patching, and hosts. The university manages function code, dependencies it includes, and IAM permissions.

q: Which TWO costs should be included when computing the total cost of ownership of an on-premises data center? (Select TWO.)
options: Cooling and power for the facility
The AWS charges of a competitor company
explain: Power, cooling, and maintenance labor are genuine ownership costs that belong in TCO. A competitor's bills and the company's own sales revenue are not costs of running the facility.

q: Why would a company choose CloudHSM over KMS for a particular workload?
options: Regulations require dedicated single-tenant HSM hardware under customer control
It needs to store database passwords
It wants a central findings dashboard
explain: CloudHSM is chosen when compliance demands dedicated HSM hardware and full customer control of keys, accepting more operational responsibility than managed KMS.

q: An event-driven platform collects events from its own microservices, from partner SaaS applications, and from other AWS services into one place where rules route each event type to different targets. Which service is this central event bus?
explain: EventBridge is the serverless event bus that ingests events from AWS services, custom applications, and SaaS partners, then routes them by rules to targets like Lambda and SQS. SQS is a point-to-point queue, Kinesis Video handles video ingestion, and Batch runs batch compute jobs.

q: A genomics lab runs fault-tolerant batch jobs that can be interrupted and restarted at any time without harm. Which EC2 pricing model minimizes its cost?
explain: Spot Instances use spare capacity at up to 90% off — perfect for interruptible, fault-tolerant batch work. On-Demand has no discount; Reserved needs a 1–3 year commitment; Dedicated Hosts are physical servers for compliance/licensing, not savings.

q: Which TWO pairings of service to purpose are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: CloudTrail: caching web content at edge locations
CloudWatch: monitoring metrics, logs, and alarms for performance and operations
CloudTrail: recording API activity for governance and auditing who did what
CloudWatch: converting database schemas between engines
explain: The canonical split: CloudWatch watches how systems behave, CloudTrail watches who did what through the API. Schema conversion belongs to SCT, and edge caching belongs to CloudFront, so those pairings are the planted errors.
The AWS Knowledge Center contains Support-created articles and videos answering the most common questions and issues. AWS Artifact is for compliance reports, not troubleshooting how-tos.
q: Which resource provides answers to common technical questions, how-to guidance, and troubleshooting articles maintained by AWS Support?
A fintech must demonstrate PCI DSS compliance of the AWS platform portion of its environment to its assessor. Which document from Artifact is relevant?
options: AWS PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance
explain: The AWS PCI Attestation of Compliance in Artifact documents the compliance status of AWS services in scope, which assessors use for the provider portion.

q: Which database delivers single-digit millisecond performance for key-value NoSQL workloads at any scale?
explain: DynamoDB = serverless NoSQL key-value/document database with single-digit millisecond latency. RDS is relational; Redshift is OLAP warehousing; Neptune is a graph database. (DAX adds microsecond in-memory caching in front of DynamoDB.)

q: A company wants to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks against its web application. Which service should it use?
explain: AWS WAF is a web application firewall: it filters HTTP/S traffic against rules for SQLi, XSS, and other OWASP Top 10 attacks. Shield handles DDoS at the network layer; GuardDuty detects threats rather than blocking web exploits.

q: A company uses AWS Organizations. How can it prevent member accounts from using a specific AWS service entirely?
explain: SCPs set the maximum permissions for an OU or account — e.g., deny a service everywhere. They don't grant permissions themselves; they filter what IAM policies can allow.

q: Which pillar focuses on protecting information, systems, and assets while delivering business value through risk assessments and mitigation strategies?
explain: That is the textbook definition of the Security pillar. It pairs protection with risk-based decision-making rather than treating security as blind restriction.

q: A financial modeling firm places EC2 instances in a cluster placement group inside a single Availability Zone. What benefit is the firm seeking?
options: Free data transfer between the instances
Protection against an Availability Zone failure
Automatic distribution of instances across Regions
The lowest possible network latency and highest throughput between instances
explain: Cluster placement groups pack instances physically close together for low-latency, high-throughput networking, at the cost of sharing one AZ's fate. Fault tolerance across AZs requires a spread strategy instead, and placement groups neither span Regions nor remove transfer charges.

q: After migrating file data into S3 with DataSync, a team plans ongoing nightly replication so the cloud copy never falls more than a day behind the on-premises source. Which DataSync capability supports this operating pattern directly?
options: Automatic conversion of files into database tables
One-time manual copy only, with no scheduling
Scheduled tasks that repeatedly sync changed data
explain: DataSync tasks can run on schedules and transfer only changed data, keeping source and destination synchronized over time. It does not convert files into tables or transcode media; those jobs belong to Glue and media services respectively.

q: Which TWO are IAM security best practices? (Select TWO.)
options: Use the root user for daily administration
explain: MFA adds a second factor and least privilege minimizes blast radius. Root for daily use, shared keys, and embedded credentials are all classic exam 'wrong answers'.

Tracking RI utilization/coverage against goals is a built-in Budgets capability (RI budgets), and RI-specific recommendations appear in Cost Explorer's rightsizing/purchasing recommendations. Trusted Advisor checks cover other optimization areas.
q: A customer wants to be alerted when its Reserved Instance utilization drops below 80%. Which AWS tool was designed for this alert?

explain: AWS Budgets supports cost budgets, usage budgets, Reserved Instance utilization/coverage budgets, and Savings Plans utilization/coverage budgets. CodeCommit lines of code is not a budget type in the service.
options: Lines of code stored in CodeCommit
q: Which of the following is NOT a budget type supported by AWS Budgets?
A company must migrate 500 TB of archives to AWS, but its internet link is so slow that a network transfer would take months. Which service should it use?
explain: Snowball = rugged physical devices shipped to you; load 500 TB locally and ship them back — built for petabyte-scale offline transfers. DataSync and Transfer Acceleration still need the network; Direct Connect gives a private link but doesn't fix a slow one.

q: A company wants newly launched EBS volumes encrypted by default in a Region without developers remembering a setting. What can it enable?
options: EBS encryption by default for the Region
explain: Enabling EBS encryption by default in a Region ensures new volumes and copies are encrypted automatically, using the default or a specified KMS key.

Always Free offers do not expire and are available to all AWS customers within their limits (for example Lambda invocations and DynamoDB capacity). The 12 Months Free tier ends one year after account creation.
q: Which AWS Free Tier type never expires and remains available indefinitely within its usage limits (for example, a monthly allotment of Lambda invocations)?

A fraud analytics team hunts for rings of accounts that share devices, phone numbers, and payment instruments in circular patterns. Which database's relationship-first model makes ring detection queries natural to express?
explain: Graph databases such as Neptune excel at multi-hop relationship questions like fraud rings, where the pattern of connections is the signal. Keyspaces stores wide-column rows, DocumentDB stores JSON documents, and Redshift aggregates tabular data; none traverses relationships as its native operation.

q: A company needs SSL/TLS certificates for its HTTPS website that are free and renew automatically before expiring. Which service provisions them?
explain: ACM provisions public (and private) TLS certificates with automatic renewal — free for AWS-integrated services. KMS manages encryption keys, not certificates; CloudHSM is dedicated key hardware; IAM manages identities, not certificates.

q: A support engineer needs an interactive shell on a private EC2 instance that has no public IP, no inbound ports open, and no SSH key distributed, with all session activity logged. Which Systems Manager capability provides this browser-based access?
options: Bastion hosts in a public subnet
explain: Session Manager opens secure, audited shell sessions through the Systems Manager service, reaching private instances with no inbound ports or SSH keys to manage. Bastions and public-key approaches reintroduce the exposure being removed, and Direct Connect is a network link, not an instance shell tool.

q: Which AWS Support plan includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) and Infrastructure Event Management?
explain: Enterprise includes a dedicated TAM, <15-minute response for business-critical issues, and Infrastructure Event Management for planned events. On-Ramp gets a pool of TAMs — dedicated TAMs are Enterprise-only.

q: Service control policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations apply to which accounts?
options: Only the root users of each account
All member accounts in the organization
explain: SCPs apply to member accounts (and OUs), restricting what their users and roles can do. They do not apply to the management account — so guard the management account carefully.

q: Two VPCs in the same account need to exchange traffic using private IP addresses as if they shared one network, and the requirement covers only this pair. Which VPC feature creates that private one-to-one link?
options: An internet gateway in each VPC
explain: VPC peering connects exactly two VPCs for private-IP communication, within or across Regions and accounts. Transit Gateway is the hub for many networks, internet gateways expose traffic to the public internet, and CloudFront delivers content rather than linking VPCs.

q: Which CAF perspective addresses culture, organizational design, and workforce skills for cloud adoption?
explain: People perspective is the CAF home for culture, roles, and skills transformation. The other perspectives cover architecture, security controls, and oversight.

q: Which activity is the clearest example of pay-as-you-go pricing?
options: Buying servers sized for the next five years
Signing a lease for data-center floor space
Paying a flat annual fee regardless of usage
Paying for each hour an instance runs and stopping charges by terminating it
explain: Pay-as-you-go ties the bill to actual consumption, and terminating resources stops the charges. Flat fees and upfront purchases do not vary with what you actually use.

q: An analyst team runs complex aggregation queries joining years of sales history across petabytes in a warehouse, caring about column scans rather than single-row lookups. Which database should hold this analytical workload?
options: Amazon RDS for MySQL with one instance
explain: Redshift is a petabyte-scale data warehouse optimized for OLAP: complex queries and aggregations over huge datasets using columnar storage. DynamoDB serves key-value lookups, ElastiCache caches data in memory, and a single RDS instance is built for row-based OLTP, not warehouse scans.

CUR data includes resource IDs, usage types, pricing, and tags at hourly granularity, delivered as refreshed files (often Parquet/CSV) to S3. It typically updates multiple times per day, not as a real-time stream.
options: Only visible in the console as charts
Updated in real time every minute
Available only at the end of the month
Delivered as files to S3, updated several times per day
q: Which statement about the AWS Cost and Usage Report is TRUE?
Which service provisions and manages AWS infrastructure from JSON or YAML templates, enabling infrastructure as code?
explain: CloudFormation = infrastructure as code: declare resources in a template and AWS provisions them repeatably. Beanstalk deploys applications; Systems Manager operates fleets; OpsWorks uses Chef/Puppet automation. Domain 4: Billing, Pricing, and Support (Q89–100)

q: A support team replaces its home-grown ticketing tool with a subscription helpdesk platform and archives the old tool's data. Which strategy applies to the ticketing workload?
explain: Switching users to a purchased SaaS replacement is repurchase, even though the old tool is then shut down. Retire describes decommissioning with no replacement workload.

q: Which TWO are AWS's responsibility under the shared responsibility model? (Select TWO.)
options: Physical security of AWS data centers
Patching the guest OS on customer EC2 instances
explain: AWS owns security of the cloud: physical facilities, hardware, and the virtualization/network infrastructure. The guest OS, data classification, and security group rules are all the customer's responsibility (security in the cloud). Domain 1 — Cloud Concepts

q: A clinic asks whether signing a BAA makes its AWS application automatically HIPAA compliant. What is the correct answer?
options: Yes, the BAA transfers all compliance duties to AWS
Yes, if it also uses encryption at rest
No, HIPAA cannot be supported on AWS at all
No, the clinic must still configure HIPAA-eligible services and safeguards correctly
explain: A BAA is required but does not transfer design duties. The customer must select eligible services and implement encryption, access control, and other safeguards.

q: Who is responsible for enabling S3 default encryption on a bucket the customer owns?
options: The customer, as a bucket configuration decision
AWS enables it identically for every bucket with customer keys
explain: Default encryption is a bucket setting the customer chooses, such as SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS. AWS secures the S3 platform but does not pick the customer key configuration.

q: A startup needs to accept an agreement in Artifact to use certain compliance programs with AWS. Which agreements live there?
options: Agreements such as the HIPAA BAA and other compliance program terms
Only the AWS service terms homepage
explain: Artifact hosts agreements, including the BAA and other program-specific terms, that account owners can review and accept for their organization.

Business Support is the first tier with 24/7 phone and chat access to cloud support engineers, making it the minimum fit for production workloads needing urgent off-hours help. It is also the tier AWS recommends for production environments.
q: A company runs production workloads on AWS and occasionally needs urgent help at night and on weekends. Which Support plan is the minimum that fits this requirement?

A retailer's blog occasionally needs its origin servers to handle ten times normal load during viral moments, and the team wants EC2 capacity to follow the load balancer's demand automatically. Which pairing is the standard elastic web-tier pattern?
options: An Auto Scaling group registered with a load balancer, scaling on demand signals
DNS records pointing at individual instances in rotation
A fixed fleet sized for the all-time peak, running year-round
One very large instance replaced manually when it struggles
explain: Registering an Auto Scaling group with a load balancer lets healthy capacity grow and shrink with real demand while the balancer spreads traffic across healthy instances. Fixed peak fleets waste money, manual replacement is slow and fragile, and DNS rotation lacks health-aware, instant traffic management.

q: Some AWS services encrypt data with keys that customers cannot view or manage at all. What are these keys called?
explain: AWS owned keys are owned and managed entirely by AWS for its internal service encryption needs and are not visible in customer KMS consoles.

q: Which TWO scenarios describe Rehost migrations? (Select TWO.)
options: Replicating a virtual machine into AWS without changing its configuration
Copying an application server to EC2 with the same OS and version
Changing a database engine to Aurora during the move
Moving an application to a SaaS product
explain: Rehost means the workload arrives in AWS essentially identical to how it ran on-premises. SaaS replacement is repurchase, and an engine change is at least replatform, usually refactor.

q: A software vendor selling to US federal agencies needs its AWS environment aligned with a government authorization program. Which program is it?
explain: FedRAMP standardizes security authorization for cloud services used by US federal agencies, and AWS offers FedRAMP-authorized Regions and services.

q: An IT team wants the simplest possible description of what an S3 bucket and an S3 object are for a new hire. Which statement is accurate?
options: A bucket is a Region, and an object is an Availability Zone
A bucket is a single file, and objects are folders inside instances
A bucket is an EC2 disk, and an object is a running process
A bucket is a container for objects, and an object consists of the data plus its metadata identified by a key
explain: In S3, you create a bucket as a container in a Region, then store objects in it, each object being the file data and metadata addressed by a unique key. Buckets are not disks, files, or Regions, and objects are data items, not processes.

q: Which tool helps find IAM roles that external principals can assume in a risky way?
explain: Access Analyzer evaluates resource and role policies for external access, flagging roles assumable from outside the zone of trust so risky trusts can be fixed.

q: Attackers are sending cross-site scripting payloads in web requests to a storefront behind an Application Load Balancer. Which service filters these Layer 7 attacks?
explain: WAF inspects HTTP and HTTPS requests at Layer 7 and blocks patterns such as XSS and SQL injection using managed and custom rules on ALBs and similar resources.

Infrastructure Event Management is included with Enterprise Support and is available to Business Support customers for an additional fee, providing planning and real-time support around events such as launches and migrations.
options: It cannot be purchased at any plan level
It is available for an additional fee
It is only available on the Developer plan
It is included free with Business Support
q: A retailer plans a major product launch and wants AWS experts to help plan and support the event through AWS Infrastructure Event Management. On the Business plan, how is this service obtained?

explain: In AWS Organizations, the management (payer) account pays the Consolidated Bill covering all member accounts' usage. Member accounts do not receive separate bills from AWS.
options: The AWS Support plan owner only
The service team that created the resources
q: Who receives and pays the combined bill in an AWS Organizations Consolidated Billing setup?
A developer provisions 20 EC2 instances from the console in minutes, without filing a ticket or contacting AWS. Which essential characteristic of cloud computing makes this possible?
explain: On-demand self-service = provisioning resources yourself, automatically, whenever you need them — no human interaction with the provider required. Broad network access is about reaching services from many devices; resource pooling is shared multi-tenant infrastructure; measured service is usage metering for billing.

All of those needs are covered by free Basic Support: documentation and whitepapers are public, and 24/7 customer service handles billing questions and disputes. Paid plans add technical troubleshooting support.
q: A non-technical founder only needs AWS documentation, whitepapers, and help with a billing dispute. Which Support plan is sufficient?

explain: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your AWS environment and flags deviations from best practices across cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits. The depth of available checks depends on the Support plan.
q: A solutions architect wants to check an account against best practices in cost optimization, security, performance, fault tolerance, and service limits. Which tool provides these checks?

A call center records every support call and needs searchable text transcripts with speakers identified, to audit quality and find calls mentioning refunds. Which service converts the call audio into transcripts?
explain: Transcribe converts speech to text with features like speaker identification and timestamps, turning call archives into searchable records. Polly creates speech from text, Rekognition analyzes visual content, and Translate converts written text between languages after it exists as text.

q: A publisher wants articles served from caches in viewers' countries but needs breaking-news pages to refresh within a minute while images stay cached for a day. Which CloudFront mechanism lets different content types carry different freshness lifetimes?
options: Per-behavior cache settings (TTL) within one distribution
One global TTL that applies identically to every file
explain: A CloudFront distribution can define multiple cache behaviors by path pattern, each with its own TTL, so news pages expire in a minute while images persist for a day. Route 53 steers DNS answers rather than caching, and security groups have no concept of content freshness lifetimes.

q: A subnet's route table contains a route to an internet gateway, and instances in it receive public IP addresses. By definition, what kind of subnet is this?
options: An isolated subnet with no routes
explain: A public subnet is defined by its route to an internet gateway, allowing instances with public IPs to exchange traffic with the internet both ways. Private subnets route outbound internet traffic through NAT instead, and the label is about routing, not peering or isolation labels.

q: Guards, cameras, and locked cages at an AWS facility fall under which side of the shared responsibility model?
explain: Physical security of facilities is security of the cloud and belongs entirely to AWS for every service model, from EC2 through fully managed services.

Each AWS Marketplace purchase is conveniently added to the customer's regular AWS bill as a line item, avoiding separate vendor invoicing for those subscriptions. Marketplace software charges are not free-tier eligible.
options: A separate paper invoice from each vendor
A line item on the customer's regular AWS bill
Automatic deduction from AWS credits only
An annual consolidated credit card charge
q: How are AWS Marketplace software subscriptions billed?
After migration, a service owner builds dashboards for service health, defines an on-call rotation, and plans capacity reviews for production workloads. Which CAF perspective is the owner working in?
explain: Day-two service health, incident readiness, and ongoing service management are Operations perspective concerns in CAF. The platform is already built; this is about running services well on it.

q: A logistics company connects its warehouse systems to AWS so inventory data flows continuously between its dock scanners and cloud dashboards. The combined environment is best called what?
explain: On-premises operational systems integrated with cloud services form a hybrid architecture. Edge locations and AZs are AWS infrastructure concepts, not names for this combined estate.

q: Which pairing of service to cloud model is correct?
options: Amazon EC2 - SaaS; Elastic Beanstalk - IaaS; vendor payroll - PaaS
Amazon EC2 - PaaS; Elastic Beanstalk - SaaS; vendor payroll - IaaS
All three are examples of SaaS
Amazon EC2 - IaaS; AWS Elastic Beanstalk - PaaS; a vendor-hosted payroll application - SaaS
explain: EC2 rents infrastructure, Beanstalk provides a managed platform for customer code, and hosted payroll is a finished application. The other pairings scramble those responsibility levels.

q: An engineering firm keeps block volumes on-premises whose snapshots are stored in S3, so local applications see fast disks while data is backed by cloud storage. Which Storage Gateway type provides cloud-backed iSCSI block volumes?
explain: Volume Gateway presents iSCSI block volumes to on-premises applications, keeping data or snapshots backed by S3 in AWS. Tape Gateway emulates tape libraries, File Gateway exposes file shares, and there is no printer gateway in the Storage Gateway family.

q: A media workflow mounts the same high-performance file system from Kubernetes pods and EC2 instances that run both Linux and Windows nodes, and the team also wants managed NetApp features. Which FSx family member is designed as a fully managed NetApp ONTAP file system?
options: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explain: FSx for NetApp ONTAP delivers managed ONTAP file systems with multiprotocol access and NetApp data-management features. FSx for Windows File Server is Windows-native only, EFS is AWS's NFS service without ONTAP features, and S3 is object storage.

q: Which term describes automatically adding or removing resources to match demand in real time?
explain: Elasticity is automatic scaling with demand. Scalability is the ability to scale (it can be manual). High availability keeps systems up across failures; fault tolerance keeps them running despite a failed component.

q: An enterprise wants GuardDuty enabled and its findings routed to one delegated security account across the whole organization. Which service view still shows the combined posture?
options: AWS Security Hub in the security account
explain: Security Hub can aggregate findings across accounts and Regions into an administrator account, giving the security team one combined posture view.

q: A system is described as both highly available and fault tolerant. During a disk failure, users notice nothing and the service never goes down. Which term explains the 'users notice nothing' part most precisely?
explain: Fault tolerance is the stricter property: failures are absorbed with no loss of service, so users notice nothing. High availability alone permits short interruptions as long as overall uptime stays high.

q: Which pillar is chiefly about running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continuously improving supporting processes?
explain: That sentence is the standard definition of Operational Excellence. The other pillars target failure recovery, resource efficiency, and spending respectively.

q: A startup wants to avoid buying servers upfront and instead pay only for the capacity it uses each month. Which advantage of cloud computing is this?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
explain: This is the CapEx → OpEx shift: pay-as-you-go instead of big upfront purchases. "Stop guessing capacity" is about scaling to demand; "go global" is about worldwide reach; economies of scale is AWS's size lowering prices.

q: A product team enables GuardDuty and sees a finding type about an S3 bucket being accessed from an unusual location. What kind of control produced this alert?
options: Preventive control that blocked the access
Directive control in a policy document
Detective control that identified suspicious activity
Corrective control that restored the bucket
explain: GuardDuty is a detective control: it observes logs and raises findings about suspicious activity but does not itself block or remediate the access.

q: A team stores per-user shopping preferences, each record a small bundle of settings retrieved whole whenever the user signs in and rarely queried by any other attribute. Which database choice is the most natural fit?
explain: Whole-record retrieval by a single user key with no cross-record querying is the signature DynamoDB pattern, offering fast, scalable preference storage. Redshift analyzes huge datasets, Neptune traverses relationships, and QLDB maintains verifiable ledgers; none matches simple key-based settings storage better.

q: GuardDuty continuously monitors for threats and raises findings, but it does not block anything by itself. What type of security control is this?
explain: Detective controls identify and alert on issues (GuardDuty, CloudTrail) without stopping them. Preventive controls block bad actions up front (WAF rules, security groups); corrective controls fix or restore after an incident (backups); directive controls are policies and procedures.

q: Which TWO DynamoDB billing and capacity choices can a team pick between? (Select TWO.)
options: On-demand capacity mode that pays per request
Provisioned capacity mode with set read and write units
Spot capacity that can be interrupted at any time
explain: DynamoDB offers on-demand mode, paying per request for unpredictable traffic, and provisioned mode, reserving throughput units for steady workloads. Dedicated Hosts and Spot pricing are EC2 purchasing concepts that do not apply to DynamoDB tables.

q: Who patches the guest operating system on an Amazon Lightsail instance used by a small bakery?
explain: Lightsail instances are still virtual servers the customer administers, including OS patching. Lightsail simplifies provisioning but does not remove guest OS duties.

q: A startup wants one dashboard where AWS security standards are scored and findings from multiple detectors are deduplicated. Which service should it enable first?
explain: Security Hub is the central posture and findings hub, running standards checks and aggregating GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and partner findings in one place.

q: Which Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads?
explain: Sustainability covers the long-term environmental, economic, and societal impacts of your workloads — for example, choosing efficient instance types and scaling to zero when idle. Operational Excellence is about running and monitoring systems; Performance Efficiency is about using resources efficiently (not specifically the environment); Reliability is about recovering from failure.

q: Which statement best describes serverless computing?
options: Customers must provision server capacity in advance
The cloud provider manages the servers; customers pay only for actual usage
There are no servers involved at all
explain: Serverless (e.g., Lambda) abstracts servers away — no provisioning or patching, and billing is per-request/compute-time. Servers still exist; you just never see them.

q: Which KMS key type does the customer create and fully control, including permissions, rotation settings, and disabling?
explain: Customer managed keys are created in the account and fully controlled by the customer, including key policies, grants, rotation, and scheduled deletion.

q: A company's AWS bill shows exactly how many EC2 hours and gigabytes of S3 storage it consumed, because usage is metered per service. Which essential characteristic of cloud computing describes this?
explain: Measured service = resource usage is monitored, controlled, and billed per unit consumed — the basis of pay-as-you-go. The other three characteristics describe how you get and reach resources, not how usage is metered.

q: An Australian education app expands to serve students in Brazil by deploying its existing application into an AWS Region in South America the same week the decision is made. Which advantage is this?
options: Benefit from massive economies of scale
Trade fixed expense for variable expense
explain: Deploying into a distant market within days using existing AWS Regions is go global in minutes. Agility is related, but the defining feature here is geographic expansion without building foreign facilities.

q: An SCP attached to an organizational unit allows everything except one denied service. A member account admin tries to use that service. What happens?
options: The admin succeeds because account admins outrank SCPs
The request is denied because SCPs cap permissions for member accounts
The SCP converts into an IAM policy for the admin
Only the management account is blocked
explain: SCPs apply to member accounts and set the maximum permissions; an explicit SCP denial blocks the service even for that account administrators.

AWS Training and Certification, delivered largely through AWS Skill Builder, provides digital courses, labs, and exam preparation. It is a learning resource, separate from Support plans that provide engineers for troubleshooting.
q: Which AWS resource offers self-paced digital courses and learning paths for building cloud skills, including preparation for certification?
A media executive reads that AWS has far more edge locations than Regions and asks what business problem that imbalance solves. Which explanation is correct?
options: Each edge location is a full copy of a Region kept in reserve
Edge locations exist only to host billing servers
Edge locations are cheaper Regions sold without support
Edge locations put cached content and DNS responses physically close to huge numbers of users, so many more of them are needed than full Regions
explain: Regions are expensive full deployments, while edge locations are lightweight cache and DNS points sprinkled widely so content sits near every audience; hence there are many more of them. They are neither discounted Regions, standby Region copies, nor billing infrastructure.

q: A software firm hosts its product videos and installer downloads in S3, and users on other continents wait painfully long for every download. Which service caches copies of these files at edge locations near users so repeat downloads are fast?
explain: CloudFront is the content delivery network: it caches static (and some dynamic) content at edge locations around the world so users fetch from a nearby copy. Route 53 only resolves names, Global Accelerator accelerates connections without caching files, and EFS is regional file storage.

q: A support lead asks why the order-entry application should stay on RDS while reporting moves elsewhere. Which distinction explains the split in one sentence?
options: RDS handles transactional OLTP row operations; the warehouse handles analytical OLAP queries
RDS cannot store more than a gigabyte; warehouses have no limits at all
RDS is only for unstructured data; warehouses are only for images
There is no functional difference; the split is purely cosmetic
explain: OLTP systems like RDS process many small transactions (orders, updates) while OLAP systems like Redshift analyze large datasets with complex queries; mixing heavy analytics onto the transactional store degrades both. The other statements invent limits or differences that do not exist.

q: A hospital group operates clinics with no reliable internet for days at a time; each clinic generates imaging data that must eventually reach S3 for central analysis. Which approach gathers the data locally on rugged hardware for shipment to AWS?
options: Amazon CloudFront distributions at each clinic
AWS Snowball Edge devices deployed at the clinics
AWS Direct Connect links to each clinic
Amazon EFS file systems at each clinic
explain: Snowball Edge devices collect and can even pre-process data at disconnected edge sites, then ship back for import into S3. CloudFront, Direct Connect, and EFS all assume working network connectivity that these clinics do not reliably have.

q: A supply-chain auditor asks whether QLDB or a public blockchain is the right fit. The auditor mainly needs one company's tamper-evident transaction log, owned and trusted centrally, with no multi-party consensus network. Which choice and reason are correct?
options: QLDB, because it mines new blocks with proof of work
QLDB, because it provides a centrally owned, verifiable ledger without running a blockchain network
DynamoDB, because it chains blocks cryptographically by default
A public blockchain, because QLDB cannot verify history
explain: QLDB gives a single owner a journal whose changes are cryptographically verifiable, delivering ledger guarantees without decentralized consensus or mining. Public blockchains add multi-party trust machinery this single-owner audit does not need, and DynamoDB offers no built-in cryptographic chaining.

q: What does an IAM policy document primarily define?
options: Permissions that allow or deny actions on resources
The network topology of a VPC
explain: An IAM policy is a JSON document that defines permissions, specifying actions, resources, and whether the effect is allow or deny for an identity or resource.
